topics.title: [post-training] Mix PivotRL pivots into broad RLVR for SWE and terminal gains
topics.body:
## TL;DR

Three matched mixed-domain RLVR runs from the Grug Datakit SFT (October 5) test whether a share of [PivotRL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21383) pivots improves SWE-bench Verified and OpenThoughts-TBLite without hurting the other domains, and whether pivot selection matters: RLVR alone, RLVR with selected SWE and Terminal pivots at 20% of prompts, and RLVR with random SWE and Terminal turns at the same share. Two optional arms move the selected share to 10% and 30%. Every arm stops at 12 steps. Status: all three arms trained 12 steps at seed 42 and were evaluated at steps 4, 8 and 12; [results](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10214#issuecomment-6305992938). B is the only arm above the SFT on SWE-bench Verified (+8.8 points at steps 4 and 8, p=.0001; +4.8 at step 12), C never transfers, and every arm drifts on Math500 and MMLU-Pro by step 12, B least. A seed-43 replicate is training.

## Hypothesis

Pivots that the SFT policy's own pass rates select (#9933), rewarded by #9933's deterministic verifiers, improve SWE-bench Verified and OpenThoughts-TBLite at 20% of prompts while broad holdout accuracy stays within noise. Random SWE and Terminal turns at the same share help less. Training pivots alone has been hard to stabilize; mixing them into broad RLVR keeps the rest of the policy anchored.

## Setup

- **Start:** [open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05), a pure SFT checkpoint. #9933 measured its SWE and Terminal pass rates on this policy, so the selections apply unchanged, and the RLVR data is unseen.
- **RLVR data:** [Nemotron-RL-Ultra-RLVR1-Cleaned-v3](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Nemotron-RL-Ultra-RLVR1-Cleaned-v3-2026-09-30) (84,403 train / 94 validation rows; 24% single-step tool use, 14% instruction following, 9% code, 13% math, no SWE or Terminal rows). Any SWE or terminal change between arms is therefore attributable to the added turns.
- **Recipe:** the #9735 reference/KL arm (frozen reference, KL 0.01, sequence-mean loss, entropy 0.001, router replay), 512 prompts × 16 samples per step, at most 12 steps, the same seed in every arm. SFT starts in #9735 collapsed after 12 to 20 steps. Asynchronous rollouts with staleness up to 2, TIS correction, a 102,400-token request window with 49,152 tokens per turn, and thinking on, as #9933 measured the pivots' pass rates.
- **RLVR blend as trained:** 63,590 of RLVR1's rows. MarinSkyRL now runs every Nemotron Ultra row as a task session, and code generation, NeMo tool use, NVARC inductive and Lean sessions execute in a Docker task machine that Iris task pods cannot start, so every arm omits those four agents (about 20% of RLVR1, including #9735's code domain). Rows containing a blank text message, which task conversations reject, are dropped too (3,991 RLVR, 59 Terminal). Validation keeps 67 of RLVR1's 94 rows.
- **Pivot prompts:** the runtime drops earlier assistant turns' reasoning from pivot prompts, which #9933's pass-rate measurement kept.
- **Pivots:** #9933's long-format SWE and Terminal candidates, selected at λ = 0.65 (1 to 10 passes of 16) from the pooled K = 16 pass rates already measured on this policy (`users/dml/pivotrl/{swe,terminal}/pass-rates/grug-67b-a2b-datakit-sft-262k-20261005+seed-1@2026.10.09`). That selects 25,792 of 72,434 scored SWE turns under `nemo` and 6,999 of 36,107 Terminal turns.
- **Reward:** `nemotron_ultra` grades pivot rows through MarinSkyRL#992 with #9933's verifiers: NeMo Gym argument comparison (`nemo`) for SWE and Terminus-2 keystroke similarity without a judge (`string_90`) for Terminal. #10000 uses the same graders. Pivot replies are capped at 4,096 tokens, the cap the pass rates were sampled at.

## Arms

| Arm | Data |
| --- | --- |
| A | RLVR1 |
| B | RLVR1, with selected pivots replacing 20% of prompts |
| C | RLVR1, with random SWE and Terminal candidate turns replacing 20% of prompts |
| B-10, B-30 (optional) | As B, at 10% and 30% |

The batch stays at 512 prompts, so added turns displace RLVR prompts. Each step carries 102 added turns, 51 SWE and 51 Terminal, because the two benchmarks weigh equally in the decision rules; MarinSkyRL's domain-weighted sampling fills every batch to these counts from route-tagged pools and draws each pool uniformly. RLVR rows come first and their pool is shuffled first, so with one seed B's and C's RLVR prompts are a prefix of A's draw order. Twelve steps use 612 of each pool (25,792 SWE and 6,999 Terminal pivots), so no turn repeats.

### Why 20%

Only groups with mixed outcomes produce a gradient, and RLVR1 groups already mostly do: `reward/informative_group_fraction` was 0.79 at the first step from the Datakit SFT (Datakit v4, #9735) and fell to about 0.55 by step 12. Resampling the stored K = 16 pass rates, 88% of selected SWE pivots and 81% of selected Terminal pivots come back mixed, against 58% and 24% of random candidate turns. Pivots' share of the gradient is therefore only 1.1 to 1.5 times their share of prompts, and C carries about half of B's pivot signal at the same share.

Pivot-only RL on this SFT, with the same policy learning rate (4e-6) and gradient clip, bounds the dose. One update of 64 SWE pivot groups raised SWE-bench Verified from 26.0% to 29.4% (146 vs 129 of 496 matched tasks, against a historical base run) with AIME24 unchanged; five updates raised held-out pivot accuracy from 0.29 to 0.38. Forty Terminal updates cost 36 points on AIME24 and 9 to 10 on GPQA Diamond, MMLU-Pro and Math500, and ninety SWE updates collapsed agentic behavior (1 of 248 SWE-bench Verified trials solved, 0 of 190 TBLite) while held-out pivot accuracy kept rising.

Counting a mixed step as its pivot gradient share of a pivot-only update, with RLVR1's informative fraction averaging about 0.68 over the first 12 steps, a first-order approximation that ignores RLVR and KL counteracting drift:

| *p* | Pivot prompts per step | Pivot gradient share | Equivalent pivot-only updates by step 12 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 10% | 51 | ~12% | ~1.5 |
| 20% | 102 | ~24% | ~2.9 |
| 30% | 154 | ~35% | ~4.2 |

With at most 12 steps, 10% delivers about one pivot-only update, the dose that gained about 3 points on SWE, below what the benchmarks resolve. 20% places the dose in the middle of the range where pivot-only training helped, about 14 times below where it did damage, with RLVR still about three quarters of the gradient. B-10 and B-30 bracket it.

## Measurements

- At steps 0, 4, 8 and 12: pass rate on #9933's held-out validation turns graded in process, broad holdout pass@1 and normalized verifier score, and per-domain reward.
- Per step and per source (RLVR, SWE, Terminal): informative group count and mean response length, so B and C are compared by delivered pivot signal and any pull toward shorter RLVR answers shows up early. Pivot replies are capped at 4,096 tokens, the cap their pass rates were sampled at, through each pivot row's request; the sequence-mean loss weights them like full RLVR answers.
- At step 0 and each arm's step 4, 8 and 12 checkpoints: full SWE-bench Verified (500 tasks, mini-swe-agent 2.1.0) and OpenThoughts-TBLite (Terminus 2), three runs each, compared per task between arms, plus AIME24, GPQA Diamond, MMLU-Pro and Math500, the benchmarks pivot-only training hurt.
- Checkpoints are selected by the broad holdout and pivot validation, never by the benchmarks. A paired comparison on 500 SWE tasks has a standard error of about 2 points; on 100 tasks it is about 4.4, too wide for the effects expected here.

## Decision rules

- B beats A on SWE-bench Verified or OpenThoughts-TBLite by more than two paired standard errors, with the broad holdout and the four reasoning benchmarks within noise: pivots help in mixed RLVR. Next, test RL-then-merge against the Campaign 3 merge recipe (#9975).
- B ≈ C: selection does not matter at this share; random turns are enough. B > C partly reflects C's smaller pivot signal, so the logged informative group counts qualify the comparison.
- B beats A on pivot validation only: the verifier reward does not transfer to the benchmarks. Revisit the reward component (`exact`) or the generation cap.
- An arm collapses: report its best checkpoint before the collapse and compare arms only at matched steps.

## Prerequisites

1. Per-agent `pivot_reward`, declared among the Nemotron Ultra session settings: MarinSkyRL#992.
2. Selection artifacts at λ = 0.65 from #9933's stored K = 16 pass rates: built, 25,792 SWE and 6,999 Terminal pivots.
3. Arm datasets: #10215 builds RLVR1 (`open-athena/Nemotron-RL-Ultra-RLVR1-Cleaned-v3-2026-09-30@600262dd`) alone, with the selected pivots, and with every scored candidate turn, each row tagged with its route. Rows move from the retired `skyrl_gym` route to `task_session`, which MarinSkyRL grades Nemotron Ultra rows on since its #879. Validation in every arm is RLVR1's 94 rows plus #9933's 508 held-out SWE and 503 Terminal turns.
4. A two-step smoke run of B on 6 nodes (64 prompts with B's composition, 32K window) confirming that every agent's rows load and grade.

## Links

- PivotRL candidates, pass rates and selection: #9933; SFT baselines on the same pivots: #10000; TaskSpec versions of the candidates: #10181
- Prior broad-domain RLVR: #9359, #9735
- Paper: [PivotRL (arXiv 2603.21383)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.21383)

comments.body:
🤖
# Research

This is a matched training experiment, not an isolated code fix. The current Marin checkout can pass multiple artifact data sources to SkyRL, but PivotRL pass-rate selection and task conversion are still in open PRs #9933 and #10181; #10181 currently has a failing aggregate `unit-tests` check. The per-agent `pivot_reward` change and verifyit pin in MarinSkyRL#992 remain prerequisites; this session cannot inspect that separate repository.

**Relevant code**
- [`skyrl.py#L150-L163`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/skyrl.py#L150-L163) — training sources and seed
- [`skyrl.py#L307-L344`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/skyrl.py#L307-L344) — artifact dependency and launcher request
- [`external_dependencies.py#L73-L79`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/external_dependencies.py#L73-L79) — pinned MarinSkyRL revision
- [#9933](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9933) — candidate pass rates and pivot selection
- [#10181](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10181) — TaskSpec conversion and in-process graders

# Proposed Fix

1. Land #9933 and resolve the stacked #10000/#10181 work without duplicating it. Produce pooled K=16 pass rates for both domains and record immutable λ=0.65 selected-pivot and random-candidate manifests, including source IDs, pool sizes, and disjoint validation identities.
2. Verify MarinSkyRL#992 supports per-agent `pivot_reward`, pins the verifyit revision with the pivot graders, and grades SWE and Terminal in one run. Pin that tested MarinSkyRL revision in Marin and cover the reward dispatch and loader path with focused tests.
3. Add an artifact-backed builder for A/B/C that records the seed, source revisions, prompt order, domain counts, and chosen pivot IDs. Keep 512 prompts × 16 samples per step; make B and C use the same pivot share and SWE/Terminal balance, with their RLVR prompts drawn in A's order. Cap pivot replies at 4,096 tokens.
4. Run B for two smoke steps to confirm `skyrl_gym` loading, both graders, reward variance, and the surviving RLVR informative-group fraction. Fix the pivot share from that result, subject to the selected pool size, before launching matched 40-step A/B/C runs.
5. Evaluate every four steps from step 0, choose checkpoints using only broad holdout and pivot validation, then run three SWE-Bench-100 and OpenThoughts-TBLite evaluations plus the disjoint SWE-bench Verified slice at step 0, best, and final. Report matched-step effects, uncertainty, any collapse, run/config/artifact links, and the issue's decision rules.

This needs the prerequisite merges, data artifacts, and production training/evaluation runs; no standalone PR from this triage would complete #10214.

🤖 Results for the three arms at steps 4, 8 and 12, paired per item against the October 5 Datakit SFT (REF). One run per arm at seed 42. Training runs: [A](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/pivot-mixed-rlvr/runs/1u013rdm), [B](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/pivot-mixed-rlvr/runs/e01zoz2k), [C](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/pivot-mixed-rlvr/runs/zblphp52). A12's SWE-bench job is still retrying verifier timeouts, so that one cell is provisional; the rest of the 54 evaluations are final.

Selected pivots are the only treatment that moves SWE-bench Verified, the effect is present at step 4, and random turns at the same share do not transfer. Every arm erodes Math500 and MMLU-Pro by step 12; B erodes least. Step 8 is the checkpoint to report.

## SWE-bench Verified

Strict scoring: a trial with no verifier result counts as unsolved, each cell is one complete 500-task run, and p-values are exact McNemar tests on the discordant pairs.

| Step | REF | A | B | C | B vs A | B vs C | B vs REF |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | .260 | .288 | .348 | .232 | +6.0, p=.004 | +11.6, p<.0001 | +8.8, p=.0001 |
| 8 | .260 | .256 | .348 | .248 | +9.2, p<.0001 | +10.0, p<.0001 | +8.8, p=.0001 |
| 12 | .260 | .272 (provisional) | .308 | .244 | +3.6, p=.07 | +6.4, p=.002 | +4.8, p=.025 |

A and C never differ from REF (every |Δ| ≤ 2.8 points, p ≥ .14). B newly solves 22 to 23% of the tasks REF fails, against 10 to 15% for A and C, and keeps about 70% of REF's solved tasks. B12 vs B8 is −4.0 (p=.054).

## Other benchmarks

Δ vs REF in points. GPQA-Diamond averages 3 trials per question and AIME24 10, tested with a paired sign-flip permutation test; Math500 and MMLU-Pro use exact McNemar; OT-TBLite counts a task solved when at least 2 of 3 trials score 1. Starred cells have p<.05.

| Step | Arm | GPQA-D | MMLU-Pro | Math500 | AIME24 | OT-TBLite |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | A | +3.9 | +0.9 ★ | 0.0 | −3.3 | +2.0 |
| 4 | B | +6.4 ★ | +0.6 | −0.8 | −0.7 | +3.0 |
| 4 | C | +7.6 ★ | 0.0 | −0.8 | −1.7 | 0.0 |
| 8 | A | +6.2 ★ | +0.8 ★ | −0.2 | +1.0 | −5.0 |
| 8 | B | +7.4 ★ | +0.4 | 0.0 | −3.0 | −2.0 |
| 8 | C | +6.1 ★ | +0.4 | −1.0 | 0.0 | −4.0 |
| 12 | A | +5.7 ★ | −1.6 ★ | −7.6 ★ | −4.0 | −4.0 |
| 12 | B | +6.6 ★ | −1.1 ★ | −2.2 (p=.052) | 0.0 | −3.0 |
| 12 | C | +4.5 ★ | −3.4 ★ | −7.8 ★ | −0.3 | −3.0 |

REF accuracies: GPQA-Diamond .635 (n=198), MMLU-Pro .780 (n=12032), Math500 .968 (n=500), AIME24 .830 (n=30), OT-TBLite .16 (n=100). At step 12 B beats A by +5.4 and C by +5.6 on Math500 (both p<.0001) and C by +2.3 on MMLU-Pro (p<.0001). No arm differs from another on GPQA-Diamond or AIME24 at any step, and TBLite with 100 tasks cannot resolve differences under about 9 points.

## Reading

Random turns are the control that makes the SWE-bench result interpretable. C uses the same turn sources, verifiers and share as B, and on the held-out pivot turns it learns the pivot task as fast as B: SWE pivot pass@1 rises from .24 to .42 in both arms and Terminal from .15 to .23, while A stays at .23. Only the selected turns transfer to the benchmark. Random turns also carry less signal, as the plan anticipated: informative-group fraction 0.59 against 0.67 for A and B, and pivot rewards about half of B's.

The GPQA gain of 4 to 8 points in every arm from step 4 comes from the RLVR mix.

The step-12 losses are on hard multi-step items. On Math500, levels 1 to 3 move within 3 points in every arm; level 4 drops 7.8 (A), 2.3 (B) and 8.6 (C) points and level 5 drops 17.2, 4.5 and 15.7. On MMLU-Pro, which is decoded greedily, the losses sit in engineering, chemistry, physics and math; B12 is flat on engineering where A12 is −5.8 and C12 −7.7. The lost Math500 answers run 4.3 times the length of REF's answer to the same question and 34 of A12's 42 end in an extracted wrong answer rather than a truncation. The share of Math500 responses over 100K characters is 0.4% for REF, 4.8% for A4, 8.2% for B12, 11.0% for C12 and 12.4% for A12.

The training curves carry the same signature. Policy entropy rises every step (A 0.83 to 2.76, B to 1.95, C to 2.18) and KL to the frozen reference climbs with no plateau (A .071, B .063, C .086 at step 12), so the 0.01 KL coefficient does not hold the policy. The arm that drifts least degrades least. The in-distribution holdout improves monotonically in every arm (A .21 to .40), so it cannot see the drift; the reference/KL run in #9735 shows the same entropy rise (1.0 to 2.2 by step 10) and had only that holdout. Length stops stay under 9% throughout training and are not the cause.

A's agentic behaviour drifts the same way. Its replies on the pivot validation turns grow 1.5 to 2 times by step 12, A8 overflows the 73K-token context in 17% of SWE-bench tasks (every non-zero agent exit in A8 and A12 is a context-window overflow), and in the A12 eval the median model call took 17 s against 3.6 s for the other runs: 171 of 500 trials hit the 30-minute agent budget, 122 of them then timing out in the verifier. Harbor retries verifier timeouts as infrastructure errors, and the retries have moved A12 from .244 to .272 so far.

## Decision rules

The first rule, B above A on SWE-bench Verified by more than two paired standard errors with the reasoning benchmarks within noise, holds at steps 4 and 8 (SE about 2 points; B−A +6.0 and +9.2). At step 12 no arm has the reasoning benchmarks within noise. The second rule, B ≈ C, fails at every step by 6 to 12 points, and the logged informative-group counts attribute part of that to C's weaker signal. Confidence is limited by one seed per arm; the B effects are 3 to 5 standard errors on SWE-bench, and isolated p<.05 cells such as B8 vs A8 on AIME24 (−4.0, p=.04) are what a hundred comparisons produce.

## What it took

- Layout: 16 H100 nodes per arm, 10 policy nodes with the colocated reference and 12 inference engines at DP4/EP4 on the other 6; 11 to 16 hours per 12-step run.
- Runtime: MarinSkyRL branch `dml/mixed-rlvr-runtime` at bfef1308, seven commits over the fork's main at 563658e5: verifyit pivot graders for the Nemotron pivot rows, per-agent `pivot_reward`, the SWE pivot agent name, null message fields in Parquet prompts, request tools passed as chat tools, and a retry for vLLM engine gangs that die during startup. marin-community/MarinSkyRL#992 carries the first six. The fork was archived on 2026-10-20, so these need porting into `vendor/skyrl` once the verifyit graders from #10215 are published.
- Evaluation: the October 5 verified paired-eval stack (`held/eval-october17-verified` at f9990d36) plus fixes on branch `dml/eval-october17-verified-pivot-mixed-rlvr`: a localhost relay that reports the Iris proxy's 404 during an inference-server reschedule as 503 for ten minutes so Evalchemy retries; Daytona verifier thread limits, because native test libraries sized their pools to the host and exhausted the 300 s verifier timeout; mini-swe-agent pinned to litellm 1.105.1 after an MCP import regression; a 24 h placement budget that treats Kueue's SchedulingGated state as unplaced; the Run:ai streamer load format for staged HF exports; `--cluster-config` so evaluations submit as the openathena.ai login after the contractor service account's default budget demoted jobs to batch band; and an export barrier that waits for the HF export job and verifies its shards before evaluating.
- Scoring: strict first-trial SWE-bench with the fullest run per arm and step; TBLite majority of 3 trials; repeated-trial benchmarks averaged per question.

## Next

- Final A12 SWE-bench number when the retry wave ends.
- A seed-43 replicate of all three arms launched 2026-10-20 21:29 UTC as the openathena.ai login, A on cw-us-east-02a, B and C on cw-rno2a: [A](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/pivot-mixed-rlvr/runs/5thdcjv5), [B](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/pivot-mixed-rlvr/runs/v8o72kqn), [C](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/pivot-mixed-rlvr/runs/2rjy7l3n). C has been preempted three times by production-band jobs on rno2a and restarts from scratch each time.
- The recipe needs a drift fix before running past 8 steps: a stronger KL coefficient, a lower learning rate, dropping the entropy bonus, or a length penalty. The optional p arms (B-10, B-30) remain open; the second seed was prioritized.

topics.title: Vendor SkyRL behind an isolated executable
topics.body:
Move the supported SkyRL runtime into `vendor/skyrl` and route Marin RL artifacts through its isolated `marinskyrl` executable. Source changes can land with Marin while SkyRL's Torch/CUDA dependencies retain their own resolution and lock. ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph Marin["Marin environment · root uv.lock"] Experiment["RL experiment / artifact graph"] --> Adapter["marin.rl.skyrl"] end subgraph SkyRL["vendor/skyrl · independent uv.lock"] Code["cloud/ · marinskyrl/
skyrl-train/ · skyrl-gym/
templates · upstream provenance"] --> CLI["marinskyrl executable · CPU environment"] end Adapter -->|"launch YAML / child process"| CLI CLI -->|"verified source + assets + lock"| GPU["Iris GPU task
editable SkyRL + frozen Megatron/vLLM profile"] GPU --> Output["Distributed checkpoints / HF policy export"] Output --> Eval["Marin evaluation artifact"] ``` Marin clears its Python environment selection at the subprocess boundary; the launcher reuses its own CPU environment. GPU workers install the bundled source and frozen profile without cloning the fork. Ray ports use Iris allocations or task-local kernel selection on Kubernetes, so concurrent jobs can share a host. The runtime identity hashes the current source, assets, and lock, so ordinary vendor edits work without migration restaging. Workers verify each bundled file against that identity. SkyRL may depend on Marin inside its nested environment; Marin accesses SkyRL only through the executable. Remove the obsolete `config/external/MarinSkyRL` pin and updater entry. Retain Megatron/vLLM, OPD, Grug, task execution, generation, and checkpoint export. Drop `skyrl-tx`, the unused replay buffer, unsupported launcher registrations, and files outside the declared entrypoint/import/asset closure. A captured local patch preserves math grading and nested runtime bundling. Use compensated reward aggregation to reduce sensitivity to asynchronous evaluation completion order. Preserve the upstream license and an independent-lock CI lane that audits the built wheel against the current checkout. The migration script can refresh the vendored tree as the fork advances. It captures upstream and active work, replays all local vendor changes with a three-way merge, and rebuilds the stacked PR report. A preview leaves the checkout unchanged; apply rejects intervening edits. Conflicts can be resolved in the candidate and saved as a normalized patch for the next refresh. ```mermaid flowchart TB Fork["Fork main + all open PRs
recently active open issues"] --> Snapshot["Snapshot
source, patches, discussions"] Snapshot --> Baseline["Prune + replay local vendor changes"] Local["Current vendor/skyrl edits"] --> Baseline Baseline --> Decision["Inspect candidate / resolve conflicts"] Decision --> Vendor["Apply vendor/skyrl baseline
save patch for next refresh"] Snapshot --> Transplants["Separate PR branches
preserve stack parents"] Transplants --> Publish["Publication after merged cutover
and unchanged source identities"] ``` Open PR changes remain separate from the baseline. Publication previews issue transfers and draft PR creation; execution requires this cutover PR to be merged with the candidate's fork revision and patch hashes, plus unchanged fork main and PR heads/bases. Incomplete transplants require an explicit disposition. Reviewed adaptations can restore needed tests and docs or relocate changes into Marin; the tool captures their patch hashes and replays all selected stacks before pushing draft PRs. Retries reject changed source identities, patch bytes, destination heads, or published text. Include the GPU-qualified Snowball layout from [#10163](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10163): separate reference nodes, recomputation, optimizer offload, and per-role geometry validation. Remove the obsolete FSDP profile. The nested runtime uses published Marin packages and the current harness API. A dedicated updater advances those libraries within the nested version constraints, checks imports and constructor keywords in the isolated environment, and restores the lock on failure. The [migration guide](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/weaver/forks-merge-marinskyrl/docs/dev-guide/skyrl-migration.md) covers refreshes, dependency updates, train/export/resume/evaluate acceptance, and rebasing PRs that edit the deleted fork pin. Move the CPU CatCount, OPD, Grug/Megatron, and asynchronous GPU CatCount schedules into Marin, preserving their metric gates, weekly/manual cases, failure artifacts, and cleanup. Run GPU CatCount from the checked-out Marin revision instead of cloning Marin and rewriting a fork pin. Point new dashboard results at Marin while preserving fork history. The nested executable boundary follows [Harbor #10287](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10287) and [Evalchemy #10288](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10288).

🤖 Holistic review of 1464be7596ee0081871a1c844206484a5efab664.

This PR replaces the pinned `MarinSkyRL` fork with a pruned copy in `vendor/skyrl` that has its own `uv.lock`. Marin launches it as a child process, `uv run --isolated --project vendor/skyrl --frozen marinskyrl iris launch`. `SkyRLRuntime.commit` becomes `source_digest`, the SHA-256 of `marinskyrl/_vendor_provenance.json`. The head commit also removes the FSDP profile and moves the Snowball curriculum arms to Megatron. The Marin integration is small and works with the vendored runtime. The vendored tree, however, cannot be edited in place, which contradicts the PR's main claim. The curriculum rewrite also duplicates an open PR that was validated on GPUs.

**Before.** `_launcher_command` ran `config/external/MarinSkyRL`, a one-package project that pinned the fork at `81ae0ef7`. `update-external.py` and the external-runtime dependency policy advanced that lock. SkyRL fixes landed in the fork, and Marin bumped the pin.

**Design.** `scripts/skyrl_migration.py` snapshots the fork, prunes it to an import closure, applies `config/skyrl-migration/*.patch`, and writes per-file SHA-256s into the provenance file. Two checks enforce those hashes: `check-vendor` in the new `skyrl-wheel` CI lane, and `runtime_bundle._bundle_paths` at launch. Root lint, type checking, and the workspace exclude `vendor/skyrl`. The same script also implements the remaining cutover: transferring issues, publishing transplanted PRs, and a Math500 bundle.

**Evidence and limits.** The PR's comments cite an end-to-end Iris run: train, export, resume in a fresh job, then GSM8K eval. They also cite a passing `skyrl-wheel` lane and a Math500 GPU run, all at `c917a22ada`/`86e91067d2`. Both the Snowball Megatron move and its 1800GB memory allocation in `1464be75` were only checked by composing configs through the launcher; no Snowball GPU run backs them. CI at this head was still pending when this review was written.

**Findings**

- **1. Blocker:** `vendor/skyrl/cloud/iris/runtime_bundle.py:81` and `scripts/skyrl_migration.py:634` reject any vendored file whose bytes differ from the provenance hashes. The only code that writes provenance is `stage` (`scripts/skyrl_migration.py:466`), which needs a fresh `gh` snapshot of the fork plus a patch under `config/skyrl-migration/`. A Marin PR that fixes one line of SkyRL in place therefore fails the `skyrl-wheel` lane, and `marinskyrl iris launch` raises "Runtime source differs from staged provenance". That contradicts the body's "Source changes can land with Marin" and its claim that the boundary matches Harbor #10287, which hashes the checked-out source. Fix: compute `source_digest` from the bundled files at launch, as a hash of the sorted (path, sha256) list, in both `skyrl_runtime_digest` and `runtime_bundle`. Then drop the per-file `files` map and the patch-hash check, so `check-vendor` reduces to `uv lock --check` plus the wheel build.
- **2. Related PR:** `experiments/post_training/curriculum_rl/launch.py:319`: `1464be75` moves Snowball to Megatron but keeps `colocate_policy_ref=True`, so the reference model shares the policy nodes. #10163 makes the same move with H100 smokes. It found that a reference on the policy nodes ran out of GPU memory, so it gives the reference two nodes of its own and adds recomputation, optimizer offload, and per-role layout preflight. #10163 also deletes `SkyRLRuntimeProfile`. This PR leaves that enum with a single member (`lib/marin/src/marin/rl/skyrl.py:62`) plus the `_STRATEGY_FOR_PROFILE` lookup. Land #10163 first, then rebase this PR so it keeps #10163's recipes and drops its own `curriculum_rl/launch.py` and `async_rl.py` rewrite.
- **3. Should fix:** `vendor/skyrl/pyproject.toml:14` and `:38` pin `marin-verifyit`, `marin-rolloutengine`, `marin-shellbox`, and `marin-taskcompendium` to `b3206ac1`. That commit exists only on draft #10190's branch, not on `main`. This PR also deletes the updater that used to advance the lock (`config/update-external.py`, `scripts/ci/dependency_update_policy.py`). As a result, the vendored runtime keeps running unmerged Marin library code, fixes to those four libraries on `main` never reach SkyRL, and the lock stops resolving if #10190's branch is rewritten. Use editable path sources to `../../lib/<pkg>` and bundle them, as #10287 does for Rigging and FineStore. At minimum, repin to a `main` commit and keep an updater entry.
- **4. Should fix:** `scripts/skyrl_migration.py:802` and `:839`: `plan`, `stage`, `transfer-issues`, `publish-prs`, and `prepare-math500` are one-time fork-migration tooling. Together with `tests/infra/test_skyrl_migration.py` (520 lines), `config/skyrl-migration/snapshot-report.md`, and `config/skyrl-migration/smoke/`, they add about 2,000 lines that nothing runs after cutover. The sibling vendoring PRs, #10287 and #10288, ship no equivalent. Keep only `check-vendor`, reduced as in finding 1, as a CI entry point under `infra/ci/`. Run the transfer and publication steps from this branch or a session artifact, and drop the migration test file with them.
- **5. Related PR:** Several open PRs still edit `config/external/MarinSkyRL/{pyproject.toml,uv.lock}`, which this PR deletes: #10078, #9799, and #9626, plus drafts #10045, #10066, #10190, and #9749. After this PR merges, each must be redone as a `vendor/skyrl` change. Under finding 1, that also means re-staging the fork. Resolve finding 1 before merging, and tell those authors which path to rebase onto.

topics.title: Marin eval policy roadmap
topics.body:
OVERVIEW

Our first task for you concerns the next iteration of our eval policy! As you are no doubt aware, we are very excited to have you help create and source new high quality evals for Marin, and help direct our eval policy. We have many directions we are excited to explore that the current iteration either does not cover, or covers with insufficient granularity.

Therefore, your first assignment at Marin is to create a *roadmap* for Marin’s eval policy. Look into the details of the current policy and consider -- what, in your estimation, are the most crucial areas for us to improve upon? Here are some candidates we could consider; please treat these as suggestions or starting points, not as mandates. You are free to pick your own priorities. Also, please treat this as an unordered set rather than an ordered priority list!

OPEN QUESTIONS

1. Marin currently does not explicitly evaluate the multilingual capabilities of its models under the policy. This stands in contrast to projects like OpenEuroLLM, which are explicitly emphasizing multilingual ability. There are many evals of this type we could consider including, such as [JudgeArena](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/JudgeArena). We could also start evaluating our models’ capabilities in the realm of culturally idiomatic language.
2. simpleQA (or a miniaturized version of it) is a benchmark we are excited to evaluate under our policy, because we believe it has the potential to correlate well with our out-of-distribution AAII target. That said, our current implementation of simpleQA is producing extremely depressed estimates of model capability. We believe this warrants some investigation; a repaired simpleQA would be a useful addition to our cohort.
3. We should consider adding a more realistic long context eval to our policy to complement MRCR and give a more holistic picture of our models’ retrieval capability.
4. We currently do not evaluate deep research or search capability directly.
5. We lack a comprehensive overview of the long tail of agentic benchmarks which now appear in many frontier labs’ model cards. Should we consider adding some of these to our policy?
6. IFBench scores are depressed and do not seem likely to be a realistic reflection of model instruction following capabilities; a well-designed benchmark derived from the [Snowball conversation lab](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/snowball-conversation-lab) might be a good replacement for this.
7. We have several biology / medical benchmarks we could consider incorporating into future eval policies; biomedical knowledge: MedXpertQA or PubMedQA, Clinical reasoning: HealthBench Professional/ Bedside Bench /ASCENT, Biological discovery: Longevity — genetics regression; LAB-Bench cloning / DNA methylation age comparison, Medical coding: MedConceptsQA — ATC Hard/ MedConceptsQA ICD-10 procedures, hard

DONE WHEN

We have a document that proposes a priority list of what we should focus on in our next eval policy (limitations) and sketches out potential solutions. Ideally, the document will also include an estimated timeline for the next eval policy release.

REFERENCES:

Marin Eval Policy 10-16-26: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197

Snowball V0 vs Baselines -> issue 10199

comments.body:
🤖

# Research

[Policy #10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197) has 26 in-distribution benchmarks, including eight agent tasks and BixBench, plus three reserved out-of-distribution benchmarks. It has no explicit multilingual or search measure; MRCR is its only dedicated long-context benchmark. The [#10199 selection record](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10199) and policy name different Snowball release checkpoints, and the policy documents an Evalchemy timeout/scoring mismatch. Those validity issues should be resolved before expanding the canonical panel.

**Relevant code**
- [Campaign configuration](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5d5f405e097b0062c7b008d3b45c40d2dd73cff7/experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/campaign.yaml) — current benchmark selection.
- [Campaign validator](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5d5f405e097b0062c7b008d3b45c40d2dd73cff7/experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/validate-campaign.sh) — pinned run checks.
- [Campaign implementation #9569](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9569) — existing launcher and records.

# Proposed Fix

Target a policy decision by **November 30, 2026** (six weeks); publish the next version only after a full baseline campaign. The ranked work is:

1. **P0, October 19–23: repair policy evidence.** Reconcile the selected checkpoint and source hashes between [#10197](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197) and [#10199](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10199). Resolve the Evalchemy timeout rule against the pinned implementation and version any scoring change. Define one admission sheet for every candidate: capability measured, task provenance and contamination check, scoring audit, baseline discrimination, runtime, failure rate, and ID/OOD assignment. Do not use reserved AAII scores to tune an in-distribution candidate; the current policy forbids inspecting them before model freeze.
2. **P1, October 19–November 6: pilot factuality and multilingual coverage.** Diagnose depressed SimpleQA results by replaying a fixed model sample through Marin and the [reference scorer](https://github.com/openai/simple-evals/blob/main/simpleqa_eval.py), then adjudicate parser, abstention, and judge disagreements before considering a pinned mini-subset. Pilot a balanced language-by-task panel with per-language scores and native-speaker review of idiomatic prompts; [JudgeArena](https://github.com/OpenEuroLLM/JudgeArena) is a candidate runner, with judge and language bias checked against human labels. Admit either benchmark only if its protocol is reproducible and separates relevant baselines beyond measurement uncertainty.
3. **P2, November 2–13: add realistic long-context evidence.** Pilot a predeclared, common-item, length-stratified subset of [LongBench v2](https://github.com/THUDM/LongBench) alongside MRCR. Report accuracy by context bin, tokenizer fit, truncation, and cost; use the same item set for models being compared. This tests multi-document and other realistic tasks that MRCR does not cover.
4. **P3, November 9–20: gate larger tracks.** Use [#10189](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10189)'s fixed-corpus BrowseComp-Plus baseline to decide whether search/deep research is ready for a later policy; keep retrieval and answer accuracy separate. Audit IFBench failure traces and a held-out Snowball conversation alternative before replacing its score. Review the existing eight agent tasks for missing capabilities, and coordinate any new biomedical task with [#9258](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258), where grading ambiguity and coverage are still open.
5. **November 23–30: freeze and release.** Select only pilots that pass the admission sheet, pin data/prompts/judges/serving configs, run the complete baseline cohort, preserve traces, and meet the policy's ≥90% scored-trial coverage rule. Publish per-benchmark scores with uncertainty, costs, failed/graded coverage, ID/OOD status, and the reasons for deferring each candidate. If a full cohort or audit misses the gate, move the release date rather than publish a partial canonical panel.

🤖

The [2026 hallucination benchmark review](https://gist.github.com/penfever/432308318dc38eaf8c32e69a8a491288) recommends a battery because closed-book factuality, grounded faithfulness, abstention, long-form verification, and detector localization measure different failures.

For the next in-distribution policy, pilot these additions:

1. [HalluLens](https://aclanthology.org/2025.acl-long.1176/) NonExistentRefusal and PreciseWikiQA for false-premise acceptance, refusal, and dynamic short-form factuality.
2. [RAGTruth](https://aclanthology.org/2024.acl-long.585/) plus [FaithBench](https://aclanthology.org/2025.naacl-short.38/) for grounded response-level and span-level hallucination detection. FaithBench is a disagreement-selected hard set, so report it as a stress test rather than a prevalence estimate.
3. [FactBench](https://aclanthology.org/2025.acl-long.1587/) or a pinned [LongFact/SAFE](https://github.com/google-deepmind/long-form-factuality) slice for claim-level support in long-form, open-world answers. Preserve retrieved evidence and judge inputs because search and judge changes can move the score.

For the SimpleQA work already proposed here, use [SimpleQA Verified](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.07968) rather than SimpleQA-mini and report correct, incorrect, and abstained rates separately.

Exclude AA-Omniscience and all other Artificial Analysis tasks. They are out of distribution under the current policy. The candidates above are not components of the current AAII 4.3 panel. Keep TruthfulQA as a narrow misconception benchmark instead of treating it as comprehensive hallucination coverage.

topics.title: [rolloutengine] History resets silently discard earlier TITO training actions
topics.body:
RolloutEngine can silently discard earlier generated actions from training when an agent changes its next request. Exact-token checks still pass because the reset clears their reference state. A whole-task training sample can therefore contain only the final segment while carrying the reward for the entire attempt.

Confirmed at Marin `f45f04b293128bd8a5b1567e03bef59c7f59e1d0`, with MarinSkyRL `97415bb1432688bc3d316b94e0f649a8d04d2ad7` and Harbor `a85964704593b7d89428ef480238ffce8be3a63c`. These are the pins of [Smartie run 2026.10.19.57](https://wandb.ai/dogml/snowball-smartie-rl/runs/v1vksnkr), using Mini SWE Agent 2.1.0, exact-token tracing, requested behavior logprobs, and whole-task training (`step_wise_training: false`). This report does not establish whether subsequent main revisions still have the defect.

Minimal reproduction procedure derived from the pinned code (not yet executed as a standalone test):

1. Run a two-turn `AgentTaskSession` with exact-token tracing. Return a first assistant message and its served prompt IDs, completion IDs, and behavior logprobs.
2. Have the agent send the same history back with an additional null-valued assistant-message field, such as `annotations: null`. Keep content, tools, and generation options unchanged.
3. `AgentTaskSession.advance()` compares raw message dictionaries and returns `reset_conversation`.
4. The engine calls `trace.reset()` and `steps.clear()`. Complete the second turn and grade the task.
5. Inspect the resulting `RolloutData` and training projection: the first action's loss tokens and step record are absent. The second turn passes exact-token checks as a fresh segment.

Changing only `max_tokens` also triggers the reset because the adapter compares the entire options dictionary.

Relevant code:

- [Adapter prefix/options comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f45f04b293128bd8a5b1567e03bef59c7f59e1d0/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/agent_session.py#L98).
- [Engine reset clears trace, steps, and completed-record fields](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f45f04b293128bd8a5b1567e03bef59c7f59e1d0/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/engine.py#L368).
- [Exact-token trace reset and prefix validation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f45f04b293128bd8a5b1567e03bef59c7f59e1d0/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/trace.py#L45).
- [MarinSkyRL whole-task and step projections](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/97415bb1432688bc3d316b94e0f649a8d04d2ad7/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/task_projections.py#L237) consume the surviving trace; neither can recover cleared actions.

In a sample of 19 training attempts, all 254 completed-turn-to-next-request boundaries satisfied the reset condition: 170 differed only by null fields or empty provider metadata, 82 omitted an assistant response after Mini SWE Agent reported “No tool calls found,” and two changed only `max_tokens`. In 136 of the metadata-only cases, the next served prompt exactly extended the previous prompt plus completion. Those resets were unnecessary even under the strict token-prefix contract. The other 34 had changed token prefixes; the cause of those token differences has not been isolated. The sample consists of 16 seeded random installed-agent directories plus three attempts linked to retained training records; it is not a population-wide frequency estimate. These boundary counts classify captured requests against the pinned reset condition.

Separately, 687 retained Stage 1 training records each contain only one trainable step boundary, although 662 contain multiple assistant messages. One 19-assistant-message attempt retains only a 522-token final segment as trainable. Retention favors failures and loops; this does not establish frequencies in consumed optimizer batches. Raw task traces remain private.

Expected:

- Under token-in/token-out (TITO), changing inference context must never silently delete earlier training evidence. Preserve each generated action's exact served prompt, completion tokens, behavior logprobs, and loss mask.
- A component that rewrites history must satisfy the training contract before the engine accepts the rewrite. In strict append-only mode, reject incompatible compaction, history edits, or tool-definition changes before applying them. This rejection is the minimum acceptable behavior when full preservation is unsupported. Do not turn an invalid whole-task trajectory into a valid-looking final-segment sample.
- Support for non-prefix histories must be explicit. If segmented training is supported, preserve all segments within the same rollout and define reward attribution across them. Do not reconstruct earlier actions under the rewritten prompt.
- Transport metadata and generation-budget changes must not cause false history resets. Genuine prompt changes still require validation.
- Enforce episode completeness separately from token integrity: aligned tokens and logprobs in the surviving segment do not prove that all required actions survived.

Regression tests should exercise a real Mini SWE Agent/LiteLLM serialization round trip, a missing-tool-call response, a budget-only change, and genuine compaction/tool-definition changes. Assert that every action remains represented in training, or that an unsupported rewrite is explicitly rejected. Changing only the projection to step-wise training is insufficient because the engine already clears the step list.

Historical scope: the older successful Terminus-2 path checked captured token streams and marked all continuous completion spans for loss; see [the pinned assembler](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/a03b2773/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/trajectory_runners/trajectory_processing.py#L1761) and [reported training results](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9225#issuecomment-5777718831). That path also had limitations for genuine history rewrites. The newer adapter/integration is described in #10054 and [MarinSkyRL #1010](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/1010). The trace-loss defect is confirmed; its contribution to Smartie's later reward decline has not been isolated experimentally.

🤖
# Research

The pinned Smartie run used the pre-[#10203](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10203) reset path, which discarded completed turns. Current Marin `5ec80e7124` retains each conversation and its token evidence, but `AgentHarness` still starts a new conversation when raw message dictionaries or any option differ. The rollout API permits a trainer to use only the last conversation; the issue's pinned MarinSkyRL projection cannot recover earlier actions, and its current pin and projection need verification during the port.

**Relevant code**
- [`recorder.py#L404-L417`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5ec80e71242485b353b1f4556d3d68eb0a4dddf5/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/recorder.py#L404-L417) — retains previous conversation on start
- [`external.py#L89-L105`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5ec80e71242485b353b1f4556d3d68eb0a4dddf5/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/harness/external.py#L89-L105) — raw history and options comparison
- [`models.py#L127-L150`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5ec80e71242485b353b1f4556d3d68eb0a4dddf5/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/models.py#L127-L150) — per-conversation evidence and trainer choice
- [`test_rollout.py#L697-L720`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5ec80e71242485b353b1f4556d3d68eb0a4dddf5/lib/rolloutengine/tests/test_rollout.py#L697-L720) — retained masks across a restart
- [`task_projections.py#L237`](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/97415bb1432688bc3d316b94e0f649a8d04d2ad7/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/task_projections.py#L237) — pinned training projection

# TITO training across conversation starts

A training attempt must account for every sampled action before carrying its task reward. The engine's retained conversations make that possible, but they do not make a last-conversation projection complete.

## Challenges

The agent's chat round trip can add null or empty provider fields without changing the rendered prompt. `max_tokens` changes generation, not prior context. A missing assistant message, compaction, or changed tool definition can change the served prefix. These cases need distinct treatment before a request becomes training data.

## Costs / Risks

The initial completeness guard will reject some otherwise useful attempts until continuation classification improves. Existing records from the old reset path cannot be repaired from their final segment. Updating MarinSkyRL's rollout engine pin and training projection must land together.

## Design

1. Port MarinSkyRL to the post-#10203 `Rollout.conversations` API. In exact-token TITO training, reject a rollout with multiple conversations before projecting or assigning its task reward. Record a structured rejection reason and retain the full rollout for diagnosis. Do not emit a final-segment sample. This is the minimum safety gate; keep old-pinned agent TITO training disabled until it lands.
2. At the agent/transport boundary, compare the fields that the real Mini SWE Agent/LiteLLM serializer puts into the model prompt. Normalize only proven transport-only null and empty metadata. Separate generation-only options such as `max_tokens` from context-defining options, and pass the current generation budget through `reply()` without starting a new conversation. Keep exact served-prefix and logprob checks.
3. In strict TITO mode, reject a missing assistant response, compaction, changed tool definitions, or any unclassified prompt rewrite before forwarding the next model request. Surface an explicit contract failure and suppress training projection for that attempt. If segmented training is later supported, project *every* retained conversation with its own served prompt, sampled tokens, loss mask, and logprobs, and specify how the task reward is attributed across segments. Never rebuild earlier actions under a rewritten prompt.

## Testing

Use a real Mini SWE Agent/LiteLLM serialization round trip with two model turns. Null assistant fields, empty provider metadata, and a budget-only change should leave both actions in one exact-token sample when the rendered token prefix is continuous; a changed prefix should fail explicitly. A missing-tool-call response, genuine compaction, and a tool-definition change should fail the strict training gate. Assert sampled-action counts, loss masks, logprobs, and reward assignment at the MarinSkyRL projection boundary; engine tests should continue to show that interrupted or restarted rollouts retain earlier evidence.

## Open Questions

- After the strict guard lands, should non-prefix attempts remain ineligible for TITO training, or should MarinSkyRL train every retained segment? Segment training needs an explicit terminal-reward attribution rule.

topics.title: [moe] Speed up d1280 baseline cross entropy backward
topics.body:
Select Levanter's existing `xla_fast_bwd` fused cross-entropy backend for the hidden-width 1280 baseline MoE heuristic. Other widths keep the default backend. The forward loss and attention configuration match the current baseline.

In matched 32-step runs with hidden width 1280, batch size 256, sequence length 4096, and TPU v4-32, median throughput over steps 10–30 rose from [161,468 tokens/s with the default backend](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/moe_baseline_ce_probe_d1280_issue9529_main_ce_control_a) to [166,723 tokens/s with fast backward](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/moe_baseline_ce_probe_d1280_issue9529_main_ce_fast_b), a 3.25% gain. Both runs finished on JAX 0.11.1 and libtpu 0.0.46. Final training loss was 8.977 for control and 8.984 for fast backward; these short runs do not establish long-run quality. A small-model test checks exact loss equality and projection and embedding gradient agreement within 1e-5.

topics.body: Design doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1LVfMDHRBKBk_Bn9PY1J9Lb_MYwdUTFP5PkX2br25TNg/edit?tab=t.izhzsywzorld. Final results and the full ledger: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9920#issuecomment-6076348127 (ledger also at https://gist.github.com/karansag/0ce1a07580bd430bc8c5b890069385b0). ## TL;DR (final, 2026-10-09). ** Given **one expert E** ([open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272 @ fb4f8051](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272/tree/fb4f8051a344fec59f902bdd2ca876ac1b2f3296) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task133-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-step92-lr1e-05/2026.10.07.5/hf/step-272`)) built from the Snowball student B ([open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92 @ fdc3c3c5](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92/tree/fdc3c3c5fff489d3fb04dcbc2387c179b1bf3fab)) by SFT on [GLM 5.3](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3) CruxEval traces, three methods were used to transfer E's gain back into B: * plain SFT on E's traces * SFT on rejection-sampled E traces (RS-SFT) * on-policy distillation from E (OPD). All three recover most or all of E's CruxEval gain on the 1,600 training-is-test prompts (4x sample traces from the test set size). Two-pass CruxEval input / output accuracy on the selected checkpoints: plain SFT 73.9 / 72.0, RS-SFT 80.8 / 77.9, OPD 79.6 / 75.2, against E 79.4 / 71.4 and B 55.4 / 57.8. RS-SFT and OPD are both 3–7 pp above plain SFT; the RS-SFT vs OPD ordering (1.2 / 2.7 pp) is unresolved with one run per arm and two evaluator passes. No arm dropped below B on GSM8K or MATH500. Training cost: plain SFT 61.6 H100-h, RS-SFT 57.4, OPD 376.4 for the full run (286.9 to the selected checkpoint, plus 14–15 per HF export). RS-SFT used ground-truth execution results to select demos; the other arms did not. These numbers measure transfer on seen prompts, not generalization. ## Results (selected checkpoints; CruxEval two-pass means, pass@1 %, 800 problems per direction; "gap closed" = gain over B divided by E's gain over B).** | Model | CruxEval input | CruxEval output | Gap closed (in / out) | GSM8K | MATH500 | Training H100-h | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | B ([baseline Snowball student, HF @ fdc3c3c5](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92/tree/fdc3c3c5fff489d3fb04dcbc2387c179b1bf3fab)) | 55.4 | 57.8 | 0 | 90.4 | 89.8 | — | | [GLM 5.3](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3) (teacher of E; served as `glm-5.3` through the internal glm53 relay, reasoning effort high) | 94.0 | 90.5 | — | — | — | — | | E (expert; B + SFT on GLM traces, step 272; [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272 @ fb4f8051](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272/tree/fb4f8051a344fec59f902bdd2ca876ac1b2f3296) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task133-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-step92-lr1e-05/2026.10.07.5/hf/step-272`)) | 79.4 | 71.4 | 100% | 92.1 | 92.2 | 35.9 | | Plain SFT on E demos, 400 updates (final; [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Plain-SFT-Step399 @ 3e34be3f](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Plain-SFT-Step399/tree/3e34be3f884ff737f85354b060ea831ce0c90636) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task145-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-plain-e-from-b-lr1e-06/2026.10.08.1/hf/step-399`)) | 73.9 | 72.0 | 77% / 104% | 94.0 | 92.6 | 61.6 | | RS-SFT on execution-correct E demos, 283 of 376 updates ([open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-RS-SFT-Step282 @ 073d128c](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-RS-SFT-Step282/tree/073d128cb1e53652126cce37a7cc2c96625d3c80) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task145-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-rs-e-from-b-lr1e-06/2026.10.08.1/hf/step-282`)) | 80.8 | 77.9 | 106% / 148% | 93.5 | 93.6 | 57.4 (full run) | | OPD from E, 75 of 100 updates ([open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-OPD-Step75 @ 9d189320](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-OPD-Step75/tree/9d1893207226cf72f701187e1d5260d9fc3c931d) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/karan/skyrl/snowball-opd-cruxeval-e-2/exports/global_step_75/policy`)) | 79.6 | 75.2 | 101% / 128% | 92.5 | 90.4 | 286.9 to the checkpoint; 376.4 full run; +14–15 per HF export | ## Models Student B = [`open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92` @ `fdc3c3c5`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92/tree/fdc3c3c5fff489d3fb04dcbc2387c179b1bf3fab) (Hugging Face commit; the repo received a later commit on 2026-10-13, so the pin matters). E = B after full SFT on 1,454 execution-correct [GLM 5.3](https://huggingface.co/zai-org/GLM-5.3) CruxEval traces (trace collection: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/scratch/karan/glm-bench-traces/`) (LR 1e-5, 3 epochs, 272 updates, 32 H100, fresh optimizer state, frozen router biases), export [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272 @ fb4f8051](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Expert-E-Step272/tree/fb4f8051a344fec59f902bdd2ca876ac1b2f3296) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task133-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-step92-lr1e-05/2026.10.07.5/hf/step-272`). E keeps B's tokenizer and chat template. E+ (E + 2 epochs at LR 1e-6; 80.2 / 75.1) was built as a separate reference and is not an arm. Every arm starts from B. ## Benchmark CruxEval (800 Python functions; input prediction and output prediction scored separately by executing the assertion). MATH500 was dropped as the target because B already scores 89.8% there; GSM8K and MATH500 are the collapse checks. Teacher gate: B 55.4 / 57.8; GLM 5.3 on the identical 1,600 prompts 94.0 / 90.5; E 79.4 / 71.4 (two-pass mean), passing the gate of B + 10 points on both tasks with no GSM8K drop. ## Frozen evaluator Marin `experiments.evaluation.cli launch` with Evalchemy [`ae362881cf53f869a6ad52c8a59fa17343c0b5f8`](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/commit/ae362881cf53f869a6ad52c8a59fa17343c0b5f8), vLLM on H100x8 (DP8 + EP8), `max_model_len` 32768, `max_gen_toks` 30720, `enable_thinking: true`, reasoning parser `grug`. Configs and pitfalls: https://gist.github.com/karansag/49de943771b98a7a23d9348b58933f71. Evalchemy's chat client sends no temperature, top_p or seed, and B's `generation_config.json` sets none, so every run samples at vLLM's default (temperature 1.0, unseeded). One pass on 800 problems has a binomial 95% half-width of about 3.5 pp; selected checkpoints get two passes. **Arms as run (all from B; AdamW LR 1e-6 constant, betas 0.9/0.999, weight decay 0, grad clip 1.0, router bias frozen; 4 epochs over the 1,600 prompts; one checkpoint per epoch).** - E demos: 8 samples per prompt from E at temperature 1.0, both directions, execution-graded in an isolated container (12,800 samples, 14.6 H100-h, shared by both SFT arms). - Plain SFT: E's first sample per prompt, correct or not (1,600 rows; 1.45M supervised tokens per epoch; batch 16; Levanter, 32 H100). - RS-SFT: first execution-correct sample per prompt (1,503 rows; 97 prompts with no correct sample stay in the eval denominator; 1.06M supervised tokens per epoch; Levanter, 32 H100). - OPD: [MarinSkyRL](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL), 4 on-policy rollouts per prompt at temperature 1.0, E as the teacher (sampled reverse KL on chosen tokens, no verifier), 64 prompts per update, 25 updates per epoch; 4 learner + 1 rollout + 1 teacher H100x8 nodes (Megatron). - Selection: the final checkpoint when it is similar or better than the previous one on both CruxEval directions, otherwise a second pass on both and the two-pass means decide. Plain SFT selected its final checkpoint (400 updates); RS-SFT (283 of 376) and OPD (75 of 100) selected their epoch-3 checkpoints after their finals dropped on one direction. ## Artifacts Trace browser (GLM, E, E+ traces, side-by-side compare): https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/072c90b0-281e-4692-a4bf-845874c021b1/. OPD W&B: https://wandb.ai/marin-community/skyrl/runs/p3ie2bg7. Selected exports: plain [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Plain-SFT-Step399 @ 3e34be3f](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-Plain-SFT-Step399/tree/3e34be3f884ff737f85354b060ea831ce0c90636) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task145-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-plain-e-from-b-lr1e-06/2026.10.08.1/hf/step-399`), RS-SFT [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-RS-SFT-Step282 @ 073d128c](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-RS-SFT-Step282/tree/073d128cb1e53652126cce37a7cc2c96625d3c80) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/task145-cruxeval/checkpoints/karan/cruxeval-rs-e-from-b-lr1e-06/2026.10.08.1/hf/step-282`), OPD [open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-OPD-Step75 @ 9d189320](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-CruxEval-OPD-Step75/tree/9d1893207226cf72f701187e1d5260d9fc3c931d) (S3 source `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/karan/skyrl/snowball-opd-cruxeval-e-2/exports/global_step_75/policy`). Eval records: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals//record.json` (every record id is in the final comment's ledger). GPU-hour method: https://gist.github.com/karansag/500604143668730f8e79277b43f39298. ## Not in scope Weight merging (needs RL-trained experts that share B's init; none exist) and transfer from the older Snowball experts (none beats B under the matched eval). ## Decision log - 2026-10-06: matched eval of B and the existing experts (E6, E17a, E18, SWE, Stage-3) on MATH500/GSM8K; none beats B, so no promotion to teacher. - 2026-10-07: MATH500 near ceiling for B → CruxEval chosen; MMLU-Pro (B 44.1) and GPQA-D (B 41.9) measured as fallbacks and not used. - 2026-10-07: full SFT over LoRA for building E; LoRA kept as the fallback if full SFT collapses out-of-domain. - 2026-10-07: rejection-sampled SFT added as a third arm. - 2026-10-08: E frozen at step 272 for every arm; E+ built as a separate reference only. Arms changed from the plan: one sample per prompt for both SFT arms (not up to 4), no LR sweep, 4 rollouts per prompt for OPD. The arms ran in parallel on Iris. - 2026-10-09: RS-SFT and OPD final checkpoints not selected (drops on one direction with paired CI excluding 0); epoch-3 checkpoints selected on two-pass means. Final results posted in one comment; the running-log comments were removed and are archived with the ledger.

# Research

Teacher training and three transfer arms make this a gated experiment. As of 23:29 UTC, the owner has submitted the W&B-corrected teacher retry; startup, optimizer progress, and export remain unconfirmed ([latest status](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9920#issuecomment-6048938002)). No open PR targets #9920, while the owner is already preparing the recipe on `task/133`; the earlier coding-teacher spike [#9528](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9528) ended without a usable MOPD transfer result.

**Relevant code**
- [`experiments/sft/launcher.py#L494`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/experiments/sft/launcher.py#L494) — shared SFT specification and training setup
- [`lib/marin/src/marin/rl/skyrl.py#L150`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/skyrl.py#L150) — versioned SkyRL experiment and export contract
- [`experiments/evaluation/cli.py#L147`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/experiments/evaluation/cli.py#L147) — shared evaluation launch path

# Proposed Fix

1. Follow the submitted teacher retry through a completed update, full training, and verified HF exports. Evaluate the planned exports with the frozen CruxEval/GSM8K configuration. Stop the transfer arms unless E clears the stated +10-point gate on both CruxEval directions without a GSM8K drop beyond noise.
2. Pin E, B, prompt IDs, tokenizer/template, grader, evaluator, and one eight-sample-per-prompt teacher generation artifact. Build unfiltered SFT from samples 1–4 and rejection-sampled SFT from up to four execution-correct samples. Record missing-correct-sample prompts, actual supervised tokens, and teacher-generation GPU-hours; a matched prompt set alone does not equalize training tokens.
3. Start OPD from the same B and prompts. Check teacher/student token-score alignment and one update plus export before the full run. Match the planned sweep and student update budget across arms, and record teacher-scoring GPU-hours separately.
4. Evaluate every selected arm twice with the same pinned evaluator on CruxEval input, CruxEval output, and GSM8K. Report each arm's accuracy, `(arm − B) / (E − B)` per direction, run-to-run spread, prompts and tokens consumed, and total GPU-hours. Label gains as transfer on the trained test prompts; this protocol cannot establish held-out generalization.

🤖 Final results: SFT vs rejection-sampled SFT vs on-policy distillation for transferring the CruxEval expert back into B

TL;DR. All three arms recover most or all of the expert's CruxEval gain. Every arm trains on prompts drawn from the same 1,600 the evaluator scores (800 input-prediction and 800 output-prediction problems; plain SFT and OPD use all 1,600, RS-SFT the 1,503 with an execution-correct E sample), so this is transfer on seen prompts. Two-pass means on the selected checkpoints: plain SFT 73.9 / 72.0 (400 updates), RS-SFT 80.8 / 77.9 (283 updates), OPD 79.6 / 75.2 (75 updates); the expert E scores 79.4 / 71.4 and B scores 55.4 / 57.8 (CruxEval input / output, pass@1 on 800 problems each). RS-SFT's two-pass means are 1.2 / 2.7 pp above OPD's; two passes on one run per arm do not resolve that ordering. Both are above plain SFT by 5.7–6.9 pp on input and 3.2–5.9 pp on output. Between arms, the measured two-pass means put RS-SFT 1.2 / 2.7 pp above OPD and both 3–7 pp above plain SFT; each arm is one training run with no LR sweep, same-checkpoint pass pairs moved 0.5–3.1 pp on the six repeated checkpoints, and two repeats do not estimate run-to-run variance, so the RS-SFT vs OPD ordering is unresolved and the gap to plain SFT is the better-supported difference. Deviations from the plan in the issue body.

- Plain SFT used one sample per prompt (E's sample 0, 1,600 rows), and RS-SFT used the first execution-correct sample per prompt (1,503 rows), instead of up to 4 samples per prompt. Uncovered prompts stayed in the eval denominator.
- No LR or epoch sweep was run for any arm; every arm used LR 1e-6 and 4 epochs, with per-epoch checkpoints as the only sweep.
- OPD used 4 rollouts per prompt, so its prompt epochs are not token- or compute-matched to the SFT arms.
- GSM8K and MATH500 are both reported as collapse checks (the plan named GSM8K only).

Material failures and fixes.

- Levanter could not HF-export from an S3 reference checkpoint; fixed by plumbing `hf_save_reference_code=False`.
- MarinSkyRL accepted teachers only as HF repo ids; added staging of the teacher from S3. The export-only job's config inherited the run's distillation objective, which requires a teacher the export job does not start, so the export failed at config validation; the fix drops the distillation block from the export config. Learner nodes ran out of host memory at checkpoint save with 512 GB; the full run reserved 1024 GB.
- MarinSkyRL does not convert checkpoints to HF format during training; it writes a small export request per checkpoint, and the conversion is a separate 4-node export-only job (about 14–15 H100-h each).
- The Marin eval runner keeps the serve address it first resolved. When the serve job is preempted and re-registers on another host, the eval loops on connection errors until its timeout. Two RS eval groups were lost this way and relaunched as fresh groups; no partial outputs were reused. Not fixed yet.
- Evalchemy sends no temperature or seed, so every run samples at vLLM's default. One GSM8K run failed Evalchemy's preflight request 9 s after the serve registered (server disconnected); relaunched alone, it passed.
- GPQA-D (41.9%, needs an HF token and a 28,672-token generation cap) and MMLU-Pro (44.1%) were measured on B while choosing the benchmark, as fallbacks in case CruxEval failed the teacher gate; they were not used further.

Reading:
- Everything is a small perturbation: no checkpoint moves more than 0.13% of B's weight norm overall, and the largest component change is the expert's attention at 0.65%.
- The expert (LR 1e-5, 3 epochs, 1,454 rows) concentrates its change in attention, the router and the LM head and leaves the MoE expert MLPs almost untouched (0.047%, 13% of weights changed). The two SFT transfer arms (LR 1e-6, 4 epochs, 1,500–1,600 rows of the expert's text) do the opposite: they move the expert MLPs 4–6× more than the expert did and touch 35–41% of all weights. OPD moves least of the three arms (0.035% overall, comparable to the expert) and touches 20%.
- Direction: none of the arms re-creates the expert's weight change. The cosines between an arm's delta and E's delta are 0.05–0.12 in attention and the expert MLPs (random directions in this dimension give ≈0). The one shared direction is the LM head, where plain SFT and RS-SFT align with E (cosine 0.68 and 0.71) while OPD moves the LM head the opposite way (−0.32). Recovering the expert's CruxEval score therefore does not require copying its weights; three different weight changes produce it.
- RS-SFT changes the weights less than plain SFT (0.094% vs 0.123% overall) while scoring higher; it trains on fewer, verifier-correct rows.

Method: every tensor of each checkpoint was compared with the student B (open-athena/Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92 @ fdc3c3c5) in float32 after widening the bf16 exports; ‖Δ‖/‖B‖ is the relative Frobenius norm over all 67.1 B weights or over one component (attention q/k/v/o and attention gates; the 26 layers' fused MoE expert MLPs, 65.4 B weights; shared experts; router weights and biases; embeddings; LM head), 'weights changed' is the share of scalars whose bf16 value differs from B's, and cos(Δ, Δ_expert) is the cosine between the checkpoint's delta and the expert's delta over the same weights. Embeddings and norms are omitted from the table (relative change ≤ 0.01% everywhere). Caveat: the exports are bf16, so training-time changes below half a bf16 ulp of a weight are invisible; magnitudes and 'weights changed' are lower bounds, and the cosines are computed only on what survived rounding. ## Method

Deltas against the student B (`Snowball-67B-A2B-10T-Mixed-RLVR-Sync-Step92` @ fdc3c3c5) for expert E (step 272) and the three selected checkpoints: OPD update 75, plain SFT step 399, RS-SFT step 282. Per component: the Frobenius norm of each delta (absolute and relative to B), cosine with E's delta, sign agreement on weights changed in both, and subspace overlap. Overlap is the share of a delta's energy inside E's top-k singular directions per matrix, with k holding 50% of E's energy, compared with a random k-dim subspace and with E's delta permuted within each matrix. |---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Expert E | 0.0366% | 13.7% | — | — | — |
| OPD update 75 | 0.0355% | 20.3% | 0.079 | 0.598 | 0.203 (0.101) |
| RS-SFT step 282 | 0.0938% | 34.5% | 0.058 | 0.581 | 0.196 (0.108) |
| Plain SFT step 399 | 0.1236% | 41.2% | 0.045 | 0.562 | 0.184 (0.108) |

Overlap with E's half-energy subspace, as a multiple of the random null:

| Component | OPD 75 | RS-SFT 282 | plain SFT 399 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Attention | 3.9× | 3.0× | 2.7× |
| Expert MLPs | 1.9× | 1.7× | 1.6× |
| Shared experts | 4.0× | 2.6× | 2.2× |
| Router | 3.7× | 2.2× | 2.1× |
| LM head | 391× | 710× | 686× |

## Reading

- **Same pattern as #9984, and stronger.** OPD shares direction with E more than either SFT arm in attention, expert MLPs, shared experts and over all weights. It is also more aligned than the MOPD update was there (all-weights cosine 0.079 vs 0.049).
- **Size.** OPD moves the weights about as much as E did (0.036% of ‖B‖). The SFT arms move them 2.6–3.4× more, mostly in the expert MLPs (0.20–0.27% vs E's 0.05%).
- **Router.** OPD leaves the router almost untouched (0.006% of its norm, against E's 0.17%). Its router cosine with E equals the SFT arms' (0.15 vs 0.14–0.15); only its sign agreement and overlap are higher.
- **LM head.** The SFT arms align strongly with E (cosine 0.68–0.71). OPD moves inside the same few top directions but with the opposite sign (cosine −0.32, sign agreement 0.26). MOPD showed the same flip in #9984 (−0.14), so it repeats across both experiments.
- **Small shared part.** 0.6% of OPD's update energy lies along E's delta, and 20% sits inside E's half-energy subspace against 10% at random. The transfer is mostly a different weight change that reaches the same behaviour.

## Limits

Correlational geometry only, with no ablation, so no causal claim about the scores. OPD 75 is the selected mid-run checkpoint, not the final update 100. The SFT arms train on E's own samples in one domain, which raises their alignment with E. bf16 exports hide changes below half an ulp, so every measure covers only what survived rounding.

🤖 Efficiency view: CruxEval score against GPU-hours and trained tokens, per checkpoint.

| Arm, checkpoint (updates) | H100-h | trained tokens | input / output |
|---|---|---|---|
| B (start) | 0 | 0 | 55.4 / 57.75 |
| Plain SFT 101 / 201 / 301 / 400 | 30.2 / 45.6 / 61.0 / 76.2 | 1.5 / 2.9 / 4.4 / 5.8M | 69.6 / 67.5; 73.5 / 69.9; 69.4 / 71.75; 74.75 / 71.25 |
| RS-SFT 95 / 189 / 283 / 376 | 29.1 / 43.5 / 57.8 / 72.0 | 1.1 / 2.1 / 3.2 / 4.2M | 75.5 / 72.0; 82.0 / 75.75; 81.4 / 77.1; 77.0 / 76.5 |
| OPD 25 / 50 / 75 / 100 | 108.5 / 203.3 / 296.5 / 391.5 | 8.8 / 14.2 / 20.2 / 26.2M | 74.9 / 68.9; 81.75 / 75.75; 79.0 / 76.75; 80.9 / 72.25 |
| E (expert, reference) | 35.9 | 1.8M | 79.4 / 71.4 (two-pass mean) |

How the numbers are built:
- **H100-hours.** Each arm's measured training-gang allocation, pro-rated by updates.
- **SFT arms.** Each carries the 14.6 H100-h of the E demo collection from step 0.
- **OPD.** Each checkpoint carries its own export job, about 15 H100-h. Measured allocation-to-checkpoint for OPD, as a cross-check: 118.8 / 197.8 / 286.9 / 375.7 H100-h.
- **Trained tokens.** Loss-bearing tokens, counted each time they are trained on: SFT from the row manifests × epochs, OPD from the run's per-update scored tokens.
- **Excluded.** Evaluations, building E, and failed attempts.

Reading:
- **Cost to reach E's level.** RS-SFT passes E on both directions at update 189 (43.5 H100-h). OPD gets there at update 50 (203.3 H100-h), about 4.7× more GPU time.
- **Matched GPU-hours.** Both SFT runs ended (72 and 76 H100-h) before OPD's first checkpoint (108.5). At the SFT arms' final cost, a straight line from B to OPD update 25 puts OPD at about 68–69 / 65. That is an interpolation between two measured points, not a measurement.
- **Trained tokens.** OPD trains on 4–6× more tokens than the SFT arms, because it trains on its own, longer samples.

Caveats:
- This is not a matched-compute experiment: different optimizers, batch geometry and verifier access (RS uses execution correctness).
- Single passes unless marked; one pass is about ±3.5 pp.
- OPD's W&B history logged 99 of its 100 updates, so the final token count misses one update.
