comments.body:
🤖 Archived the description before automated prose cleanup.
<!-- marin-prose-cleanup-archive:f3222dff26877140da42e038840bb148e9f38e4c71cc334766adb1cad00861b1 -->

<details><summary>Original description</summary>

```markdown
* part of #10165
* stacked on #10203, so this PR shows only its own two commits
* a managed agent is one `run_task` call: a registered harness is the agent program, the model is its endpoint, and a task with `NoGrader` holds open-ended work
* add `ChatModel` in `rolloutengine.chat` (extra `marin-rolloutengine[chat]`), a `TraceMode.MESSAGES` model over an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint, such as vLLM, SGLang, or GLM
  * prompt options replace its `max_tokens` and its `extra_body` keys, and `model`, `messages`, `stream`, and `n` are reserved, also in `extra_body`
  * a response without `usage` is a model failure of one attempt, not a `RolloutContractError` that stops the caller
  * the next request sends back only `role`, `content`, `tool_calls`, and `reasoning_content`, and a refusal goes into `ModelTurn.metadata`
* move `limits` from `RolloutRecorder` to `HarnessContext`, so that an `agent_harness` program, which has no recorder, can read them
* fix three defects that a swarm of agents can get:
  * `check` now rejects `output_paths` without a task machine, which gave `outputs={}` and no error
  * an agent that ends with a `CancelledError` that no task requested, for example from a cancelled child task, now fails its attempt instead of making `run_task` raise `CancelledError` [^1]
  * `RolloutInterrupted` and `GradedRolloutInterrupted` now go through pickle with their rollout, operation, and grade, and `RolloutFailure.diagnostics` keeps the error message and notes, which pickle does not keep [^2]
* docs: a short "Run an agent" section in `docs/references/task-rollouts.md`

[^1]: a requested cancel stays a cancellation, as before
[^2]: before, Zephyr replaced the exception with a `ZephyrWorkerError` that kept only its type and message

```

</details>

🤖 Holistic review of f0934cd1f0b57dafec26a2e6d087eac9002a608a.

This PR lets a managed agent run against an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint through one `run_task` call. It also fixes four failure paths that previously lost information or stopped the caller. The design fits the engine as it is after #10203. Two findings: one guard still lets a `CancelledError` escape `run_task`, and the new `chat` extra installs nothing that the package doesn't already pull in.

**Before.** A `Model` was always a token-exact transport, such as `ReplayModel` or a vLLM bridge. Nothing in the package spoke chat completions. A harness read the attempt's limits from `ModelSession.limits`. An interrupted attempt recorded only `RolloutFailure(type_name, {"operation": ...})`, and `RolloutInterrupted` lost its rollout when pickled across a Zephyr worker boundary. If an `AgentHarness` agent ended with a stray `CancelledError`, for example from awaiting a cancelled child, `agent.result()` re-raised it out of `run_task`, which cancels a caller's `TaskGroup`.

**Design.** `rolloutengine/chat.py` adds `ChatModel`, a frozen dataclass that turns each `ModelRequest` into one non-streaming `chat.completions.create` call. It is valid only under `TraceMode.MESSAGES` and rejects continuation or pinned-token requests. Prompt options override its `max_tokens`/`extra_body`, and setting `model`/`messages`/`stream`/`n` raises. It strips the returned message to fields that a server accepts on the next request. It reports `usage`, which the recorder's `max_total_tokens` budget needs in place of token IDs. `limits` moves from the `ModelSession` protocol to `HarnessContext`, and the two in-repo constructors are updated (no other in-repo caller reads `session.limits`). `_failure_record` in `recorder.py` adds the first 2,000 characters of the message and any `__notes__` to the failure, and is shared by `engine.run_task` and `harness_rollout`. `validate_spec` now rejects `output_paths` when there is no task machine.

**Evidence and limits.** Locally, `tests/test_chat.py` and `tests/test_rollout.py` pass (202 passed, 3 deselected). The chat tests drive the real `openai.AsyncOpenAI` client over an `httpx.MockTransport`, so request bodies and response parsing are exercised. No test runs against a live vLLM/SGLang/GLM server. The pickle round trip is tested for `GradedRolloutInterrupted` only, and `RolloutInterrupted.__reduce__` is untested.

**Findings**

- **1. Should fix:** `lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/harness/external.py:64` The `not agent.cancelling()` clause doesn't separate the caller's cancel from a stray one. A caller or deadline cancel interrupts `asyncio.wait` in `run` and never reaches this check. `stop()`, the only engine code that cancels the agent, runs later during cleanup. So `cancelling() > 0` here means the agent's own code cancelled its task, for example `asyncio.current_task().cancel()` followed by an await. That case still raises `CancelledError` out of `run_task`, which is the failure this PR describes fixing. I reproduced it on this head: the agent from the new `test_an_unrequested_cancellation_…` test with `asyncio.current_task().cancel(); await asyncio.sleep(1)` in place of the child task makes `run_task` raise `asyncio.CancelledError`. Use `if agent.cancelled():`, drop "A requested cancel stays a cancellation" from the comment and from `docs/references/task-rollouts.md`, and add the self-cancel case to the new test.

- **2. Should fix:** `lib/rolloutengine/pyproject.toml:17` The `chat` extra installs nothing. `marin-rolloutengine` already depends on `marin-taskcompendium`, which depends on `marin-verifyit[judge]`, which pins `openai>=1.59.9`, and `taskcompendium/grading.py` imports `openai` at module top level. So `openai` is always installed, and `[chat]`, the test-group entry, the `provides-extras` lock change, and the docs' "(extra `marin-rolloutengine[chat]`)" are surface with no effect. Since `chat.py` imports `openai` itself, declare `"openai>=1.59.9"` in `[project].dependencies`, then delete the extra, the test-group line, and the docs parenthetical.

<!-- marin-holistic-review:f0934cd1f0b57dafec26a2e6d087eac9002a608a -->

🤖 The two findings are correct. Both are fixed at 90f554c94:

1. d2cc06f8f: an agent that ends cancelled before the cleanup fails its attempt (`if agent.cancelled():`). The test has a `self` case for an agent that cancels its own task, and the docs and the comment no longer say that a requested cancel stays a cancellation. `test_an_agent_cancelled_by_another_task_propagates_its_cancellation` from #10203 asserted the reverse contract. A cancel from another task takes the same path as the `self` case, so I deleted that test.
2. 90f554c94: `openai>=1.59.9` is a direct dependency. The `chat` extra, its test-group line, its `uv.lock` entries, and the docs parenthetical are gone.

🤖 Shortened the pickle serialization comment. The author’s new head addresses the two holistic findings.

topics.title: Hero Run: Sudden drop in PTB Paloma Eval
topics.body: Issue to track the investigation into the sudden drop in PTB Paloma Eval PTB is in general OOD data due to token, 'N' token, and all lowercase. Among other quirks. Initial hypothesises: 1. Some in-context learning capacity turned on for a checkpoint. 2. Data contam/very similar article in training data around then. 3. Some very rare tokens in PTB happened to get upweighted on a checkpoint that under normal checkpoints are heavily penalized. 4. Other/Unk Artifact comparing first 4k tokens: https://claude.ai/artifact/W82uDiQuQygwAaqfX3hEiR Most noteworthy drop is: "los angeles financier marvin" " mar" for marvin is predicted with 80% confidence on the overperforming checkpoint- seems likely that the exact phrase los angeles financier marvin appeared in the training data. It then dropped back down to its usual 0.2% on the following checkpoint. Completions API with prompt for every checkpoint: https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/rav/hero-completions/latest/index.html#a=1ed4a3edd3645961c051e72c8b85a9ec7b6fbea0f2c5b3a27960cc1c806b237d&b=dde26b9fe079446f0c76ecc1b7f469d59815aca5f3f3c84f50a3993df7a26978&prompt=biocorpus-protein-design-heldout

comments.body: 'mar' was at 15% on checkpoint 198k. And the model always knows mar ->vin ->d ->avis. So the person marvin davis is cleanly in the training data for a while. Google search-> "Marvin Davis was a prominent Beverly Hills billionaire, oil tycoon, and corporate buyout artist who made massive waves as Wall Street's highest-paid financier in 1989." Any docs related to news ongoings in Los Angeles may be spiking the eval.

PTB is '1989 Wall Street Journal (WSJ) articles'. We want our model to understand what happened in the 1980s in general.. so having the facts of this eval in the training data is intentional. Will see what comes up from scanning our data in this 6k step range.

🤖 **Data scan result: PTB's own text was in the training stream ~500 steps before the 210k checkpoint (hypothesis 2, contamination).**

**Method.** I rebuilt the hero's exact training stream from the run's logged data config: launch commit `ad754c6d67`, seed 0, the 0 / 108,000 / 312,192 mix stages, and the block shuffle. Then I read every sequence trained in steps **204,000–216,000**: 12,000 steps × 11,264 sequences × 4,096 tokens, about 554B tokens over 48 CPU jobs on cw-us-east-02a. The scan searched for PTB-specific lowercase phrases, their normal-cased counterparts, and runs of ` <unk>`.

**Result.** A block of about **231 sequences (~1M tokens)** in source **`c13q3`** at **steps 209,272–209,669** contains Penn Treebank text expanded into sliding n-gram windows (`<s> <s> … <word>` per line). It reads like an NLP exercise repository: it also has NMT training notes and scraped request headers. It includes the exact sentences in our PTB eval, e.g. `los angeles financier marvin`, `in london british airways chairman lord king`, `the stock of ual corp. continued`, `the dow industrials were off N points`. A related source, `c28q1`, has n-gram log-probability tables over the same text around step 206.3k (`lg P(corp. | acquire ual)`).

| Lowercase PTB-format hits | steps 204k–210k | steps 210k–216k |
|---|---|---|
| `los angeles financier` | 3 | 0 |
| `british airways chairman` | 3 | 0 |
| `ual corp` | 26 | 0 |

Normal-cased news about the same entities appears about equally in both ranges:

| Normal-cased hits | steps 204k–210k | steps 210k–216k |
|---|---|---|
| `Marvin Davis` | 331 | 332 |
| `UAL Corp` | 226 | 230 |
| `British Airways chairman` | 25 | 27 |

So general knowledge of the 1989 story is steady. What changed before 210k is exposure to the PTB text itself, which the checkpoint partly retained and which had faded by 216k. "Lord King" alone produced thousands of false positives ("Sovereign Lord King James…"), so those hits are excluded.

**300-character chunks: PTB eval text vs. the training document**

PTB (Paloma `ptb` val):
```
this is a total <unk> for takeover-stock traders one investment banker said 
 los angeles financier marvin davis who put united in play with a $ N billion bid two months ago last night <unk> both a ray of hope and an extra element of uncertainty by saying he remains interested in acquiring ual 
 but
```
Training stream (`c13q3`, step 209,550):
```
 traders one investment
for takeover-stock traders one investment banker
takeover-stock traders one investment banker said
<s> <s> <s> <s> <s> los
<s> <s> <s> <s> los angeles
<s> <s> <s> los angeles financier
<s> <s> los angeles financier marvin
<s> los angeles financier <NAME>
los angeles financier
```

PTB:
```
in london british airways chairman lord king was quoted in the times as declaring he is not prepared to take my shareholders into a <unk> deal 
 observers said it appeared that british air was angered at the way the bid has <unk> into confusion as well as by the banks ' effort to round up financing 
```
Training stream (`c13q3`, step 209,665):
```
<s> <s> <s> <s> in london
<s> <s> <s> in london british
<s> <s> in london british airways
<s> in london british airways chairman
in london british airways chairman lord
london british airways chairman lord king
british airways chairman lord king was
airways chairman lord king was quoted
chairman lor
```

The training copy has "marvin davis" replaced with `<NAME>` in most windows, presumably by PII scrubbing. One window, `los angeles financier marvin`, kept the first name because the scrubber only caught "marvin davis" as a pair. That is the token the 210k checkpoint predicted at 0.80. It also explains why every checkpoint already completes `marvin → davis`: that part is general knowledge, not this document.

**Takeaways**
- The 210k drop in PTB loss (about −0.2 nats, spread across almost every line) comes from verbatim exposure to the eval text in an n-gram layout roughly 330–730 steps earlier. It is not a capability change. 210k still misses PTB's genuinely surprising words ("declaring", "my"), which fits brief, partial exposure.
- Paloma PTB is contaminated in the hero mix, at least in `c13q3` and `c28q1`. Its curve will spike whenever those windows come up in the data order, so it shouldn't be read as a quality signal. Wikitext-103 and the other public eval sets may warrant the same scan.

Raw hits: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/larry/scratch/hero_scan/full/*.jsonl`. Scanner: `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/ops/scan_training_data.py` on local branch `hero-data-scan`, not pushed.

🤖 **The contaminated document, and every step that reads it**

**What it is.** One GitHub repository dump in source `c13q3`, **`quanpn90/torch-nplm`**: a Torch implementation of Bengio et al. (2003), with the name scrubbed to `<NAME>` in the README. It is **1,385,899 tokens** (4.83M characters), a single BOS…EOS document that spans 340 training sequences of 4,096 tokens.

| File | Characters |
|---|---|
| README.md | 260 |
| extract_ngrams.py | 2,308 |
| train.lua | 12,261 |
| **data/ptb/test.6grams** | **2,543,118** |
| **data/ptb/valid.6grams** | **2,262,165** |
| util/BatchLoader.lua | 4,901 |
| util/IdentityLinear.lua | 985 |

About 99.6% of the document is the **full PTB test and validation sets as sliding 6-gram windows**. `valid.6grams` starts `<s> <s> <s> <s> <s> consumers / … / consumers may want to move their / may want to move their telephones …`, which is exactly the start of Paloma's `ptb` eval document. So the whole Paloma PTB eval set is in the training data, with each word appearing in 6 overlapping windows.

First 500 characters:
```
Repository: quanpn90/torch-nplm

File: README.md
# torch-nplm

Neural probabilistic language model (<NAME>, 2003) implemented in Torch.

GPU supported for fast training.

Hierarchical supported for fast softmax-ing on a large vocabulary. 

HSM borrowed from https://github.com/yoonkim/lstm-char-cnn


File: extract_ngrams.py
#!/usr/bin/python
import sys

# This script extracts n-grams from a set of PREPROCESSED text files (train, set, valid)

data_dir = sys.argv[1]
ngram_order = int(sys.argv[2])

tra
```

**Every step that reads it over the full 390,251-step schedule.** I inverted the mixture and block shuffle using the run's logged data config: launch commit `ad754c6d67`, seed 0, the 0 / 108,000 / 312,192 stages, and `c13q3` at 69.8M sequences per epoch. The document straddles two 256-sequence shuffle blocks, which land in different shuffle windows, so each epoch reads it in two bursts:

| Epoch | Document part | Sequences | Steps |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | code + first ~60% of `test.6grams` | 112 | **176,080–176,355** |
| 0 | rest of `test.6grams` + **all of `valid.6grams` (Paloma PTB)** | 228 | **209,390–209,669** |
| 1 | code + first ~60% of `test.6grams` | 112 | 327,205–327,493 *(future)* |
| 1 | rest of `test.6grams` + **all of `valid.6grams`** | 228 | **362,280–362,578** *(future)* |

**Implications**
- The 210k checkpoint was saved about 330–610 steps after the hero trained on the entire Paloma PTB eval set. That explains the drop, and its fading by 216k.
- **The PTB eval should drop again right after step ~362.3k**, when epoch 1 reaches the same block; that's in the cooldown stage. It's a useful sanity check that this explanation is right. The ~176k and ~327k bursts carry only PTB test-split text, not the Paloma eval text.
- Other copies of PTB in the mix, for example the n-gram probability tables in `c28q1` around step 206.3k, aren't covered by this mapping. A dedup or decontamination pass against Paloma would find them.

Files: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/users/larry/scratch/hero_scan/docs/` holds the full document text (`doc_209550_4116.txt`), `summary.json`, and `torch_nplm_steps.json`, which maps every read to its step and row. Scripts: `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/ops/{scan_training_data,find_training_doc,find_doc_steps}.py` on local branch `hero-data-scan`.
Its https://github.com/quanpn90/torch-nplm/, specifically https://github.com/quanpn90/torch-nplm/blob/master/data/ptb/valid.6grams. The sort of doc that could induce very weird repetition behavior.

@ClassicLarry, I went through the public W&B evals: all 16 Paloma and 7 Uncheatable subsets, every eval from step 2,999 to 227,999. I also ran the decon matcher on the torch-nplm files. Here are four results that may help the scan. **1. PTB has drops the torch-nplm reads don't explain** | Evals | PTB loss | Note | |---|---|---| | 101,999 → **104,999** → 107,999 | 2.143 → **1.961** → 2.109 | A one-eval drop with no mapped read nearby | | 188,999 → **191,999** | 2.115 → **2.015** | Drops 0.10 and stays below 2.08 through 227,999 | | 173,999 → **176,999** → 179,999 | 2.141 → **2.099** → 2.114 | Just after the 176,080–176,355 read, which has only the PTB *test* split | | 203,999 → **206,999** → 209,999 | 2.079 → **1.903** → 1.712 | The first half comes before the 209,390 read; it fits the `c28q1` tables at ~206.3k | The 176,999 row is a natural control. That read had PTB test text but none of the eval sentences. It moved the eval 0.029 below the average of its two neighbours, while the curve otherwise stays between 2.113 and 2.141 from 155,999 to 188,999. By the same measure, 104,999 is 0.165 below its neighbours, close to 209,999's 0.187. So I'd guess another copy of the validation text was read in steps **102,000–104,999**. If your scanner can run on that range, and on **189,000–191,999**, that would test it. **2. WikiText-103 shows the same pattern; general Wikipedia doesn't** At steps 125,999 / 128,999 / 131,999 / 134,999, `wikitext_103` reads 1.707 / **1.558** / 1.638 / 1.684. Over the same evals, `m2d2_wikipedia_unsplit` reads 1.828 / 1.827 / 1.823 / 1.824. Smaller one-sided drops recur at 137,999, 152,999, 203,999 and 212,999–215,999. None of them shows up in m2d2_wikipedia. A 0.15 drop on the WikiText eval with flat general Wikipedia looks like a document containing the eval text itself, not a Wikipedia-heavy stretch. Candidate windows: - **126,000–128,999**; - **210,000–212,999**, which your 204k–216k scan already covers. Re-running it with a few WikiText eval sentences may be the cheapest first check. **3. Decon would have missed torch-nplm even with Paloma indexed** Paloma isn't in the decon eval corpus, and `wikitext` is excluded on purpose (`DECON_EXCLUDED_EVAL_TASKS`, #6852 cluster A). I indexed the PTB validation text (Paloma's `ptb`) anyway to test the matcher. I ran the matching functions in `lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/decon.py` unchanged, using the `reference_pipeline.py` settings: 13-grams, overlap ≥ 0.5, ≥ 2 matched features, paragraphs split on `\n\n`. The repo was rendered the way `stack_v3.row_to_doc` renders it. | Training document | Max overlap | Flagged | |---|---|---| | torch-nplm as trained (6-gram windows) | 0.000 | no | | the same repo plus the raw `data/ptb/valid.txt` | 1.000 | yes | | the validation set as windows of any width from 3 to 30 | ≤ 0.14 | no | A small pre-pass recovers it. When most lines of a paragraph are windows that shift by one token, stitch them back into running text, drop ``, and score the result as an extra paragraph. Overlap goes back to 1.000. In 5,724 ordinary code and text files (the Marin repo and the CPython 3.12 standard library), the pass triggered on none of 241,449 paragraphs. Details are on #6852, the issue about this matcher's recall. So one store-wide pass may be cheaper than scanning step ranges. Run decon in flag-only mode against Paloma `ptb` and `wikitext_103`, with the stitching pass, and then run `find_doc_steps.py` on what it flags. Raw copies would score about 1.0. **4. For alerts and for comparisons with the pre-registered prediction** After the 108k mix swap, PTB accounts for 50–68% of the variance in the Paloma macro's eval-to-eval movement, and WikiText-103 for 19–27%. The ranges cover three detrending methods; the block-bootstrap 95% CI for PTB is 0.33–0.85. Dropping both subsets cuts the macro's noise SD to 43–61% of its current value. The 7 Uncheatable subsets show no drops at any threshold I tried, which fits #9729. For the Paloma chart and the #8435 comparison, a 14-subset macro without `ptb` and `wikitext_103`, shown next to the official one, would keep these exposures out of the trend. Scripts and outputs: [eval-audit/](https://github.com/bethehand/marin-hero-forecast/tree/main/eval-audit). Everything uses the public W&B project and public GitHub files.

A follow-up on the store-wide pass from (3). I ran a narrower check: a 13-gram scan of the public Stack v3, the source of the torch-nplm document, limited to files whose path or size looks like PTB or WikiText data. Apart from torch-nplm, none of them holds either validation text. So the other drops, at 104,999 and 191,999 for PTB and the WikiText ones, still need your scanner or a store-wide pass.

**Scope**
- All 8,192 parquet files of `HuggingFaceCode/stack-v3-train`, 172.8M repos.
- The parquet files at your pinned `bb2fa950` (`stack_v3.py`) now return 403; HF squashed the dataset history on 2026-09-25. I used the current `1f61b735` (v3.1). It differs from v3.0 by opted-out repos and by the duplicated file entries that `deduplicate_files` already drops (#7788).
- 529 files passed the path/size filter. Each was scored by 13-gram overlap with PTB and WikiText-103 valid/test, as written and de-windowed.

| Eval text | Best file in Stack v3 | Share of the eval's 13-grams |
|---|---|---|
| PTB valid (Paloma `ptb` val) | `quanpn90/torch-nplm` `data/ptb/valid.6grams` | 0.988, de-windowed |
| PTB test | `quanpn90/torch-nplm` `data/ptb/test.6grams` | 0.987, de-windowed |
| WikiText-103 valid (Paloma `wikitext_103` val) | `DavidFanzz/llm_decoding` `data/wikitext/test.jsonl` | 0.024, as written |
| WikiText-103 test (raw) | `shaochenze/PatchTrain` `wikitext_document_level-test.json` | 0.699, as written (JSON-escaped) |

- **PTB.** torch-nplm is the only copy the scan found. None of the standard `ptb.*.txt` files is in stack-v3-train, and no selected file outside torch-nplm shares a single 13-gram with the validation text, as written or de-windowed. So the other copy I guessed at in (1) isn't in a Stack v3 file that looks like PTB data.
- **WikiText validation.** No selected file holds more than 2.4% of it. I also checked that Paloma's `wikitext_103` val is the WikiText-103 validation split: it contains 98% of validation's 13-grams and none of test's.
- **WikiText test.** The PatchTrain file is the full test set, all 62 articles, stored as JSON lines: the GitHub original decodes to it, identical up to whitespace, and the Stack v3 copy is 0.9% shorter, which fits the dataset's PII redaction (names become `<NAME>`). It doesn't touch Paloma, but it is the test set of lm-eval's `wikitext` task, since WikiText-2 raw test is the same text. `wikitext` is in `DECON_EXCLUDED_EVAL_TASKS` because "every web/book corpus overlaps it" (#6852 cluster A). Here, though, a code repo carries nearly the whole test set, so if the hero read this repo (`find_doc_steps.py` would show), its lm-eval `wikitext` score would be contaminated.
- **Limits.** The filter misses copies under unrelated names, PTB/WikiText-named files under 50 KB, and copies inside code or markup files (`.py`, `.md`, `.html`, …). The scoring only recognizes running text and shift-by-one windows, so it would also miss tables like the `c28q1` n-gram ones. Repos that opted out before v3.1 can't be checked. A flag-only decon pass over the whole store, with the stitching pass from (3), would close the name, size and opt-out gaps. It wouldn't catch tables, and it has low recall on copies embedded in code (#6852).

**New since my first comment.** The drops continue on `hero-mfu30-step231k`, and the latest one reaches a new low:
- `wikitext_103` fell from 1.584 at 230,999 to 1.491 at 233,999, held at 1.500, and fell to 1.301 at 239,999. Over the next four evals it rose to 1.427–1.455, still below its 1.52–1.59 range from 212,999 to 230,999. At 254,999 it fell again, by 0.168 in one eval, to 1.271, its lowest so far. Over the same evals `m2d2_wikipedia_unsplit` fell steadily from 1.732 to 1.705.
- PTB, from 230,999 to 254,999: 1.957 → 2.003 → 1.882 → 2.017 → 1.877 → 1.942 → 1.996 → 2.030 → 2.029. It dipped at 236,999 and 242,999, by 0.12 and 0.14 from the eval before, and then rose.
- Together, `wikitext_103` and PTB account for about 65% of the Paloma macro's drop from 2.140 at 230,999 to 2.118 at 242,999; the other 14 subsets fell 0.009 on average. As PTB rose, the macro rose back to 2.126 at 248,999. At 254,999 it fell 0.012 in one eval, to 2.111, and 88% of that came from `wikitext_103`: the other 14 subsets fell 0.0016 on average, and the Uncheatable macro moved from 1.583 to 1.582.

Neither the torch-nplm reads nor the Stack v3 pass explains these drops, so they give new windows for your scanner: 231,000–233,999, 237,000–239,999 and 252,000–254,999 for WikiText, and 234,000–236,999 and 240,000–242,999 for PTB, whose dips sit 0.13 and 0.10 below the average of their two neighbours (the 176,999 control in (1) was 0.029).

From 257,999 the evals pack at 16K (#10101), so their values can't be compared with those above. Between the first two 16K evals, `wikitext_103` rose from 1.372 to 1.419 while `m2d2_wikipedia_unsplit` stayed at 1.672. That fits the 254,999 drop fading.

topics.title: [eval] Add graders for agent protocol probes
topics.body:
Add four structural probes for agent behavior: required-file submission,
actual tool execution, disabled thinking, and URL loading. Each grader
reads a versioned evidence bundle with the request settings, raw response,
parsed tool calls, executor events, URL accesses, and files read from the
task environment. It never reads the model's own account of what it did,
so a narrated shell session, tool-call markup in plain text, or an answer
left in chat fails.

Each result reports protocol compliance, submission completeness, and
answer correctness separately. EvalSample.correct carries only answer
correctness. A serving or extraction error, an unsupported setting, or
evidence the harness did not capture marks the trial not evaluable instead
of charging the model. Archiving stores the evidence bundle beside the
sample and links it from the grading detail.

Running these probes through Harbor and the served endpoint remains open.
Current ATIF trajectories record no executor lifecycle or pre-parser text,
so that capture must be added first.

Part of #10393

topics.title: [levanter] LM evaluation fails with explicitly context-sharded tokens
topics.body:
Held-out LM evaluation fails when token positions are explicitly sharded across a context mesh. Training updates succeed; the first evaluation raises:

```text
lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval.py:238, _default_lm_eval_loss_fn
per_pos_token_id = jnp.roll(named_batch.tokens.array, -1, axis=-1)
ShardingTypeError: `a` cannot be sharded on the axis being rolled over.
Got arr type=i32[16@(replica_dcn,data,expert),32768@context] and axis=(1,)
```

Reproduce:
1. Use an explicit mesh with local axes `data=1, replica=1, model=1, expert=8` and inter-node axes `replica_dcn=1, context=4` (32 GPUs).
2. Map `batch` to `(replica_dcn,data,expert)` and `position` to `context`, with global batch 16 and sequence length 32,768.
3. Run `cb_tagged_lm_evaluate` on a model and batch with that layout. Its default loss callback reaches the failing roll.

Expected: target-token shifting and token-weighted evaluation agree with an unsharded reference. The training loss path in `models/loss.py` already gathers the token IDs along the sharded position axis before shifting and restores their layout afterward.

Observed in the #10213 sweep at completed update 548, its first held-out evaluation, on base commit `753bbb163c78f0e7ea50059522f42156708162c8` plus experiment-local changes. Iris job: `/karan/task203-lr1e6-20261017-r3/snowball-v0-pilot-sft`. Retrieve the error with `uv run iris --cluster=marin task logs /karan/task203-lr1e6-20261017-r3/snowball-v0-pilot-sft/1 --substring ShardingTypeError`.

The labeled callback contains the same roll at `eval.py:277`; that path was not exercised in this run. This issue tracks the shared evaluator fix separately from moving the sweep's validation offline.

comments.body:
🤖 # Research

Both default LM evaluation callbacks call `jnp.roll` on token arrays whose position axis may be explicitly sharded. JAX rejects that roll before the evaluator can aggregate loss or byte counts. The evaluator already receives the mesh mapping needed to restore the token layout after shifting.

**Relevant code**
- [`eval.py#L223-L237`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval.py#L223-L237) — tagged callback token shift
- [`eval.py#L259-L276`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval.py#L259-L276) — labeled callback token shift
- [`eval.py#L531-L577`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/eval.py#L531-L577) — token IDs feed byte aggregation

# Proposed Fix

`TaggedEvaluator.accum_for_batch()` or `LabeledEvaluator.accum_for_batch()` → default loss callback → `jnp.roll` on context-sharded positions → `ShardingTypeError`. Replicate the position axis for the shift, then restore its mapped sharding in both default callbacks; verify token IDs and token-weighted metrics against an unsharded reference on a small context mesh.

🤖 Fix is open in #10233. Both default callbacks use the training loss's sharding-safe token shift, and byte lookup keeps an explicit output layout for context shards. Two-device CPU regressions match unsharded tagged loss and bits-per-byte metrics and labeled next-token IDs; the focused evaluator and loss suite passed 23 tests. The full Levanter run hit an unrelated Grug MoE test that uses `ragged-all-to-all`, which XLA:CPU does not support; all-files Pyrefly reported missing optional imports outside the changed files.
🤖 PR #10233 passed CI, including the Levanter unit and repository lint jobs. It remains open and mergeable, with review required and no submitted reviews after the 12-hour monitor timeout.

topics.title: [rl-data] Nemotron RLVR1 IF dataset rewards all-caps and letterless answers
topics.body:
> Context: 
> I've been running some IF training experiments on my own and noticed that that Nemotron RLVR1 blend checker has issues and the model is prone to reward hacking such as producing non-sense answers or language switching to circumvent constraints. Since the same dataset was used in Snowball RL training, I'm reporting the issue here to raise awareness about IF training set quality issues. 


_Some instruction-following (IF) rows in the Nemotron RLVR1 blend reward answers that ignore the request (all caps, Title Case, no Latin letters, or a non-Latin script), score at random, or cannot be passed._ 

[Cleaned-v3](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Nemotron-RL-Ultra-RLVR1-Cleaned-v3-2026-09-30) has 1,142 such rows among its 11,817 IF rows. Cleaned-v3 is the training set of the Antidoom RLVR1 v2 run, which produced Antidoom RLVR1 Step12, and of its Reference-KL continuation, which produced Reference-KL Step20 (#9735). The PivotRL mixed-RLVR arms (#10214) also train with its IF rows in the mix (#10215). Snowball v0.1 (Smartie run `.32`, #10305) trained on no IF constraint rows, but it started from the Campaign 2 merge, whose parents include Antidoom Step12 and Reference-KL Step20 (#9975).

| Constraint | Rows | Prompt text | NVIDIA checker |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `count:lowercase_counting` | 869 | "all lowercase words should appear at most N times", N = 2 or 3 | Allows at most N lowercase words in the whole answer, so only all-caps, Title Case or non-Latin answers pass ([instructions.py:2348](https://github.com/abukharin-nv/verifiable-instructions/blob/f46a5ac87b1400a4f8973039844b6be9b56e3faf/verifiable_instructions/instructions.py#L2348)) |
| `letters:letter_counting` with `relation: "less than"` | 203 | "Answer with less than N letters", N = 2 or 3 | Passes only answers with fewer than N Latin letters, such as `42` ([instructions.py:2355](https://github.com/abukharin-nv/verifiable-instructions/blob/f46a5ac87b1400a4f8973039844b6be9b56e3faf/verifiable_instructions/instructions.py#L2355)) |
| `length_constraints:nth_paragraph_first_word` with `nth_paragraph = num_paragraphs + 1` | 77 | "There should be 3 paragraphs. ... Paragraph 4 must start with word feedback." | Replaces the out-of-range `nth_paragraph` with `randint(1, num_paragraphs + 1)` on every call, so the paragraph it checks is random ([instructions.py:929](https://github.com/abukharin-nv/verifiable-instructions/blob/f46a5ac87b1400a4f8973039844b6be9b56e3faf/verifiable_instructions/instructions.py#L929)) |
| `count:counting_composition` | 1 | "delimited by the markdown divider: * * *" | Splits paragraphs only on `***`, so an answer that uses the prompt's `* * *` divider fails ([instructions.py:2440](https://github.com/abukharin-nv/verifiable-instructions/blob/f46a5ac87b1400a4f8973039844b6be9b56e3faf/verifiable_instructions/instructions.py#L2440)) |

Eight rows carry two of these constraints.

Antidoom RLVR1 v2 and Reference-KL graded IF rows with MarinSkyRL's [`grade_instruction_following`](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/53bb00e83910a7dbd3f21efcb1c9384231b0fca3/skyrl-gym/skyrl_gym/envs/nemotron_ultra/instruction_following.py#L61-L84). It runs NVIDIA's pinned `verifiable_instructions@f46a5ac` checks and returns 1.0 only when every constraint passes. Its paragraph patch ([L54-L57](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/53bb00e83910a7dbd3f21efcb1c9384231b0fca3/skyrl-gym/skyrl_gym/envs/nemotron_ultra/instruction_following.py#L54-L57)) applies only when `nth_paragraph` is missing, and the 77 rows set it. MarinSkyRL's opt-in verifyit path rejects those 77 rows at preparation ([instruction_verifyit.py:242](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/3a8e8a72681011012ebb59c0c1ed34688ad6fdea/skyrl-gym/skyrl_gym/envs/instruction_verifyit.py#L242)). It is off by default ([env.py:80](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/53bb00e83910a7dbd3f21efcb1c9384231b0fca3/skyrl-gym/skyrl_gym/envs/nemotron_ultra/env.py#L80)), and I found no setting that enables it in the Antidoom RLVR1 v2 run notes or the Reference-KL config. The reward does not check that the answer addresses the request. It also does not check the answer's language, so a non-Latin answer passes `lowercase_counting` on an English prompt. 3,166 of the 11,817 IF prompts (26.8%) contain CJK characters.

The task-curation grader on main (#10077) checks these constraints with verifyit, then asks a GLM-5.3 judge whether the answer addresses the request ([graders.py:316-378](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5ec80e71242485b353b1f4556d3d68eb0a4dddf5/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/nemotron_ultra/graders.py#L316-L378)). verifyit's `count:lowercase_counting` passes answers with at least N lowercase words ([ifeval.py:547-552](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5ec80e71242485b353b1f4556d3d68eb0a4dddf5/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/ifeval.py#L547-L552)), which inverts the prompt. Its `nth_paragraph_first_word` check fails every answer to the 77 off-by-one rows ([ifeval.py:143-155](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5ec80e71242485b353b1f4556d3d68eb0a4dddf5/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/ifeval.py#L143-L155)), so a run trained on this grader gives every sample on those rows reward 0. The GLM-5.3 judge scores the 203 `letter_counting` rows instead of a letter count.

11,688 of the 11,817 Cleaned-v3 IF rows appear verbatim in [`nvidia/Nemotron-Cascade-2-RL-data`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-Cascade-2-RL-data) `IF-RL/train.jsonl`. 

**Our observations:** 
In a GRPO run of Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 on that file, scored with open-instruct's IFEvalG checkers (whose `lowercase_counting` rule matches NVIDIA's), the `lowercase_counting` pass rate rose from 0.21 at step 0 to 0.96 at step 199. From step 79 on, 85–93% of those passes were mostly CJK (more than 20% CJK characters). Mostly-Chinese answers to English IFEval prompts went from 0% at step 0 to 34.5% at step 199, and `lowercase_counting` is one of the constraints that paid for them. I have not re-scored Snowball's logged IF rollouts, so I do not know whether its runs took these shortcuts. 

In our later runs, we excluded these rows and added two checks to the reward. A language check scores an answer 0 when more than 20% of its characters are CJK and the prompt has no CJK characters and no language:response_language constraint. With it, mostly-CJK answers that would otherwise have passed never exceeded 0.42% of all answers. We then required a Qwen3-32B judge to confirm that each constraint pass attempts the request before it scores 1, the same role as the GLM-5.3 judge in the task-curation grader. 

Reproduce:

1. Download `data/train.parquet` from Cleaned-v3 and count the affected rows:

   ```python
   import collections, json
   import pyarrow.parquet as pq

   info = pq.read_table("train.parquet", columns=["extra_info"]).column("extra_info").to_pylist()
   rows = [json.loads(i["nemotron_ultra"]["record_json"]) for i in info
           if i["nemotron_ultra"]["agent"] == "instruction_following_simple_agent"]


   def shortcuts(row):
       found = set()
       for name, kw in zip(row["instruction_id_list"], row["kwargs"]):
           kw = kw or {}
           if name == "length_constraints:nth_paragraph_first_word" and (kw.get("nth_paragraph") or 0) > kw["num_paragraphs"]:
               found.add("nth_paragraph_first_word off by one")
           elif name == "letters:letter_counting" and kw.get("relation") == "less than":
               found.add("letter_counting less than")
           elif name in ("count:lowercase_counting", "count:counting_composition"):
               found.add(name)
       return found


   flagged = [shortcuts(r) for r in rows]
   print(len(rows), sum(map(bool, flagged)), collections.Counter(c for f in flagged for c in f))
   # 11817 1142 Counter({'count:lowercase_counting': 869, 'letter_counting less than': 203,
   #   'nth_paragraph_first_word off by one': 77, 'count:counting_composition': 1})
   ```

2. Run NVIDIA's checks, after `pip install "verifiable-instructions @ git+https://github.com/abukharin-nv/verifiable-instructions.git@f46a5ac87b1400a4f8973039844b6be9b56e3faf"`:

   ```python
   from verifiable_instructions import instructions_registry


   def build(name, **kwargs):
       checker = instructions_registry.INSTRUCTION_DICT[name](name)
       return checker, checker.build_description(**kwargs)


   lower, _ = build("count:lowercase_counting", N=3)
   lower.check_following("THE INTEGRAL IS FOUND BY SUBSTITUTION.")  # True
   lower.check_following("The integral is found by substitution.")  # False
   letters, _ = build("letters:letter_counting", N=2, relation="less than")
   letters.check_following("42")  # True
   for _ in range(4):  # the paragraph number in the description changes between builds
       print(build("length_constraints:nth_paragraph_first_word", num_paragraphs=3, nth_paragraph=4, first_word="feedback")[1])
   ```

3. Run verifyit's check:

   ```python
   from verifyit.modes.ifeval import CONSTRAINTS

   check = CONSTRAINTS["count:lowercase_counting"]
   check("The integral is found by substitution.", {"N": 3})  # (True, 'lower_words=5 need>=3')
   check("THE INTEGRAL IS FOUND BY SUBSTITUTION.", {"N": 3})  # (False, 'lower_words=0 need>=3')
   ```

Expected: no IF training row rewards all-caps, letterless or random answers, and verifyit's `count:lowercase_counting` implements its prompt text. If verifyit's check is changed to match the prompt, it will reward all-caps answers on the 869 `lowercase_counting` rows as NVIDIA's checker does, so those rows also need to be excluded or rewritten.

topics.title: [taskforge] Turn failed rollouts into capability ideas
topics.body:
Doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1DXtl3bOsGvhb1usA3cfZ6-G1TDyObf_G0g-TRVq4DtA

Turn policy failures into capability ideas that `task_workpieces` and `generate_tasks` can use to create training tasks. `analyze_failed_runs(rollouts, make_client, *, pass_threshold, max_new_ideas, shard_size, extract_ideas_llm_policy, merge_ideas_llm_policy, catalog_version, min_tasks_per_idea=2, max_ideas_per_merge=1000)` takes `(TaskSpec, GradedRollout)` pairs and returns the plan of one Zephyr map-reduce pipeline, as the doc proposes. The source is the rollouts in shards of `shard_size`. `filter` keeps the policy failures, `flat_map(yield_ideas)` makes one structured call for each failed rollout, `reduce(merge_ideas, merge_idea_lists)` merges each shard and then the lists of the shards, with one structured call for at most `max_ideas_per_merge` ideas, and `flat_map(to_ideas)` makes the `CapabilityIdea` values, the ideas with more rollouts first.

Each capability is a general skill that transfers to many tasks and domains, such as the answer format, tool use, a stop to loops of repeated calls, or a careful reading of the task. It holds the catalog fields `name`, `outcome`, `includes`, and `excludes`, and it does not describe the failed tasks, so `generate_tasks` writes the details of the training tasks. A rollout that stopped at its turn limit counts as a gap only if it used its turns on repeated or unneeded steps, because the policy does not see the limit.

`policy_failed` is true for a grade below `pass_threshold`, an invalid submission, or an attempt that ran past its deadline or whose harness failed after a model turn, because a slow or looping policy or a bad tool call can cause those. It is false for task, grader, and infrastructure failures and for interruptions by the model server or the machine, so those do not become training targets. The rollout's first line names the operation that interrupted it. The call for a rollout gives up to three ideas, or none if the rollout shows no gap. It sees a summary line, the tools that the task gave, and the messages, with no grader or its answer. The task comes with each rollout because the record does not keep the tools. A rollout whose reply stays invalid gives no ideas and adds 1 to the pipeline counter `failed_runs.invalid_replies`.

A `MaybeIdea` keeps its evidence as a set of run IDs, and the IDs of their tasks. A merge call sees each idea with its number of rollouts and gives the line IDs that each merged idea holds, and code takes the union of their evidence, so a rollout counts once. The reply must name only its lines and give each merged idea a different ID, and the structured call sends an invalid reply back with the error. A reply can leave out the lines of rare skills, as the prompt keeps the ideas that explain the most rollouts, and the pipeline counter `failed_runs.dropped_rollouts` adds the rollouts that the merged ideas no longer cite. A rule that put each line in exactly one merged idea failed 2 of 3 merges of the 797 tau-bench failures and made larger catch-all ideas, and the merge that can leave out lines lost the evidence of at most 2.2% of the rollouts. The same merge serves the two levels, and one group needs no second merge. The merge reply lists the line IDs of each merged idea, and GLM sometimes runs away to the output limit in a long structured reply, so a merge makes up to three calls. A merged idea cannot repeat its line IDs as its `includes`, because GLM wrote the IDs there for every capability in 6 of 27 merges. A final idea must cite failed rollouts of at least `min_tasks_per_idea` tasks, or of every failed task when there are fewer, so that one defective grader on a task with many samples cannot make an idea by itself. The merges rank such ideas last, so that they do not take the place of an idea that cites enough tasks. A merge call sees at most `max_ideas_per_merge` ideas, about 66 prompt tokens each, and more ideas merge in rounds, so neither a large shard nor many shards can make a merge prompt too long. The calls of one shard run one after another on one worker, and the shards run in parallel. Zephyr calls the functions on its workers, outside an event loop, so each call makes its own client with `make_client`, for example `functools.partial(GlmClient, source, GLM_PROVIDER)`.

This design replaces a managed agent that read the failed rollouts as files on a ShellSim machine. Both designs ran with GLM-5.3 at low reasoning effort on real failed rollouts: tau-bench trajectories of GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet (72, 144, and all 797 failures) and 120 SWE-agent rollouts on GitHub issues. The agent's evidence named 16%, 6%, and 1% of the tau-bench failures and 8% of the SWE failures. Per-rollout calls read every rollout. They beat the agent in every direct comparison on these sets, with a GLM judge, and with a Claude judge on all sets except the 797 failures. They also found all the failure categories of a reference taxonomy. The merged capabilities are broader than the agent's: a blind judge rated their focus about 3 of 5, against about 4.4 for the agent. A merge that kept more and narrower capabilities lost recall. Results: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/user/rav/projects/analyze-failed-runs/compare/`.

This pipeline ran end to end with GLM-5.3 on cw-us-east-02a, with a local Zephyr client (Iris jobs `/rav/zephyr-batch-a` and `/rav/zephyr-batch-b`). On 72 tau-bench failures in one shard it gave 8 ideas in 279 s, and on 144 failures in two shards of 72 it gave 7 ideas in 320 s. Both cited every failed rollout and skipped none. An earlier version with one shard for each rollout and a `reshard` before the merge took 37 s and 57 s on the same sets and found every category of the reference taxonomy, because its per-rollout calls ran in parallel.

`FILE_SAFE_ID` moves from `generate_tasks` to `catalog.py`, so that the analysis does not import the generation driver. `marin-taskforge` depends on `marin-rolloutengine` for the rollout records and the task tools and on `marin-zephyr` for the pipeline, and `taskforge-unit` also runs when `lib/rolloutengine`, `lib/zephyr`, or `lib/fray` changes.

Part of #10164.

comments.body:
🤖 Archived the description before automated prose cleanup.
<!-- marin-prose-cleanup-archive:61f76321f1dd436665942c890653d45f8bcf42daef5f063ca8267fbd73349b67 -->

<details><summary>Original description</summary>

```markdown
* part of #10164
* stacked on #10264 and #10203, so this PR shows only its own two commits
* add `analyze_failed_runs(runs, model, *, pass_threshold, limits, catalog_version)`: one managed agent reads the policy's failed runs and returns the missing capabilities as `CapabilityIdea` values, which `task_items` and `generate_tasks` turn into training tasks
  * a capability can be any behavior that would have made a run pass, for example the answer format, the use of tools, a stop to loops of repeated calls, or a careful reading of the task
* `policy_failures` keeps a run whose grade is below `pass_threshold` or whose submission is not valid, and leaves out interrupted attempts and infra, task, and grader failures, so that they do not become training targets
* the agent is one `RolloutEngine` attempt whose `shell_harness` serves two read-only tools, `read_run` and `search_runs`, and the `JsonValueAnswer` format of its task extracts the answer
  * each capability must cite failed runs, and an answer that cites another run, repeats an id, or does not validate raises `ValueError`
  * the agent sees only what the policy saw and wrote, never a grader or its answer
* one agent reads all the failed runs, and a later version can shard them with Zephyr
* `marin-taskforge` now depends on `marin-rolloutengine[chat]`, because the capability environments run in its package environment, so `taskforge-unit` also runs on `lib/rolloutengine` changes

```

</details>

🤖 One overlap to know about while this is a draft: the Taskforge stage stack now open as drafts #10291 to #10302 also makes marin-taskforge depend on marin-rolloutengine (in #10291, the llm slice, with the same pyproject line and the uv.lock stanza), and #10301 adds the capability driver this module would sit beside under experiments/post_training/capability_driven_envs. Whichever lands second will see a trivial conflict in lib/taskforge/pyproject.toml and the select_tests trigger; nothing else collides. No action needed now.

🤖 Evidence from the gen1000 env analysis (1,468 Taskforge envs, 8 adversary trials each) that bears on `policy_failures`.

**1. A graded reward below the threshold is about half the time a grader artefact.** The analysis agent cannot tell, because the files never show the grader.
- A DeepSeek pass over every sub-1.0 trial put 51% of them down to grader strictness.
- A blind Codex audit of 85 answers across 30 envs found a grader-defect mechanism in 53% (CI 35–70%). The defects were parsing and lexical (equivalent notation, keyword presence, any-number scans, disqualifier regexes), not numeric tolerance.
- Where an answer failed only non-core checks, strictness was confirmed in 76% of cases.

`SYSTEM_PROMPT` gives "obey the answer format that a task asks for" as its first example capability. That is the label these artefacts will get, so the loop would train the policy toward particular graders' lexical quirks.

**2. Most sub-threshold runs are partial credit on non-core checks.**
- 76% of in-band envs never score 0.
- Moving from the shortest to the longest grader quartile, the core-check miss rate stays flat at 8–11%, while failing only non-core checks rises from 1.6% to 18.2%.
- With `pass_threshold` near 1.0, most "failures" are therefore keyword rubrics, gates and caps.

Suggestions, in rough order of cost:
- Require each capability's `evidence` to span at least 2 distinct `task_id`s; the index already has them. With several samples per task, one defective grader otherwise yields a capability by itself. This is a cheap check next to the existing unknown-run check.
- In the prompt, say that a rollout whose substance is right but whose wording lost reward is not evidence of a missing skill.
- Put the grade's per-check pass/fail names from `GradeResult.detail` into the index, without the expected values, so the agent can set aside runs that failed only format or prose checks. Alternatively, exclude or down-weight tasks whose grader trips a static lexical flag (≥ 8 `re.*` calls or ≥ 6 `"literal" in text` tests). Against our labels that flag has precision about 0.8.

There is also a related point for `generate_tasks` rather than this PR. Catalog sample tasks were the largest source of formula-plug-in envs in gen1000:
- 45% of entry examples were plug-ins;
- capabilities whose two samples were both plug-ins ended up 46% plug-in, against 9% when neither was.

So whatever writes the training tasks for these capabilities should ask for multi-step work rather than the smallest checkable exercise.

topics.title: [canary-datakit-smoke] Store workers pending through CI wait deadline
topics.body:
The October 20 tier-1 Datakit ferry exceeded the 7,100-second Actions wait while `datakit/store` waited for workers. The store worker job was pending from 13:21:30 UTC through the 13:57 UTC deadline. The uploaded Iris job tree reported `Scheduler: Insufficient memory (need 32.0GB, available 20.7G...)`. At 14:00 UTC, all 106 workers were still pending; the driver had zero failures and preemptions. This recurs the store placement problem in #10064 and #10149.

Reproduce:
1. Run `.github/workflows/marin-canary-datakit-tier1.yaml` at commit `5ec80e71242485b353b1f4556d3d68eb0a4dddf5` under the observed cluster capacity.
2. Inspect the clustered-store worker job after `datakit/store` starts. `TIER1_SCALE.store` requests 4 CPU, 32 GiB RAM, and 64 GiB disk per worker.

Expected: enough store workers start for the ferry to finish within the CI wait budget, or the capacity shortage is reported before the deadline.

## Canary run context

- Lane: `datakit-smoke`; date: 2026-10-20 UTC
- Iris job: `/runner/iris-run-job-20261020-115834`
- [Actions run](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/39418711091) and [uploaded diagnostics](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/39418711091/artifacts/12269368696)
- [W&B run ID](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin/runs/datakit-smoke-39418711091-1): `datakit-smoke-39418711091-1`

<details>
<summary>Evidence</summary>

- Actions `Wait for datakit smoke ferry` raised `TimeoutError` at 13:57:23 UTC after 7,100 seconds.
- Finelog `marin` / `log`, key `/runner/iris-run-job-20261020-115834/0:0`, `epoch_ms` 1792497600000–1792504800000: seq `29992199313` starts `datakit/store` at 13:18:45 UTC; seq `29992199315` records 106 input shards and 106 map tasks. The preceding `datakit/verify_fuzzy_clusters` step succeeded at 13:18:43 UTC (seq `29992197765`).
- The uploaded `job-tree.txt` records the store worker job as pending since 13:21:30 UTC with the insufficient-memory scheduler verdict. Live Iris at 14:00 UTC showed 0/106 tasks completed and 106 pending. The durable ferry status still said `running` at 14:01 UTC.

</details>

topics.title: [iris] Capability proxy returns 502 while a preempted serve task is being replaced
topics.body:
When a served model's Iris task is preempted and replaced, the native capability proxy answers requests that arrive during the replacement with HTTP 502 `upstream transport error: client error (Connect)`. Clients see a hard failure for a gap Iris is already recovering from.

Impact: on 2026-10-18 an Evalchemy GSM8K screen on H100 lost 112 of 1,319 rows. Kueue preempted the serve task at 00:14:07 UTC; Iris rescheduled it and the replacement was initializing from 00:14:55. At 00:19 the proxy returned 502 to the queued requests, the client exhausted its retries, and the rows were recorded as `EVALCHEMY_INFRASTRUCTURE_ERROR` (`model_transport`). Recovery needed a manual selective rerun of the 112 doc ids and a cached regrade before the record could be merged (1,215/1,319 after recovery).

A second instance on 2026-10-19 lost 960 of 1,319 GSM8K rows. Kueue preempted the serve task at 03:42:04 UTC. Requests in flight at that moment got 502 `client error (SendRequest)` (15 responses at 03:42). Requests sent afterwards got 502 `client error (Connect)` (985 responses from 03:42 to 03:47) until the client gave up, and the rows were recorded as `EVALCHEMY_INFRASTRUCTURE_ERROR`. The same serve task was preempted six more times over the next 11 hours (attempts 1 to 6) at interactive priority. That record needed a full GSM8K rerun.

The 502 comes from the native proxy's upstream error path ([`lib/iris/rust/src/lib.rs` L1243-L1246](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8e99858a17df0463daac6b104f5eddb0ffa79ffd/lib/iris/rust/src/lib.rs#L1243-L1246)), which maps any connect failure to `BAD_GATEWAY`. [`lib/iris/docs/federation.md`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8e99858a17df0463daac6b104f5eddb0ffa79ffd/lib/iris/docs/federation.md) documents this message as "cannot connect to its upstream".

Reproduce:
1. Serve a model through a capability URL (for example the eval launcher with Harbor or a capability-routed Evalchemy run).
2. Send a steady stream of requests through the capability URL.
3. Preempt or cancel the serving task and let Iris start a replacement under the same endpoint name.
4. Requests sent before the replacement registers return 502 with the message above.

Expected: while the endpoint's job is still live and a replacement task is pending or initializing, the proxy holds the request until the endpoint registers again (bounded by the request timeout), or returns 503 with `Retry-After`. Clients retry connect errors and 503s with backoff for at least the documented serve replacement time. A replacement can take much longer than a request timeout: in the second instance the serve stayed unavailable for the rest of the GSM8K client's retry budget. Holding requests therefore covers short gaps only. Long gaps need the 503 signal so that the client can pause instead of recording failures.

Done when: a serve-replacement test through the capability proxy completes requests sent during the gap, or receives 503 with `Retry-After`, and no 502 is returned while the job is live.

Related: #10237 covers the direct-route client (`remote_inference`) keeping a stale address after rescheduling.

Evidence (Iris task events and the Evalchemy client log, URLs omitted):

```
2026-10-18T00:14:07.473Z attempt 0  k8s/kueue        WorkloadEvictedDueToPreempted  Preempted to accommodate a workload (UID: 3fc9af02-…)
2026-10-18T00:14:50.525Z attempt 0  iris/controller  TaskRetryScheduled             Backend reported PREEMPTED; controller returned the task to PENDING.
2026-10-18T00:14:55.578Z attempt 1  k8s/container    PodInitializing
[00:19:08] eval-gsm8k-0shot-2a8d8acc/0 | API request failed! Status code: 502, Response text: {"error":"upstream transport error: client error (Connect)"}. Retrying...
[00:19:09] eval-gsm8k-0shot-2a8d8acc/0 | API request failed! Status code: 502, Response text: {"error":"upstream transport error: client error (Connect)"}. Retrying...
```

Second instance: serve task `/karan/eval-20261019-025403-task238-arm-recovery-lr1e-06-step791-04d5/inference-177d09d0c73a4f048310e082db087746/0` (Kueue `WorkloadEvictedDueToPreempted` at 03:42:04, 05:19:02, 07:12:39, 10:56:25, 11:04:59, 14:19:01 and 14:24:54 UTC), evaluator task `/karan/eval-20261019-025403-task238-arm-recovery-lr1e-06-step791-04d5/eval-gsm8k-0shot-4ac3cd86/0`, record `20261019-025403-task238-arm-recovery-lr1e-06-step791-gsm8k-0shot-6554` (`infra_failed`, 359/1,319 scored).

First instance: serve task `/karan/eval-20261018-000555-task204-lr1e-06-step1095-1b9b/inference-a54b7942d3b34ffba92e5f0d4192aa69/0`. Evaluator task: `/karan/eval-20261018-000555-task204-lr1e-06-step1095-1b9b/eval-gsm8k-0shot-2a8d8acc/0`. Record: `20261018-000555-task204-lr1e-06-step1095-gsm8k-0shot-77c1`.

comments.body:
🤖
# Research

Iris keeps a serving endpoint's last address until its lease expires (at most 10 minutes). The native proxy can therefore route a request to a preempted task; its upstream transport error path returns 502. Once the lease expires, the registry omits the endpoint and the same live job can instead return 404. The registry has no replacement state, so changing 502 to 503 alone would leave that later gap unresolved. [PR #10033](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10033) handles Evalchemy's direct-route relay and does not change this capability path.

**Relevant code**
- [`endpoint_service.py#L40-L49`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/endpoint_service.py#L40-L49) — ten-minute registration lease.
- [`endpoint_service.py#L165-L177`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/endpoint_service.py#L165-L177) — live mappings enter the proxy snapshot.
- [`lib.rs#L230-L264`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/rust/src/lib.rs#L230-L264) — expired mappings are skipped.
- [`lib.rs#L1190-L1240`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/iris/rust/src/lib.rs#L1190-L1240) — transport failures become 502.
- [`client.py#L79-L93`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evalchemy/client.py#L79-L93) — Evalchemy allows eight request retries.

# Proposed Fix

The failure chain is task preemption → old endpoint address remains routable → connect/send fails → proxy returns 502; after lease expiry, lookup returns 404. This needs a controller/proxy availability contract and a capability-client retry budget, so it is larger than a local status-code patch.

1. Preserve an authenticated endpoint name while its owning task is being retried. Publish `ready` versus `replacing` in the controller's proxy snapshot/deltas; preemption and lease expiry make the old address unavailable, replacement registration restores `ready`, and terminal job/task state removes the route. Reconstruct the same state after controller restart.
2. Return 503 with `Retry-After` for `replacing` and for connect/send failures to task-owned endpoints, including a race before the registry update. Keep ordinary 404 for unknown names and 502 for unrelated upstream/protocol failures. Do not replay an in-flight POST inside the proxy.
3. Verify the pinned Evalchemy and Harbor capability clients retry 503 according to `Retry-After` with a time budget tied to the evaluation deadline and stop on terminal serve state. Extend their policy where needed; leave the direct-route relay in #10033 alone.
4. Add a real HTTP capability-proxy test that sends requests before preemption, during replacement, after the old lease expires, and after a new address registers. Assert no 502/404 during the recoverable gap, 503 plus `Retry-After` until recovery, successful forwarding afterwards, and terminal/unknown routes ending promptly. Cover an in-flight send failure and the federated capability relay as separate cases.

Open decision: the repository documents a 10-minute endpoint lease but no upper bound on serve replacement. Use the evaluation's overall deadline as the retry cap unless a shorter serve-replacement contract is established; eight immediate request retries are insufficient for the observed multi-minute gaps.

topics.title: [iris] Follow re-registered serve endpoints from Evalchemy evals
topics.body:
## tl;dr

While doing evals for another experiment ( https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9984), agent found that serve endpoints that got pre-empted permanently lost their connection. This should fix that.


## Full Explanation (agent)
Evalchemy children now reach their serve through a loopback relay that looks
the endpoint name up in the Iris registry, instead of a host:port resolved once
at launch. When Kueue preempts the serve and its retry registers on another
host, the old address refuses connections, hangs, or answers 404. The eval used
to retry that address until the group timed out: nine groups on cw-rno2a were
lost this way on 2026-10-09/10, some after 16-20 h.

The relay (iris.cluster.client.endpoint_relay) looks the name up every 30 s and
after each connection failure or 404. It aborts requests still waiting on a
replaced address and replays requests that have no response yet once the
endpoint is registered again (for up to 1 h, then 503). A response that has
started is never replayed; the relay drops the client connection so lm-eval's
own retries apply. Each relay thread keeps a pooled direct connection, so evals
keep the direct routing that #9480 chose over the hub proxy.

The fix sits in an Iris client module so any in-cluster client can use it. A
stable cluster-level address (a per-endpoint Kubernetes Service, or
controller-side forwarding) would cover every client without a helper process,
but it needs a controller deploy and work in each backend. The hub proxy
already follows re-registrations, and it is the path #9480 moved away from. The
relay ships in the job bundle and takes effect on the next eval launch.

While the Evalchemy job runs, the parent now reads the serve job states every
60 s. When one is terminal, it cancels the Evalchemy job and the record becomes
infra_failed with the serve job ID and state. A failed status read does not end
the eval. Before, the parent waited with no bound.

Tests drive the relay with real HTTP servers and a fake registry whose endpoint
moves mid-run. On a local in-process Iris cluster, the relay CLI in a client
task followed a serve job that was cancelled and replaced under the same
endpoint name; the request in flight during the gap waited about 4 s and was
answered by the replacement. A [CoreWeave smoke test](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10033#issuecomment-6136856836)
also passed task-token registry lookup and failover to a replacement port through
the `$IRIS_VENV` relay subprocess. Both serve tasks ran on the same node, and
the helper ran in a plain Iris task. Cross-host relocation and the actual
Evalchemy child's isolated uvx environment remain untested by that smoke.

Fixes #10030

topics.title: [grug] Add GB200 launch and H100 validation support
topics.body:
Add a GB200 launcher, tracked JAXPP runtime overlay and fresh Harrier data support to the H100 pipeline foundation merged in #9279. The launcher requests one NVLink domain in the opportunistic batch queue, separates admission and execution deadlines, and disables failure and preemption retries. Fresh-data trials disable simulated epoching before budget validation, preserving full datasets even when the mixture schedule exceeds the simulated-token budget. The runner closes its sampling and training iterators. Checkpoint metadata includes the data source, seed, schedule horizon and router-bias adaptation mode.

The runtime pins JAXPP `328f75a80cecf22c7cc030a82d8941d3c1e220b6` plus `runtime/jaxpp_host_startup.patch` (SHA256 `d987c16ece399fe5eeb69d413703d549135635f19a57dc4b6c60cc0d1ea4b1a7`), which keeps activation copies in forward tasks, preserves pinned-host output placement and warms tasks with disposable inputs. JAX 0.11.1 overrides JAXPP's declared compatibility cap and remains experimental. The overlay installer prevents Git from silently skipping files inside a repository-local virtual environment. Installer recovery avoids duplicate global reinstall flags; the [incident record](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/600) distinguishes the initial GitHub fetch failure from the recovery-command failure.

At executable `0da04acccf7b0842319a8668d71ccc697a7b10ec`, the eight-GB200 synthetic gate completed two finite updates with losses 11.806337356567383 and 0.4912489652633667. All eight native processes, both GPU tasks and the coordinator exited zero; all 48 startup task ABI records had zero input memory-kind mismatches. At `a1e3ab278eeb05bb645db641dd3e7dabedf90dbb`, 16 H100s completed ten synthetic and twenty fresh-data updates, consuming 2,621,440 fresh tokens with all 200 components nonempty. Both gates used two width-6144 layers from the [Hero model recipe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/hero-gb200-pipeline/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/hero_recipe.py) and FP32 parameters with BF16 compute. The H100 adapter uses pooled-wave/FA4 transport with SYRK disabled and establishes no ragged-transport parity. [GB200 commands](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/hero-gb200-pipeline/experiments/grug/moe_hero_pipeline/GB200.md) and the [H100 reference](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/hero-gb200-pipeline/docs/references/hero-pipeline-h100.md) retain runtime details and acceptance criteria.

The hardware gates predate the merged foundation's expert-bank normalization correction and option to freeze the adaptive router bias. The reconciled branch has not been rerun on GPUs. GPU checkpoint evidence remains limited to the [historical reduced-model comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/hero-gb200-pipeline/docs/references/hero-pipeline-h100.md#checkpoint-boundary-and-storage) at `77b4b15cae978b9acf2a721c47c3606773f6a177`: 90,018,826 stored bytes and a resumed-versus-uninterrupted loss difference of 9.5367431640625e-7 within unchanged 1e-5 tolerances. topics.title: [grug] Balance attention work across batch shards in hero train step
topics.body:
The hero train step now permutes the rows of each global batch so that each batch shard gets a similar amount of attention work. Document packing gives rows very different attention costs. When rows stay in loader order, the busiest of the 64 shards does 2.10x the mean global-attention work on real 16K hero batches. All other shards wait for that shard at the next collective.

`balance_attention_rows` uses the FA4 segment bounds of each row to count its attended query-key pairs. Padding tokens do not add to this count. The function sorts the rows by this cost. Before the forward pass, it deals the rows to the batch shards in snake order. Even rounds go from the first shard to the last shard, and odd rounds go back. Each shard then keeps its rows in loader order.

Expert capacity drops the later tokens of a shard first. If each shard kept its rows in cost order, the tokens of short-document rows would be dropped first. The permutation adds one all-gather and one reshard of each per-row batch array. Every token still enters the loss and the router statistics. However, the row placement can change which assignments exceed expert capacity, so the loss can also change.

On real batches at 16K, the ratio of busiest-shard work to mean work decreases from 2.10 to 1.17 for global layers and from 1.46 to 1.05 for local layers. At 4K, the ratio decreases from 1.29 to 1.01.

We measured both arms on the same GB200 NVL72 rack, with 106 scored steps per arm. Each arm restored from hero step 240000. At 16K context, the step time decreases from 13.131 to 13.055 s/step (+0.58% tokens/s). At 4K, it decreases from 12.764 to 12.732 s/step (+0.25%). The loss stays within same-code noise of the control. The drop fraction changes by less than 3%.

The companion PR changes the FA4 mask. With both changes on a second rack, the 16K step time decreases from 13.046 to 12.833 s/step (+1.66%). In that stack, balancing alone gives +0.29%, because faster masked attention also makes the imbalance smaller.

All numbers above come from the code before two later fixes. The cost now excludes padding, and each shard now keeps its rows in loader order. We did not measure again after these fixes.

All measurements used one rack. The all-gather sends the whole global batch to each GPU, so its cost increases with the number of racks. We did not measure this cost at the 11-rack hero size.
topics.head: 443e62c974ad679b937b7896e742ddd3283e1c4b

topics.title: [agents] Add a skill for auditing eval and reward graders
topics.body:
Add audit-grader, a skill for measuring how often a grader contradicts its task text before its scores are trusted. It covers code checks, LLM judges, and RL reward functions, and estimates a grader's error rate with a blinded review of frozen samples by two reviewers.

The worked example is the #10060 audit of Marin's 58 IFBench checkers. That audit found 43 checker findings, 9 of which depend on an interpretation decision. On held-out responses, Marin's checkers under strict grading contradicted the consensus of two Claude Opus 5.5 reviewers on an estimated 6.1% of constraint verdicts. The audit's validated checkers with IFBench's official readings (fixes only) contradicted it on 3.2%, a paired difference of 2.9 points (95% CI 2.4 to 3.4). Both reviewers are the same model, so they may share blind spots. The fixtures and review records are in the Hugging Face dataset at revision ceaba90: https://huggingface.co/datasets/xiaoyuanwang/ifbench-audit/tree/ceaba90ba6a2acac8fd8b51368a37e27c0ba688f.

The skill's reviewer prompt adapts the audit's, with the IFBench details replaced by placeholders.

Part of #10060.
