- "Clean-only line": a source line the Bug Patch removed that occurs nowhere in the bugged tree. 7 of the 20 tasks have none, so only the ref checks apply to them.
- The filesystem search found no git leak. It did find copies of clean lines in installed packages: `setuptools/_vendor/typeguard` is an older vendored typeguard, which is relevant for `agronholm/typeguard` tasks (57 in the pool). The `_pytest` (iniconfig) and `rapidfuzz` (thefuzz) hits are probably coincidental.
- Residual: `github.com/swesmith/<repo>` is public and keeps every instance branch, so an agent with internet access can still fetch the fix. In the Kimi traces this happened once (`git fetch origin; git show origin/main:<file>`).

Per-task results: `pool/swesmith-validation-20.jsonl` and `pool/swesmith-leak-probe-20.jsonl`.

**TMax: same class of leak, different mechanism.** In `allenai/TMax-SFT-16.5K@848e2182` `tasks.zip`, 221 of 2,200 environments build verifier assets into the agent's image (for example `/opt/oracle/<reference program>`, `/app/verifier/ground_truth_valid_events.txt`, `/home/user/oracle.py`), and `test_final_state.py` reads them. In 181 of the 221, the instruction never names the path. In the #202 Qwen3.6-27B success traces (`allenai/tmax-sft`), 63 trajectories across 18 tasks name one of these hidden paths in a bash command. That is a heuristic: naming a path doesn't prove the answer was copied. The pool excludes the 181 (`excluded.jsonl`, `leak_risk=hidden_verifier_assets`) and keeps the 40 visible ones. TMax's Harbor converter (`hamishivi/tmax@6d3d606c`) does not copy `task.json` (including its `truth` field), `solutions/`, `setup.sh` or `test_initial_state.py`; `test_final_state.py` goes only to `tests/`.

**Effect on #202's pilot training set:** 860 Kimi history-reading passes and those 63 TMax trajectories were removed before training (manifest `selection.swesmith_git_history_rule` and `selection.tmax_hidden_asset_rule`).

🤖 The public `github.com/swesmith` mirrors are now unreachable while the agent runs, and a second leak was found in mini-swe-agent's own install.

**TL;DR**
- During the agent phase, the sandbox can reach only the model proxy. github.com, PyPI, apt and every other host fail DNS, and direct-IP HTTPS (GitHub 140.82.112.3, 140.82.114.4; 1.1.1.1) has its TLS handshake cut. Setup and the verifier keep full network.
- mini-swe-agent 2.1.0 installs a tool env that the agent can read. It holds clean copies of three pool repos: pygments, pandas, tenacity. GLM read `tenacity/retry.py` from it and called it "the reference". The conda base in the images also holds boltons 23.0.0. All four repos (469 tasks) are excluded from pool P.

**Why not a whole-trial block:** Harbor sets the Daytona network policy once per sandbox. Both the mini-swe-agent install and the SWE-smith verifier (`tests/test.sh`) download uv from github.com releases (`astral.sh/uv/0.7.13/install.sh`), so a whole-trial allow-list without github.com breaks them.

**Mechanism** ([`harbor_agents/trial_agents.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/1555295d4d5a233e1bb854c814b927c21889574c/experiments/post_training/sft_shootout/harbor_agents/trial_agents.py), `AgentPhaseNetwork`, branch `task/207` @ `1555295d`): just before the agent's run, the live sandbox is switched to `domain_allow_list=iris.oa.dev` (the proxy host). The run starts once that host resolves, and the task's own policy is restored before the verifier. Each trial writes the applied policy to `agent/agent_network.json`, and the run's `driver_config.json` records it under `agent_network`.

**Measured** (null agent on swesmith-00008, -00698, -00763; HTTPS HEAD from inside the sandbox):

| Target | Before | Agent phase | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| `https://github.com/swesmith` | 200 | DNS failure | 200 |
| `api.github.com`, `raw.githubusercontent.com`, `codeload.github.com` | 200 | DNS failure | 200 |
| `https://140.82.112.3/`, `https://140.82.114.4/` (GitHub by IP) | 200 | TLS handshake cut | 200 |
| `https://1.1.1.1/` | 403 | TLS handshake cut | 403 |
| `pypi.org`, `deb.debian.org`, `archive.ubuntu.com`, `www.google.com` | 200 | DNS failure | 200 |

On these unchanged trees the verifier completed afterwards and scored 0, as expected. With GLM (`swe-net2`), 3/3 trials passed under the limit, and all 76 proxy calls returned 200. In one trial GLM ran `pip install pytest ...` and saw `No internet`.

A probe ran mini-swe-agent's real setup on one task from each of the 36 repos (`toolenv2`). It found the same 80 distributions on every image. Only three of them are pool repos: pygments (222 tasks), pandas (196) and tenacity (30). Every conda-based image also ships conda's own `boltons-23.0.0` under `/opt/miniconda3/pkgs`, including the mahmoud/boltons image (21 tasks). The install is now pinned (`mini-swe-agent-2.1.0-constraints.txt`, sha256 `c67d1ee2…`, Python 3.12), so this set cannot drift between the pilot and the full run. SWE-smith ingestion also drops any trace whose commands or outputs touch `/root/.local/share/uv/tools/`.

**Run folders** (`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/generation/dryrun/`):
- `netprobe2`, `netprobe3`, `netprobe4`: network probes; `agent/network_probe.json` per trial.
- `swe-net2`: GLM trials under the limit.
- `toolenv2`: tool-env listing; union in `tool_env.json`.

- **AgentTrove clone tasks:** 40,590 of AgentTrove's swesmith rows (the GLM-4.6, GPT 5.1 Nano and Kimi K2.0 streams, and part of GLM-4.7) use a different task format. The instruction itself says "clone the repo `swesmith/<mirror>` and run `git fetch && git checkout <instance branch>`". Every one of those sandboxes holds the mirror's full history, including the clean `main`, by design. 8.8% of them then read git history.

**Method:** the shootout's own rules, used verbatim: `GIT_HISTORY_READ` from #202's selection, and the host prefix from chukar's `repository_pytest.py`. Each task's repo and fix lines come from DCAgent's packages (`78b0d879`). Code: [`scripts/task215/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/29a6fb1919/scripts/task215); `audit.py` docstring and README list the exact regexes. Spot checks of random hits were all real history reads or real fix lines.

The shootout pool's fixed packages (one commit, no remote) and its no-internet agent phase close this path for new traces. Any SFT that used these sets' passes trained on traces that may have copied the fix.

topics.title: [taskforge] Add validation trials, failure classifier and control replay
topics.body:
Add `stage50_validate`, which runs a built task's trials and replays its fixed controls. `lowering.lower` lowers a draft's task for the validating host, with machine startup deadlines that outlast the Iris factory's scheduling budget so a sandbox that never starts is the factory's typed timeout. `control_drafts.write_controls` asks the model for a round's fixed controls and checks them against the grader step's reference answer and rejection ceiling, refusing a control that submits the same reply and files as a candidate the grader step already graded, since controls are written, not fitted to the grader.

Before trials, `preflight` probes a grader-base task machine on the local backend once and moves it to the container backend if its setup fails there, because a setup command can write where the local backend cannot and only running it shows that. `trials.run_trials` runs k trials of a `TaskRolloutSpec` on one RolloutEngine (`EngineSettings.engine`) under the messages trace. Each trial is `Graded` or `Ungraded` with one typed `Cause` from `classify.classify`, the only failure classifier, and a retryable cause triggers another attempt. `evidence` totals graded trials, and `controls.replay` replays each control as a `CONTROL` trial.

The standard template's end-to-end test now lowers its built task and runs it through RolloutEngine, and the infrastructure test checks the validation deadlines; both assertions were held back from #10298.

Builds on #10298; #10301 builds on it.

---

topics.title: [grafana] Reduce dashboard query fan-out and align live windows
topics.body:
Fetch only the source groups needed by each dashboard view and share their Arrow results across related panels. Accelerator queries return scalar tiles and chart aggregates directly; device histories pack repeated labels before transfer. Jobs, Runs, and RL avoid unrelated source queries.

Floor both window bounds independently to 15-second boundaries when the end is within 60 seconds of server time, so independently resolved panel overrides share cached work. Original bounds are validated first; older historical windows and ranges shorter than 15 seconds remain exact. Absolute windows ending near now are also aligned. Rounding adds less than 15 seconds of lag alongside the existing 20-second cache TTL.

Across two matched replays with cold bridge caches against the unchanged live hub, median Home latency fell from 14.77 to 1.80 seconds and SQL calls from 25 to 6. Median Jobs latency fell from 8.02 to 1.23 seconds for 128 selected jobs. One isolated three-hour power request fell from 9.11 to 0.77 seconds with the same result. These are bridge measurements; browser rendering, variable selectors, and external data sources are excluded. A subsequent matched comparison of the already optimized Accelerator page fell from 7.81 to 5.99 seconds by selecting existing metric-family Parquet projections. RL phase filtering reduces unused source rows but has no demonstrated page-level latency gain; both pages retain substantial cold-query costs.

Add a dashboard replay benchmark that retains source SQL, Arrow inputs, panel responses, and timing evidence, plus fixed-query support in the Finelog benchmark. Finelog runtime and storage behavior are unchanged. The [Accelerator/RL follow-up](https://loom.oa.dev/s/m6hemaex/artifacts/finelog-dashboard-followup) records the SQL candidates and remaining scan costs. The [report and full comparison](https://loom.oa.dev/s/m6hemaex/artifacts/finelog-query-report) include output parity, timing ranges, freshness limits, and rollout gates.

topics.title: [shellbox] Let local machines write system directories copy-on-write
topics.body:
LocalMachineFactory takes system_directories=SystemDirectories.COPY_ON_WRITE,
which overlays /usr, /bin, /sbin, /lib*, /etc and /opt in each machine with a
writable layer of its own. Commands see the host's files plus their machine's
writes; the writes persist across that machine's commands, close() discards
them, and the host never changes. The default stays READ_ONLY.

Generated Taskforge tasks that write under /opt (a seeded generator written by
a setup command, task resources shipped there) failed on the local backend and
passed in gVisor. With this mode they run locally.

Files the host mounts inside an overlaid directory are bound back read-only
after the overlay, because overlayfs shows only the directory's own
filesystem; without this, a Kubernetes pod's /etc/resolv.conf and /etc/hosts
would revert to the image's copies. The workdir may lie in an overlaid
directory, and upload and download there, like an upload to /, go through the
sandbox as a tar stream so they see the machine's layer. These transfer
commands run in a fixed environment that MachineSpec.env does not change, and
the downloaded stream is treated as untrusted: it must start with a regular
file or directory, hard links must stay inside it, and devices are refused. A
download of / from a copy-on-write machine is refused. The factory's startup probe mounts
the overlays, so a host without overlayfs, or with a temporary directory on
overlayfs, raises SandboxUnavailable. Writes keep file permissions, so changing
root-owned directories needs a root host process, as on Iris under the
PRIVILEGED profile.

On cw-rno2a, the layer adds no measurable cost per command (18.1 ms with
/opt, /usr and /etc overlaid, 18.2 ms without), and two concurrent commands of
one machine share its layer correctly.

The local-machine suite passes as root on cw-rno2a under the PRIVILEGED profile, except `test_a_python_environment_runs_its_own_interpreter_and_locked_packages`, which also fails on main there (offline resolution with a fresh uv cache). The copy-on-write tests skip on non-root hosts. After the review fixes, the local-machine suite gave 34 passed, 2 skipped and that same failure as root on cw-rno2a. Part of #10119.
topics.head: b1c18cff3e55d7479302b51fd6d7347686dcd444

comments.body:
On it — https://loom.oa.dev/s/hkl7gybj
[marin-style-nightly-updates](https://loom.oa.dev/s/hkl7gybj/artifacts/marin-style-nightly-updates)

- 🟢 `Oct 15 20:01Z` Preparing filesystem consolidation comment for PR #10155
- 🟢 `Oct 15 20:03Z` Posted filesystem consolidation proposal with Mermaid diagrams: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10155#issuecomment-6201163021

🤖 I would consolidate around the *guest filesystem view*. A Python `CoWMount.write()` that intercepts writes by path would have to reproduce the symlink, nested mount, and permission rules that bubblewrap and overlayfs already enforce.

Today [upload/download](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/71c7031f20929f833455f367705e13e0bb7dee40/lib/shellbox/src/shellbox/backends/local/machine.py#L463-L495) choose between host `shutil` and a tar command in the sandbox:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["upload / download"] --> B{"Path under an overlay?"}
    B -->|yes| C["tar through run()"]
    B -->|no| D["_host_path + shutil"]
    C --> E["guest view: root + overlays + binds"]
    D --> F["host root or host mount"]
```

That split misses a nested mount when the requested path is its parent. For example, uploading a tree containing `opt/task` to `/` writes the private host backing directory at `root/opt/task`, which the `/opt` overlay hides. Downloading `/app` similarly misses a read-only mount at `/app/data`. `_overlaid()` is a lexical prefix check, so it does not describe the effective mount after a guest symlink or a read-only bind inside `/etc`.

I suggest two narrow pieces:

1. A `SandboxLayout` value holds the private root, overlay upper/work directories, system binds, and declared read-only mounts. It also supplies the read-only bind-backs for host mounts hidden by an overlay, such as a pod’s `/etc/hosts`. Pass this value to the existing `_sandbox_argv`, which already serves the startup probe that checks overlayfs support and each command. Keep early validation of declared read-only workdirs here.
2. Keep `Machine.upload`/`download` as the file API. Route **every guest-side copy** through a helper with `copy_into_guest` and `copy_out_of_guest` operations in that same bwrap view. Give it a fixed control environment instead of task `PATH`/`TAR_OPTIONS`, and define one policy for symlinks, archive extraction, directory merges, and size limits. Stream an archive through the helper, or bind a temporary host staging directory into its sandbox; either way, copy at the guest path.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    Factory["LocalMachineFactory"] --> Layout["SandboxLayout"]
    Layout --> Args["ordered bwrap mounts"]
    Run["run user command"] --> Args
    Transfer["upload / download"] --> Helper["guest transfer helper"]
    Helper --> Args
    Args --> View["one kernel-resolved guest filesystem"]
    Host["host source / destination"] <--> Helper
```

This removes `_overlaid()` and `_host_path()` from transfer routing; the mount plan remains for setup and validation. I would cover a tree uploaded at `/` that contains `/opt` files, a download of a parent with a nested bind, merged-`/usr` symlinks, and the [existing symlink escape case](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10155#discussion_r4284678943). Keep `COPY_ON_WRITE` explicit: falling back to read-only after a failed overlay probe would change whether a task can write `/opt`.

🤖 I addressed the review threads in 2cf890a2bb and b1c18cff3e:

- Transfers that reach a layer, including an upload to `/`, now pass through the sandbox.
- A download of `/` from a copy-on-write machine is refused.
- The backend's transfer commands run in a fixed environment.
- A downloaded stream is treated as untrusted.
- An upload of a symlinked source sends what the link leads to.
- `_sandbox_error` is now `_prepare_sandbox`.

I merged `origin/main` into the branch. As root on cw-rno2a under the PRIVILEGED profile, `lib/shellbox/tests/test_local_machine.py` gave 34 passed, 2 skipped and 1 failed. The failure is `test_a_python_environment_runs_its_own_interpreter_and_locked_packages`, the offline-resolution failure that also happens on main there.

The consolidation in the proposal above (one `SandboxLayout` and a guest transfer helper in place of `_overlaid` and `_host_path` routing) is left for the cleanup pass.

topics.title: [taskforge] Add machine factories, task images and the image builder
topics.body:
Taskforge runs a task's machines on whichever host it is on, a laptop or an Iris task, and builds task images from Dockerfiles the model writes. This adds the `sandbox` package that the build and validation stages share for both.

`sandbox.factories` picks the shellbox machine factories per host: ShellSim and Docker on a laptop, ShellSim and gVisor on Iris, and the local backend for lock-only graders where bubblewrap works. A laptop whose Docker daemon is missing, unreachable or slower than the 20 s probe keeps ShellSim only. `task_refusals` asks each factory about the machines of a `TaskRolloutSpec` before a trial starts, so validation can record a typed refusal with the factory's message instead of failing inside a started trial. ShellSim gets the package catalog its CPython comes from.

`IrisImageBuilder` builds a `DockerBuild` with kaniko in one Iris CPU job and pushes it with `crane` in a second job, so the registry credential never shares a container with the model-authored Dockerfile. It returns the image pinned by manifest digest. The builder takes the credential at construction and reads no secret store, so it runs on a host without `gcloud` or Google credentials, such as a coordinator in an Iris task. Only the laptop helper `registry_credential_json` calls `gcloud`, and `scripts/build_image_job.py` uses it to run one build from a laptop. `sandbox.host_failures` holds the host-failure messages that both stages classify.

Builds on #10292; #10294 builds on it. The build stage (#10298) constructs the builder and classifies host failures, and validation (#10300) calls `task_refusals`. Two manual machine tests need `spec.draft` and land in #10294.

topics.title: [dependencies] Upgrade Rigging with the MarinSkyRL external lock
topics.body:
The external lock updater upgrades `marin-rigging` together with `marinskyrl`. The MarinSkyRL lock overrides Rigging's requirement with a lower bound, which hides the exact Rigging version that published Iris, Finestore and TaskCompendium wheels require. Upgrading only `marinskyrl` let uv keep the locked Rigging 0.2.174 beside Iris 0.2.206, and the updater's `uv pip check` then failed. That failure stops both the scheduled external dependency refresh and the MarinSkyRL CatCount nightly, which runs the same updater.

Running `uv run config/update-external.py MarinSkyRL` on this branch resolves Rigging, Iris, Finestore and TaskCompendium to 0.2.206.dev39408141072, and `uv pip check` reports all installed packages compatible. The refreshed lock is left to the scheduled refresh.

Fixes #10117

topics.title: levanter: keep eval metrics between telemetry detail intervals
topics.body:
Keep evaluation metrics between telemetry detail intervals. `TelemetryTracker` publishes metrics under `eval/`, `labeled_eval/`, and `lm_eval/` at every step. At steps outside the detail interval, it previously published only `train_loss`, `phase`, and progress time, so evaluation metrics logged at those steps were lost.

These prefixes are the defaults in `eval.py`, `callbacks/labeled_eval.py`, `eval_harness.py`, and `train_dpo.py`. A run with a custom prefix keeps the detail interval. A shared constant would change the defaults of those four modules and is outside this fix.

Split from #10108.

---

topics.title: [grug] Add an AMD Grug attention layer benchmark for one or more GPUs
topics.body:
Add `lib/levanter/scripts/bench/bench_grug_attention_amd.py`, which times one Grug attention layer on one or more AMD GPUs. It exits unless the backend is ROCm: it targets the AMD Pallas-Triton kernel, and the NVIDIA FA4/CuTe kernels need packed segment IDs that its inputs do not have. 

For each mask (2048-token sliding window, global causal) and each implementation passed to `--impl`, it reports forward and forward-plus-backward time and the max absolute output difference against the first implementation. 

With `--sweep --sweep-part fwd|dq|dkv` it times a grid of tile sizes, warps and stages for one of the three Pallas-Triton flash kernels (forward, dQ, dK/dV) and keeps the defaults for the other two. `--block-q`, `--block-k`, `--num-warps` and `--num-stages` replace that kernel's default values for one axis of the grid. 

TFLOP/s counts only the FLOPs the mask needs over the allowed (query, key) pairs. Each time is the median of ten 0.2 s windows after a 1 s warmup. Results are printed as `RESULT {json}` lines.

`--num-devices N` runs on the first N GPUs with the batch sharded over an explicit `data` mesh axis, as in Grug training. `--batch` is per GPU, so the global batch is N times it; TFLOP/s are reported in total and per device.

Defaults are the June per-GPU shape at global batch 64 on 8 GPUs: 8 x 4096 tokens, 20 query heads, 5 KV heads, head_dim 128, bf16.

```bash
python lib/levanter/scripts/bench/bench_grug_attention_amd.py --impl reference xla_flash gpu_pallas_triton_flash
python lib/levanter/scripts/bench/bench_grug_attention_amd.py --sweep --sweep-part dkv --block-q 64 128 --num-stages 1
python lib/levanter/scripts/bench/bench_grug_attention_amd.py --num-devices 8
```

Forward plus backward time on one MI350X with jax 0.11.1 and the ROCm 10.1 plugin (job 460980):

| Mask | reference | xla_flash | gpu_pallas_triton_flash |
|---|---|---|---|
| window 2048 | 18.84 ms (96 TF/s) | 22.66 ms (80 TF/s) | 6.74 ms (268 TF/s) |
| causal | 20.89 ms (115 TF/s) | 22.89 ms (105 TF/s) | 10.02 ms (240 TF/s) |

In the same job, the dK/dV sweep with the window mask ran all 36 configs. The default tile, 128 queries x 64 keys with 4 warps and 1 stage, was the fastest at 6.80 ms.

On one Vultr MI355X node with jax 0.11.0 in the TheRock 7.14 container (job 11645), 8 GPUs at global batch 64 run within 1% of one GPU at batch 8, so per-device throughput holds under batch sharding. Forward plus backward, TF/s per GPU:

| Mask | GPUs | reference | xla_flash | gpu_pallas_triton_flash |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| window 2048 | 1 | 15.60 ms (116 TF/s) | 21.47 ms (84 TF/s) | 5.87 ms (307 TF/s) |
| window 2048 | 8 | 15.78 ms (114 TF/s) | 21.77 ms (83 TF/s) | 5.91 ms (305 TF/s) |
| causal | 1 | 15.08 ms (160 TF/s) | 21.57 ms (112 TF/s) | 9.19 ms (262 TF/s) |
| causal | 8 | 15.24 ms (158 TF/s) | 21.81 ms (110 TF/s) | 9.23 ms (261 TF/s) |

On 8 GPUs, the default dK/dV tile was again the fastest of the six block sizes swept (block_q 64 or 128, block_k 32, 64 or 128, 4 warps, 1 stage), at 5.91 ms.

The script imports `TritonFlashBlockSizes` and `pallas_triton_flash_attention` from `levanter.grug.attention._amd_pallas_triton_flash`, which #10014 added.

Part of #9812

topics.title: Marin 67B-A2B (65k and 262k checkpoints) vs Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base and Gemma 4 26B-A4B: Paloma and UncheatableEval BPB with lm-eval-exact scoring
topics.body:
🤖 Comparison of the Marin 67B-A2B checkpoints from #6044 and #8813 against Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base, scored the same way lm-eval scored the open-weight baselines in #8824.

## TL;DR

- On the Paloma test split, the 65k-context checkpoint (step 156k) gets **0.7812** macro BPB and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base gets **0.8397** (−7.0%). Our model is lower on 15 of 16 subsets; M2D2 S2ORC is the exception (+2.4%).
- On the 7 legacy UncheatableEval subsets, it gets **0.5178** vs **0.5245** (−1.3%). We are lower on Wikipedia, BBC News and AO3. Qwen is lower on C++ (by 5.7%), arXiv Physics and arXiv CS; Python is a tie.
- Against Gemma 4 26B-A4B, the pre-trained base (`google/gemma-4-26B-A4B`; the instruction-tuned model is the separate `-it` repo), the 65k checkpoint gets **0.7812** vs **0.8100** on Paloma (−3.6%). Our model is lower on 12 of 16 subsets; Gemma is lower on C4 100 domains, 100 subreddits, Gab and Twitter AAE. On the 7 UncheatableEval subsets Gemma is lower: **0.5138** vs our **0.5178** (ours is 0.8% higher). We are lower on GitHub Python, arXiv Physics and arXiv CS; Gemma is lower on Wikipedia, GitHub C++, BBC News and AO3. All Gemma numbers are our own lm-eval run, not #8824's (see "Gemma: correction to the #8824 numbers").
- **Correction:** an earlier version of this issue used #8824's Gemma Paloma macro of 0.8494 and reported our lead as −8.0%. Run through our lm-eval setup, Gemma gets 0.8100. The difference is concentrated in short-document subsets (Twitter AAE 2.564 vs 2.016, Gab 1.469 vs 1.287), so #8824's Gemma setup differs from ours in a way that isn't context length. Qwen's #8824 numbers do reproduce under our setup.
- At 32k context, Paloma macro is **0.7716** (ours), **0.8278** (Qwen, −6.8%) and **0.7837** (Gemma, −1.5%). Gemma gains more from the longer context (−3.2%) than ours (−1.2%) or Qwen (−1.5%). UncheatableEval does not change, because every document fits in 4k tokens.
- The 262k context extension (qk_mult 1.75, 8× long-document skew, step 157k) is slightly lower again: 0.7795 Paloma, 0.5171 UncheatableEval.
- Marin's in-training Paloma numbers are not directly comparable to the #8824 open-model rows: Levanter scores Paloma **val**, lm-eval scores Paloma **test**, and Levanter packs documents. See "Why earlier Marin numbers differ" below.

| **Macro (7)** | 7,052 | **0.5178** | **0.5171** | **0.5245** | **0.5138** | **-1.3%** | **+0.8%** |

## Method

The scorer reimplements lm-eval 0.4.12 `loglikelihood_rolling` for grug checkpoints. Evalchemy pins upstream lm-eval v0.4.12, and Qwen's run used the stock `local-completions` backend with `max_length=4096`, `tokenizer_backend=huggingface`, `tokenized_requests=True` (from its results JSON).

- **Documents:** scored one at a time, nothing packed. Paloma test split (revision `65cd6fc`, 154,440 docs); UncheatableEval Sept 1–14 2025 dumps (7,052 docs).
- **Windows:** lm-eval's API backend uses `max_length - 1` and rolls with `max_length - 1` again, so windows predict 4,094 tokens, each conditioned on the single preceding token, except the final window of each document, which keeps a full 4,094-token left context. The window code was checked against lm-eval's own `get_rolling_token_windows` + `make_disjoint_window` for lengths 0–30,000.
- **Tokenization:** HF tokenizer with `add_special_tokens=False`. The prefix token is BOS when the tokenizer has one (Marin: `<|begin_of_text|>`; Qwen has no BOS, so lm-eval used `<|endoftext|>`).
- **BPB:** summed NLL ÷ UTF-8 bytes of the document text, per subset; macro is the unweighted mean over subsets (matches Qwen's reported 0.839683).
- **Model:** params-only restore on a v4-64 in us-central2, bf16 compute. Before scoring, each job checks `qk_mult`, width, depth, expert counts, sliding window, `disable_long_rope` and `disable_pko` against the training run's `.executor_info` and fails on any mismatch (65k ckpt: qk_mult 1.57; 262k ckpt: 1.75).
- **Qwen numbers:** taken from the #8824 results file [qwen-results.json](https://storage.googleapis.com/marin-public/held/hero-open-weight-ppl/2026.09.05.1/qwen-results.json). A rerun of Qwen with lm-eval 0.4.12 reproduced them (Paloma 0.8404 vs 0.8397, UncheatableEval 0.5246 vs 0.5245; [W&B run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/lz5m5lk3)).
- **Gemma numbers:** our run of `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B` revision `24548b6` with lm-eval 0.4.12 `local-completions` (`max_length=4096`, HF tokenizer, tokenized requests) against vLLM 0.30.0 on 8×H100, on the same 154,440 Paloma and 7,052 UncheatableEval documents: [W&B run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/3rzcpy9e) (lm-eval results JSON attached). This is the same setup that reproduced Qwen.

## Reproduce

```bash
git checkout 9cb1640a79
# one job per checkpoint; each runs Paloma (test) and UncheatableEval as two child jobs on v4-64 us-central2
.venv/bin/iris --cluster=marin job run --no-wait --region us-central2 -e WANDB_API_KEY "$WANDB_API_KEY" \
    -- python -m experiments.grug.moe.eval_67b_a2b_step156k_paloma_lm_eval_rolling step156k
.venv/bin/iris --cluster=marin job run --no-wait --region us-central2 -e WANDB_API_KEY "$WANDB_API_KEY" \
    -- python -m experiments.grug.moe.eval_67b_a2b_step156k_paloma_lm_eval_rolling skew8
git checkout e5caad072b && uv run --with matplotlib python experiments/grug/moe/plot_67b_a2b_vs_open_bases_bpb.py bpb.png
```

Each child job takes 5–15 minutes once the slice is up. The 262k job ran exactly this commit. The 65k job ran an earlier revision of the same file with identical scoring code but without the startup config check; its config was checked separately (qk_mult 1.57).

## Context length: 4k vs 32k

All three models rescored with lm-eval `max_length=32768` (ours: same grug scorer, [W&B Paloma](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/moe_67b_a2b_d2560_step156k_paloma_lm_eval_rolling32768); Qwen: [W&B](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/rfqtrvbi); Gemma: [W&B](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/qtfi2lqk)). The 4k columns are our own runs of each model; Qwen's 4k column is the rerun, not #8824. Only documents longer than 4,094 tokens change, so Gab, 100 subreddits and Twitter AAE are identical at both lengths, as expected. UncheatableEval is unchanged for all three models (its longest document is 4,082 tokens).

## Gemma: correction to the #8824 numbers

#8824's Gemma file gives Paloma macro 0.8494. Our lm-eval setup, which reproduces #8824's Qwen numbers, gives 0.8100 at 4k. The per-subset differences go both ways, so it is not a context-length effect:

| Paloma subset | #8824 | Ours, 4k | Ours, 32k |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Twitter AAE | 2.5644 | 2.0164 | 2.0164 |
| Gab | 1.4689 | 1.2869 | 1.2869 |
| 100 subreddits | 0.8904 | 0.8599 | 0.8599 |
| 4chan | 0.8415 | 0.8773 | 0.7979 |
| M2D2 S2ORC | 0.6173 | 0.6480 | 0.5861 |
| Penn Treebank | 0.8385 | 0.8932 | 0.8109 |
| **Macro (16)** | **0.8494** | **0.8100** | **0.7837** |

Short-document subsets are much worse in #8824 (Twitter AAE, Gab), while some long-document subsets are better in #8824 than in our 4k run (4chan, M2D2 S2ORC, Penn Treebank), which suggests a longer window there. The #8824 Gemma file is a summary without its lm-eval config, so we can't pin down the difference; BOS handling on short documents is one candidate. This issue now uses our own run for every Gemma number.

## Why earlier Marin numbers differ

Same checkpoint (step 156k), three ways of scoring Paloma:

| Scoring | Paloma split | Macro BPB |
|---|---|---:|
| In-training Levanter eval, 65,536-token packed sequences | val | 0.7896 |
| Levanter eval, 4,096-token packed sequences, full coverage | val | 0.8037 |
| lm-eval-exact (this issue) | test | 0.7812 |

- **Split:** lm-eval prefers a task's test split when it has one, and the Paloma template defines both. Levanter's validation sets use val. They are different documents (e.g. Falcon 1,553 val vs 1,711 test; mC4 1,108 vs 1,202).
- **Packing:** on UncheatableEval, where the documents are identical, the 4k packed eval gives 0.5395 and the exact method gives 0.5178. Packing cuts short documents at sequence boundaries and drops each subset's final partial sequence; lm-eval scores every document whole.
- **Context:** going from 65k to 4k packed sequences raised BPB most on long-document subsets (code +10.0%, M2D2 S2ORC +5.6%, RedPajama +5.1%) and barely moved Gab, Penn Treebank and Twitter AAE.

The Hero numbers and forecast in #8824 come from the packed Levanter eval on val, so they share this mismatch with the open-model rows there.

## Caveats

- `uncheatable_eval_hero`, the task #8824 used for Qwen, is not in evalchemy or the marin repo. Its per-subset document counts match ours exactly, but we could not confirm that it scores the raw `text` field.
- Training-data overlap with Paloma is unknown for both models. Paloma's C4, Dolma, RedPajama and Falcon subsets come from web-crawl sources close to our mix; the lead over Qwen is larger on Paloma (−7.0%) than on UncheatableEval (−1.3%).
- One evaluation per checkpoint. Scoring is deterministic, but the 262k vs 65k gap (−0.0017 Paloma, −0.0007 UncheatableEval) is small enough that we would not read much into it.
- Qwen's training compute is not public; #8824 assumes 36T tokens.

## Next

- Score Trinity Mini Base and Ling-lite-base-1.5 with the same lm-eval setup for more same-size base-model points. GPT-OSS-20B and GLM-4.7 Flash have no base checkpoints.
- Confirm the `uncheatable_eval_hero` task definition with the #8824 author.

topics.title: [rl] Build a 10k quality and annotation pilot for Snowball
topics.body:
Build a fixed 10,000-environment pilot to evaluate lightweight quality filtering and curriculum annotations before processing the full Snowball candidate pool.

Sample the converted training population before curation admission, retaining prior admission status for comparison. Use `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-semantics/publication-008e95e5/2026.10.15.1/release.json` and each source's pinned `curation_root`. The full converted population contains evaluation tasks, so training intent and known holdout exclusions must be applied explicitly.

Done when:

- [ ] Remove evaluation/known holdout overlap and exact duplicate task contracts, then allocate exactly 10,000 available inputs: 50% equal source mass and 50% proportional to square root of source population. Cap at availability, redistribute, and use seeded deterministic selection.
- [ ] Freeze selected TaskSpecs, source counts, inclusion probabilities, hashes, and prior admission evidence. Do not refill the cohort after quality filtering.
- [ ] Bind the intended decision model explicitly. Produce keep/reject/uncertain decisions with reason codes and evidence; distinguish infrastructure or unavailable evidence from task defects.
- [ ] Bind DeepSeek Flash explicitly for public-content summaries, domain/skill tags, and provisional difficulty with rationale/confidence. Keep private grading evidence out of summaries and model-visible RL inputs.
- [ ] Embed summaries with the existing pinned Harrier pipeline. Reuse request/vector caching and retain model, prompt, schema, and input provenance.
- [ ] Report quality acceptance, uncertainty, failures, timing, and cost by source, plus tag/difficulty coverage and embedding-neighborhood audits. Validate a small endpoint calibration batch before full pilot inference.
- [ ] Define a bounded Snowball rollout calibration panel separately from static quality judgments. Pin checkpoint, tokenizer/runtime, attempts, decoding settings, resource limits, and pass definition before execution; distinguish infrastructure failures from model failures.

An initial metadata-only allocation totals 10,000 inputs across 142 training sources, with 40–480 per source. Recompute it after eligibility checks. TaskSpecs have not been selected and inference has not run. Storage credentials and the decision/Flash model IDs and service bindings remain unresolved.

Reuse the [existing curation description/embedding graph](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/205558e1a7fc3dd705b1132691798b09dc1f254c/experiments/post_training/task_curation/README.md#task-and-curriculum-embeddings); its diagnostic assessment currently does not change admission.

Related efforts: [#10314](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10314), [#10316](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10316).

Local prototype implemented in `experiments/post_training/snowball_curriculum/{pilot,annotations}.py`, with usage in its README. It freezes a cohort, prepares or executes explicit model requests through the existing cache, retains failures in the fixed denominator, and preserves task-to-summary-to-vector lineage. The combined curriculum suite has eight passing tests; repository lint passes and scoped Pyrefly reports zero errors. No code has been pushed, real TaskSpecs have not been selected, and inference has not run. Production admission joins, human audits, and cost/token aggregation remain open; Harrier execution also needs the optional PyTorch dependencies.

# Research

The published corpus is a pre-admission population. The existing embedding driver reads its `normalize` view, but its optional sample is per source and runs before the pilot's holdout and contract checks; it cannot freeze the specified global 10,000-task cohort. The proposal in [#10316](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10316) defines the pilot separately from the admitted training pool in [#10314](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10314). No open PR targets #10315; [#10280](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10280) adds a TaskSpec decision grader, which is a separate use of a decision model.

**Relevant code**
- [`embedding.py#L106-L129`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5ec80e71242485b353b1f4556d3d68eb0a4dddf5/experiments/post_training/task_curation/embedding.py#L106-L129) — converted view and current sampling boundary
- [`fingerprints.py#L74-L97`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5ec80e71242485b353b1f4556d3d68eb0a4dddf5/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/pipeline/fingerprints.py#L74-L97) — task contract identity
- [`sampling.py#L11-L29`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5ec80e71242485b353b1f4556d3d68eb0a4dddf5/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/pipeline/sampling.py#L11-L29) — seeded selection primitive
- [`semantics.py#L160-L179`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5ec80e71242485b353b1f4556d3d68eb0a4dddf5/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/pipeline/semantics.py#L160-L179) — public-only model input
- [`curriculum/embedding.py#L47-L74`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/5ec80e71242485b353b1f4556d3d68eb0a4dddf5/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/pipeline/curriculum/embedding.py#L47-L74) — pinned text/vector cache key and normalization

# Proposed Fix

1. Add a versioned pilot entry point under `experiments/post_training/task_curation/`. Resolve the pinned `release.json` and each source's `curation_root`; hash the resolved manifests and read converted `normalize` TaskSpecs. Require training intent, apply the explicit evaluation and known-holdout registry, and group exact contracts with `deduplication_key`. Assign each cross-source duplicate one representative by source ID, task ID, and locator; retain its aliases and distinct verifier contracts. Join the pinned production catalog's `final` rows only to record prior admission; unresolved holdout coverage fails the freeze gate.
2. Count eligible representatives per source, then allocate 10,000 quotas using `0.5 / source_count + 0.5 * sqrt(eligible_count) / sum(sqrt(eligible_count))`. Round by largest remainder with source-ID ties, cap at availability, and redistribute until filled. Select by seeded contract identity without replacement. Publish immutable TaskSpecs and a sidecar keyed by source, task ID, locator, and contract digest with source counts, quotas, inclusion probabilities (`quota / eligible_count`), exclusion reasons, aliases, seed, hashes, and prior admission evidence. Fail with an explicit shortfall if fewer than 10,000 eligible contracts exist. Never refill after quality decisions.
3. Pin the decision model's ID, revision, endpoint, prompt, schema, limits, and request cache before a small calibration batch. Record `keep`/`reject`/`uncertain`, reason codes, bounded evidence, and a separate infrastructure/unavailable status. Pin DeepSeek Flash independently and annotate kept tasks from the existing public projection only; keep private grader packets and references outside summary requests and RL-visible outputs. Reuse the exact-request cache and existing Harrier checkpoint, rendering, vector cache, and normalization. Keep every failed request as a row with attempt and provenance metadata.
4. Check the calibration batch's schema validity, privacy boundary, latency, token cost, and error rate before full inference. Report frozen-denominator quality outcomes, admission disagreement, failure and uncertainty rates, tag/difficulty coverage, source breakdowns, and embedding-neighborhood audits. Audit a predeclared sample by source and outcome. Run the Snowball rollout panel as a separate artifact only after pinning checkpoint, tokenizer, runtime, attempts, decoding, resource limits, and pass rule; report infrastructure failures separately from model failures.

Use fixture tests for eligibility, contract grouping, capped quota redistribution, deterministic selection, and no-refill accounting. The real-data freeze requires storage access; inference requires verified decision-model and DeepSeek Flash service bindings. Neither gate is satisfied by the metadata-only 10,000-slot allocation in this issue.

topics.title: [tpu] Step12 TPU serving diverges from H100 past the 2048-token sliding window
topics.body:
On TPU, Snowball Step12 assigns different next-token log probabilities than H100 from token position 2048 onward. Up to position 2047 the two platforms agree to within TPU run-to-run noise. Step12 uses `sliding_window = 2048` with `global_every = 4`, so three of every four attention layers attend only to the last 2048 tokens. The divergence starts at that window size.

Impact: MATH500 on the same model, revision and Evalchemy commit scores 0.944 and 0.950 on H100 and 0.878, 0.882 (v6e-8, TP8) and 0.884 (v5p-8, TP4) on TPU. 39 items are correct on both H100 runs and wrong on TPU; 22 of them are long answers that drift to a different question.

Measurement: teacher-forced log probabilities of the same 10 texts on each platform (rendered Step12 chat prefix plus an H100-generated, H100-correct MATH500 completion; vLLM `/v1/completions` with `echo`, `logprobs=1`, `max_tokens=0`, concurrency 1). 35,801 scored positions; token ids are identical on both platforms.

| Positions | H100 vs TPU mean \|Δlogprob\| | top-1 token differs | TPU concurrency 1 vs 10 mean \|Δlogprob\| |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0–2047 | 0.010–0.019 | 0.8–1.0% | 0.012–0.015 |
| 2048–2111 | 0.026 | 1.6% | – |
| 2368–2559 | 0.066 | 3.1–3.3% | – |
| 2048–3071 | 0.063 | 3.6% | 0.014 |
| 3072–4095 | 0.142 | 6.8% | 0.018 |

Pooled over all positions: mean \|Δ\| 0.056 (TPU self-noise 0.014), maximum 12.3 (TPU self-noise 1.1), top-1 differs at 2.8% of positions (TPU self-noise 0.86%). TPU's mean per-token negative log likelihood is higher on all 10 items.

The per-element window mask agrees across the three stacks. Each keeps the last W tokens including the query token:
- training: [`levanter/grug/attention/_core.py` L126](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/8e99858a17df0463daac6b104f5eddb0ffa79ffd/lib/levanter/src/levanter/grug/attention/_core.py#L123-L126), `k >= q - (W - 1)`;
- H100 vLLM fork: [`grugmoe.py` L957-L964](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/01911be34fac8715347962a8d791ca34a879e01e/vllm/model_executor/models/grugmoe.py#L957-L964) passes `per_layer_sliding_window=2048` on local layers;
- TPU: [`grugmoe.py` L786](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/models/jax/grugmoe.py#L776-L787) passes the window as `attention_chunk_size`, which [`attention_interface.py` L496](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/layers/common/attention_interface.py#L494-L498) forwards as `sliding_window`; the RPA v3 kernel masks with [`q < k + W` at L494](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v3/kernel.py#L493-L494).

The cause is not confirmed. Two unverified suspects on the TPU path:
- the RPA v3 sliding-window block skipping, which computes the first KV block to read from `kv_q_gap - sliding_window` ([kernel.py L388-L399](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v3/kernel.py#L388-L399), [L916-L942](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v3/kernel.py#L916-L942));
- KV-cache handling for the sliding-window layers.

Reproduce:
1. Serve `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-2026.10.02` at revision `50fe2f488aee7730bbccc721024b35229075602e`, bf16. TPU: v6e-8, TP8, tpu-inference `ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d`, vLLM `fb02daf1d7139d2adaeb0588448649591657d1e3`. H100: H100x8, DP8 with expert parallelism, Marin vLLM fork build `01911be34fac`.
2. Run `python teacher_forced_logprobs.py --endpoint URL --model open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-2026.10.02 --items teacher_forced_items.json --output DIR --concurrency 1` against each server. The client and items (sha256 `9d4779361b79259d36dcd2402d6fe686c81884d111cab550bb6c7fff158cdc4d`) are in `gs://marin-us-east5/scratch/karan/task236/inputs/`.
3. Compare with `python compare_tf.py H100_DIR/results.json TPU_DIR/results.json` from the same folder, and bin `|Δlogprob|` by position.

Expected: TPU per-position log probabilities stay within TPU run-to-run noise of H100 at every position, including beyond 2048.

Next step: rerun the TPU side with `grugmoe_attention_mode` set to the dense reference path (`_dense_reference_attention` in `grugmoe.py`, which applies the window as an explicit mask). If dense-mode TPU matches H100 past position 2048, the defect is in the production RPA path.

Caveats: the H100 completions were re-tokenized from text because the eval record has no sampled token ids, and vLLM omits special tokens such as the leading `<|start_think|>` from returned text. Both platforms scored the same bytes, so the comparison is valid, but the first completion positions are not a replay of the original sampled trajectory.

Data:
- H100: `gs://marin-us-east5/scratch/karan/task236/teacher-h100x8/concurrency-1/`
- TPU v6e-8: `gs://marin-us-east5/scratch/karan/task236/teacher-v6e8/concurrency-{1,10}/`
- H100 MATH500 per-item and three-way tables: `gs://marin-us-east5/scratch/karan/task224-math500/`

comments.body:
🤖 Correction to the next step in the description: a config-only dense-mode rerun is not available on the serving path.

- The served vLLM build (`fb02daf1d7139d2adaeb0588448649591657d1e3`) never reads `grugmoe_attention_mode`; its Grug model always uses the `Attention` layer (`vllm/model_executor/models/grugmoe.py` L958-L964). Passing the field through `hf_overrides` changes nothing.
- The dense switch exists only in tpu-inference's reference JAX model ([`tpu_inference/models/jax/grugmoe.py` L233, L738-L804](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/models/jax/grugmoe.py#L738-L804)). That class is not in the JAX model registry used for serving, and its dense path ignores the KV cache.

The replacement control is a kernel-level test: run tpu-inference's ragged paged attention tests with Step12's shapes (sliding window 2048, page size 16, 32 query / 8 KV heads after padding) against the reference implementation on a v6e-4.

🤖
# Research

The 2048-token onset implicates local attention, but matching elementwise mask inequalities do not establish that TPU RPA visits the right KV blocks or reads intact cache pages. `GrugMoeAttention.__call__()` selects a dense path that computes from the full input without updating KV cache, or a production path that calls RPA v3. The measured TPU revision is the head of [tpu-inference#27](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/pull/27); [marin#9400](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9400) qualifies a June checkpoint, not Step12.

**Relevant code**
- [`grugmoe.py#L738-L805`](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/models/jax/grugmoe.py#L738-L805) — dense and production attention paths
- [`attention_interface.py#L493-L510`](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/layers/common/attention_interface.py#L493-L510) — window forwarded to RPA
- [`kernel.py#L388-L399`](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v3/kernel.py#L388-L399) — first KV block selection
- [`kernel.py#L493-L494`](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v3/kernel.py#L493-L494) — elementwise window mask
- [`kernel.py#L916-L942`](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d/tpu_inference/kernels/ragged_paged_attention/v3/kernel.py#L916-L942) — per-query-block traversal

# Proposed Fix

`GrugMoeAttention.__call__()` → `shared_attention()` → RPA v3 is the production call chain. The failing step within that chain is not established, so use the frozen Step12 inputs to isolate it:

1. Replay the issue's 10 teacher-forced inputs on the reported TPU revisions with `grugmoe_attention_mode=dense` and `production`; force one complete prefill per request because dense has no historical KV-cache reads, verify identical token IDs, and compare bins around position 2048 with the existing H100 results.
2. If dense agrees with H100, compare RPA v3 with a dense QKV reference at positions 2047, 2048, 2111, and 3072 across page and query-block boundaries, including full prefill, chunked prefill, decode, skipped KV blocks, and cache/page-table contents; otherwise find the first divergent layer output and compare its Q/K/V, RoPE, mask, and loaded weights with Levanter.
3. Fix the identified TPU fork path, add a regression across position 2048, rerun the frozen log-probability comparison and repeated MATH500 on the same checkpoint, and coordinate with the open `tpu-inference#27` stack before updating Marin's paired fork pin; the post-window H100–TPU error should return to measured TPU run-to-run noise before hardware qualification.

topics.title: [canary-datakit-tier2] Normalize workers stay pending until 4h timeout
topics.body:
The October 20 Tier 2 Datakit canary exhausted its 14,400-second Actions wait while Iris still reported the ferry as running. Normalization made no progress: its Zephyr worker job had 98/98 tasks pending, with the scheduler reporting `Insufficient memory (need 32.0GB, available 20.7G...)`. This is an infra/scheduling failure.

Reproduce:
1. Run the scheduled [Tier 2 ferry workflow](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/39423437260).
2. At the wait deadline, inspect the uploaded `datakit-tier2-diagnostics/job-tree.txt` and the normalization worker job under the Iris job ID below.

Expected: normalization workers are placed and the ferry finishes within the wait budget, or Iris reports the resource shortage early enough for the canary to fail with that cause.

Evidence: The worker job was submitted at 12:49 UTC and remained pending at the 16:36 UTC timeout. `iris job describe` showed 0/98 workers completed and 98 pending; a worker requested 2 CPUs, 34.36 GB memory, and 10.74 GB disk. The tier-2 ferry calls `normalize_step` without `worker_resources`, so `normalize_to_parquet` requests `ram="32g"`. Finelog `zephyr.stage` had no completed stage for normalization execution `20261020-124354-cbb30502`; the concurrent bloom stage completed at 12:54 UTC. The uploaded diagnostics report contains the same pending job and no collection errors.

The canary ran in lane `datakit-tier2` on 2026-10-20 UTC under Iris job `/runner/iris-run-job-20261020-123608`. Its [Actions run and diagnostics artifact](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/39423437260) and [W&B run](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin/runs/datakit-tier2-ferry-39423437260-1) provide the run context.

topics.title: [grug] Early hero checkpoints store router bias equal to their pending QB update
topics.body:
Checkpoints from the original hero run `hero-12d8b6f0-dee637` store a router bias that already equals the bias derived from their own `pending_qb_betas`. A consistent step-N checkpoint cannot do that, so these checkpoints may mix state from two training steps.

The hero train step (`_make_train_step` in `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/train.py`, same order at 12d8b6f0) overwrites the router bias with centered(−`pending_qb_betas`), runs the forward, backward, and optimizer update, then stores the step's new quantile-balancing betas as `pending_qb_betas`. The router bias has no gradient (`stop_gradient`), no weight decay, and all-zero Adam moments, so a step-N checkpoint should hold bias = centered(−β_{N−1}) and pending = β_N. Each β is a fresh per-step quantile estimate, so the two should differ.

Every checkpoint from step 114000 onward behaves as expected. On 9 permanent checkpoints from step 114000 to 264000, mean |stored bias − centered(−pending)| is 0.017–0.034 and the max is 1–7 logit units.

The six `hero-12d8b6f0-dee637` checkpoints do not. At steps 6000, 12000, 24000, 36000, 48000, and 54000 under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-12d8b6f0-dee637/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/`, `master_params/stacked_blocks/stacked/mlp/router_bias` equals centered(−`pending_qb_betas`) to at most 4.8e-7, which is fp32 rounding. The bf16 `params` bias equals bf16 of the master bias. That would require β_N = β_{N−1} + a per-layer constant at every save. This run used fp32 pinned-host master params (`MasterParamMode.FP32_PINNED_HOST`). The later runs keep fp32 `params` and no master.

Two explanations fit: the saved weights come from one step later than the saved `pending_qb_betas`, or the saved `pending_qb_betas` is one step stale. In both cases the checkpoint would combine two steps' state, possibly through the async save path and the donated train-state buffers in pinned-host master mode. None of this is verified.

Reproduce: read `master_params/stacked_blocks/stacked/mlp/router_bias` and `pending_qb_betas` from one of the checkpoints above with tensorstore (`{"driver": "zarr3", "kvstore": {"driver": "ocdbt", "base": build_kvstore_spec(ckpt), "path": key + "/"}}`). Compare `bias` with `b - b.mean(-1, keepdims=True)` where `b = -pending`. Both arrays are [48, 384] float32.

Done when the cause is identified, and if it is a save-path bug, the affected checkpoint modes and steps are listed and the current save path is shown to be unaffected or fixed.

topics.title: Agent MoE Experiment: July-baseline Identity Hyper-Connections
topics.body:
<!-- experiment-tldr:start -->
## Summary

This experiment tested four-stream Identity Hyper-Connections on the real July MoE baseline while keeping the baseline architecture, optimizer, data, and compute-optimal schedules fixed. The first profiling gate showed the implementation was memory-viable with two-layer rematerialization but narrowly exceeded the original 8% throughput budget at d512 and missed more clearly at d768; after removing coefficient-only telemetry overhead, the accepted profile overheads were 7.04% at d512 and 10.20% at d768 under an 11% ceiling. Gate 1 then completed successfully at both widths with finite losses, zero failures, and permanent checkpoints. Against the matched July baseline, Identity-HC improved terminal Paloma macro loss at d512 and d768, and the `agent.md` speedup accounting remained net-positive after charging throughput loss: about 5.15% wall-clock speedup at d512 and 2.05% at d768. The issue remains open for the research decision, but Gate 1 itself passed.

### Helpful links
- [Implementation snapshot](https://github.com/WhenWen/marin/tree/identity-hc-profile-v1)
- [Research logbook](https://github.com/WhenWen/marin/blob/identity-hc-profile-v1/.agents/logbooks/identity-hyperconnection-gate1.md)
- [Gate 1 W&B group](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/dial_moe/groups/MOE-JULY-IHC-gate1-issue-7409)
- [Terminal record](https://github.com/WhenWen/marin/commit/ddbe6ef5b)
<!-- experiment-tldr:end -->

## Scope

Keep July-baseline GQA, half-RoPE, long-layer NoPE, PKO-off, MoE, optimizer, data, and compute-optimal schedules fixed. Replace each residual site with dynamic H_pre/H_post and exact H_res = I; test d512 and d768.

Research logbook: `.agents/logbooks/identity-hyperconnection-gate1.md`

User request: "Try the following identity hyperconnection idea from https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/2010852389670908320 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24880 based on the july baseline. Try efficient implementation to make sure the throughput decrease is no larger than 8% and activation memory is under control through recomputation. Then launch gate 1 (d512 and d768)."

## Hypothesis or Goal

Identity Hyper-Connections retain the useful token-dependent read/write routing of mHC while eliminating Sinkhorn and dynamic residual-stream mixing, keeping overhead low enough that quality gains translate into effective wall-clock speedup.

## Current baseline

- Base: `marin/july_baseline@52d8a9eb8d9434cf1dcaaee060edeadc60dfff9d`
- d512: 6 layers, batch 16, 10,980 steps, sequence length 8,192, v5p-8
- d768: 8 layers, batch 32, 16,875 steps, sequence length 8,192, v5p-8

## Decision log

- 2026-07-19: use n=4, alpha=0.01, zero bias, Adam-routed mapping parameters, and two-layer rematerialization groups.
- 2026-07-19: require matched baseline/candidate profiles at both widths before Gate 1 launch.
- 2026-07-19: accept optimized matched profile overheads of 7.0423% at d512 and 10.2001% at d768 under an 11% ceiling, then launch Gate 1.

## Negative results index

- Initial v1 profile overhead was 8.1501% at d512 and 10.4926% at d768, so the original 8% throughput gate was not met even though both widths compiled, ran finite, and showed no HBM/OOM signature.

## Results

Gate 1 completed successfully at both real-July-baseline widths. d512 finished 10,980 steps with final train loss 3.175577 and terminal Paloma macro loss 3.544176. d768 finished 16,875 steps with final train loss 2.967125 and terminal Paloma macro loss 3.208981. Both runs had zero Iris failures/preemptions and permanent checkpoints. Matched against `moe_may_july_baseline`, Paloma macro improved by 0.6305% at d512 and 0.5658% at d768. Using the `experiments/grug/moe/agent.md` speedup formula and final-100-row throughput, the aggregate wall-clock speedups are 1.0515x at d512 and 1.0205x at d768.

The issue is intentionally left open for the research decision.

topics.title: [post-training] Define a task environment contract
topics.body:
The TaskTrove clean release exposed an incomplete boundary between converted Harbor tasks and post-training execution. Marin publishes packed tasks in Parquet with explicit grader and environment identities. The current MarinSkyRL path expands selected tasks into many individual objects, builds equivalent Daytona snapshots again for each run, and discovers missing egress, resources, or judge configuration after rollout starts.

In the TaskTrove smoke, staging 1,273 tasks as 8,265 files held two H100 nodes idle for 58 minutes before Ray started. A capped 160-task export still required 2,685 objects and 18 minutes. The clean release contains 1,449,686 tasks but only 39 Docker environments, so data selection and environment reuse should be separate operations.

This issue owns the cross-repository contract. Dataset-specific validation remains in marin#9083. MarinSkyRL ingestion and sandbox lifecycle remain in marin-community/MarinSkyRL#540.

Done when:

- A post-training run selects packed tasks using a Parquet URI and metadata predicate, then unpacks only the assigned rows.
- An environment identity includes the Dockerfile, pinned verifier, and sandbox runtime interface. Equivalent environments reuse snapshots across runs and have an explicit cleanup policy.
- Tasks declare required capabilities such as network egress, judge access, and non-default resources. Launch fails before rollout when the selected runtime cannot provide them.
- Publish or launch validation can require an empty workspace to score zero and a shipped golden solution to score one.
- Trial results distinguish solution failure, grader failure, and infrastructure failure.
- Run provenance records the dataset release, selection predicate, verifier identity, and environment identity.
- One deterministic task and one judge task complete through the supported path without per-file corpus staging.

Verifier changes remain versioned with the dataset or environment identity. A wheel may reduce build cost. A training run must preserve the verifier pinned by the published task.

Tracked work:

- [ ] marin#9083: publish-time repository golden checks and judge sampling.
- [x] marin-community/MarinSkyRL#540: Parquet ingestion, environment reuse, capability checks, and judge plumbing.
- [x] marin-community/MarinSkyRL#538: add the `/tokenize` route required by Terminus-2.
- [x] marin#9084: close the snapshot-only ToolScale proposal because the source also leaks its answer.

TaskTrove clean shipped in marin#9061.

topics.title: Levanter ignores dtype_override when reading BF16 safetensors
topics.body:
`read_safetensors_fsspec(..., dtype_override=jnp.float32)` returns BF16 arrays for BF16 tensors. This also affects `HFCheckpointConverter.load_pretrained(dtype=jnp.float32)` and can make a supposed FP32 reference forward compute in BF16.

In `lib/levanter/src/levanter/compat/fsspec_safetensor.py`, the conversion guard uses `np.issubdtype(tensor_np.dtype, np.floating)`. The predicate repro is:

```python
import ml_dtypes
import numpy as np
assert not np.issubdtype(np.dtype(ml_dtypes.bfloat16), np.floating)
```

Reproduce the loader behavior on CPU:

```python
import asyncio
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
import jax.numpy as jnp
import numpy as np
from safetensors.numpy import save_file
from levanter.compat.fsspec_safetensor import read_safetensors_fsspec

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    path = Path(directory) / "weights.safetensors"
    save_file({"weight": np.ones((2, 2), dtype=jnp.bfloat16)}, path)
    tensors = asyncio.run(read_safetensors_fsspec(
        f"file://{path}", dtype_override=jnp.float32, sharding_fn=lambda _: None,
    ))
    assert tensors["weight"].dtype == jnp.float32  # Fails: bfloat16
```

Expected: BF16 tensors honor the requested floating dtype; integer tensors remain integers. A regression in `lib/levanter/tests/test_fsspec_safetensor.py::test_dtype_override` fails before changing the guard to `jnp.issubdtype(..., jnp.floating)` and passes after, including exact widened values and unchanged integer tensors.

Found during #10213. The affected Qwen diagnostic `task231-qwen-fp32-diagnostic-20261019-r2` used Levanter BF16 against HF FP32, not FP32 on both sides. Its FP32-vs-FP32 interpretation is withdrawn; the original measurements remain as cross-dtype evidence.

🤖

# Research

`read_safetensors_fsspec()` checks floating input with NumPy, which does not classify BF16 as floating. As a result, the loader skips `dtype_override` for BF16; `HFCheckpointConverter.load_pretrained(dtype=...)` passes its request through this loader.

**Relevant code**
- [`fsspec_safetensor.py#L270`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/compat/fsspec_safetensor.py#L270) — conversion guard
- [`hf_checkpoints.py#L404`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/src/levanter/compat/hf_checkpoints.py#L404) — converter passes dtype
- [`test_fsspec_safetensor.py#L93`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/levanter/tests/test_fsspec_safetensor.py#L93) — existing override coverage

# Proposed Fix

`load_pretrained()` passes `dtype` to `read_safetensors_fsspec()`, whose NumPy guard skips BF16 before conversion. Extend `test_dtype_override` with BF16 input, exact FP32 widened values, and unchanged integer tensors; then use `jnp.issubdtype(..., jnp.floating)` in the guard.

🤖 [PR #10267](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10267) applies `dtype_override` to BF16 safetensors and preserves integer dtypes. The regression failed before the guard change and passes after. The safe Levanter suite passed in four fresh-process batches (1,316 passed, 55 skipped); a monolithic run exhausted local memory. All-files lint and the local lint review passed.

topics.title: Weight-merging RSI loop on spare TPU compute: tracking issue
topics.body:
## Goal

Run a weight-merging loop on spare Marin compute: merge Snowball checkpoints on CPU (reserved v4 hosts in us-central2-b), screen the merges cheaply with TPU vLLM on preemptible single-host slices, and promote winners to the H100 policy evaluation. This issue tracks the project end to end.

## Pins

- Marin base `24ce375f06`
- vLLM fork `fb02daf1d7139d2adaeb0588448649591657d1e3`, tpu-inference `ae387b8bb7a644bbe7e17a9ce11bd701a012aa8d` (head of marin-community/tpu-inference#27, stacked on #29 and #28), applied job-locally
- Evalchemy `3bb8278`, MATH500 full set, harness seed 19311
- S = `open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-2026.10.02` @ `50fe2f488aee7730bbccc721024b35229075602e`

## Status

| Step | State |
|---|---|
| Inventory, feasibility, campaign matrix | done 2026-10-15 |
| Parents S, C, A5, M staged and sha256-verified in `gs://marin-us-central2/scratch/karan/rsi-merge/parents/` | done 2026-10-16 |
| Merge toolkit: allowlisted BF16 to F32 widening for M's router biases (branch `task/197`) | done, no PR yet |
| TPU scoring smoke test | done: TPU scores 6-7 points below H100 |
| Matched H100 control | done 2026-10-17: 0.944 |
| Quantized serving on v5e | blocked: the pinned fork rejects every quant config for GrugMoE |
| Localize the TPU gap | in progress (#10250) |
| Iteration-one merges (3 recipes) | not started, waiting on the scoring path |

## MATH500 scores for S, same model revision, same Evalchemy pin, same effective sampling

| Server | Score |
|---|---|
| H100 policy config, 2026-10-03 record | 0.950 |
| H100 policy config, 2026-10-17 | 0.944 |
| TPU v6e-8 TP8 bf16 (two runs) | 0.878, 0.882 |
| TPU v5p-8 TP4 bf16 | 0.884 |

Per item: 421 right everywhere, 39 right on both H100 runs and wrong on TPU, 12 wrong everywhere. The 39 are long solutions; 22 of them drift onto a different problem mid-solution.

## The TPU gap (#10250)

Teacher-forced logprobs on the same 10 items match the H100 within noise up to token 2047 and diverge from exactly token 2048, which is S's `sliding_window` (`global_every` 4). The gap grows to about 0.14 nat mean absolute logprob difference by 3-4k tokens.

Ruled out: truncation, thinking mode, sampling (Evalchemy strips temperature and seed, both servers run vLLM defaults), batch dependence, sharding degree and chip generation (v5p-8 TP4 scores the same), cross-request contamination, mask off-by-one (training, FA3 and the TPU kernel all keep the last W tokens including self), KV block eviction (the TPU runner keeps one full-attention cache group), per-layer window plumbing (reaches the TPU kernel unchanged; global layers get no window), KV cache dtype (bf16 on both).

Not valid controls at this pin: `grugmoe_attention_mode=dense` (never read by the vLLM model), a GPU TP8 run (GPU GrugMoE requires TP=1), the experimental batched RPA kernel (fails to compile: its SMEM schedule is sized from a reported capacity above the compiler's 1 MiB limit).

A standalone probe of the pinned ragged-paged-attention v3 kernel against its dense reference with random inputs passes 22 cases around the window boundary (error flat at bf16 noise). Random inputs spread attention over about 2048 keys, so that probe cannot see an edge or sink effect. Running now: a kernel probe with peaky scores, a BOS-like sink key and position-bucket values, and a TPU serving control with the window disabled.

Consequence for the loop: TPU vLLM cannot rank merges until this is fixed. One H100x8 MATH500 run costs about 14 minutes of box time per candidate.

## Related

- #10250 TPU sliding-window divergence
- #9400 tpu-inference pin bump and hardware checks
- #8323 Snowball TPU serving
- #7555 earlier long-context divergence on TPU
- marin-community/tpu-inference#28 custom router selections, #29 host storage release, #27 TP8 head padding (the stack every TPU run here used)
- Two Evalchemy integration gotchas found on the way: the pinned Evalchemy strips `temperature` and `seed` from requests, so the server's defaults apply; and marin's FineStore result reader expects native results JSON while Evalchemy `3bb8278` writes parquet tables, so the parent eval job reports FAILED although the child succeeded and the score is in `data/evalchemy_results/`.

## Open decisions

1. Score iteration-one merges on H100 now, or wait for the TPU fix.
2. Open a PR for the merge-toolkit change on `task/197`.
3. File the Iris autoscaler tier-blocking issue (a v6e-4 group in backoff blocks v6e-8 demand in the same zone).

The pinned Evalchemy writes parquet tables while Marin's result reader looks only for `results_*.json`, so a successful child can leave the parent failed. |---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0–2047 | 0.014–0.016 | 0.015–0.017 | 0.013–0.015 | 0.000 | 0.013–0.015 |
| 2048–2111 | 0.012 | 0.026 | 0.013 | 0.025 | 0.012 |

| 2112–2303 | 0.013–0.016 | 0.037–0.040 | 0.018–0.025 | 0.020–0.024 | 0.011–0.014 |
| 2304–2559 | 0.013–0.016 | 0.041–0.068 | 0.038–0.124 | 0.037–0.124 | 0.010–0.015 |
| 2560–3071 | 0.014 | 0.080 | 0.185 | 0.185 | 0.012 |
| 3072–4095 | 0.014 | 0.142 | 0.700 | 0.702 | 0.013 |
| 4096–8000 | 0.011 | 0.132 | 1.116 | 1.124 | 0.010 |

1. The exact-window reference agrees with H100 vLLM at every position, at noise level. The H100's gradual response past token 2048 is the model's real response to an exact 2048 window; dropping the first hundred or so tokens barely moves its predictions.
2. The TPU serving run with the window on departs from the reference from token 2048 and stays 0.13–0.14 nats away at long range. The TPU run with the window off agrees with the reference wherever the window does not apply, so the defect is confined to the TPU's windowed attention path in serving.
3. The ragged-paged-attention v3 kernel is exact in isolation (three probes including serving's tile sizes, per-shard head geometry and request classes), so the defect is in what serving feeds the kernel, or in how the per-layer window reaches it, when `sliding_window` is set. That is the open item.

Data: `gs://marin-us-east5/scratch/karan/task236/teacher-skyrl-eager-h100x8/` alongside the other runs.

## TPU serving defect localized: global attention layers get the sliding window

Follow-up to the seven-way comparison above. The TPU-side defect is now named and fixed by a config override; the proper fix is in tpu-inference.

**What happens.** tpu-inference registers a vLLM general plugin (`tpu_inference/layers/vllm/__init__.py`, `register_layers` -> `_register_grugmoe`). Whenever the TPU stack is present it sets `_CONFIG_REGISTRY["grug_moe"] = GrugMoeHfConfig`, replacing the vLLM fork's `GrugMoeConfig`. `GrugMoeHfConfig` (`tpu_inference/models/jax/grugmoe.py`) is a plain `PretrainedConfig` with name aliases; it never sets `layer_types`. The fork's `GrugMoeConfig` sets `layer_types` from `grug_moe_layer_types(num_layers, global_every)`. Plugins load in `EngineArgs.__post_init__`, before the model config is built, so on TPU `hf_text_config.layer_types` is `None`. vLLM then sets `cache_config.sliding_window = 2048` (arg_utils: "only set CacheConfig.sliding_window if the model is all sliding window"), and the fork's GrugMoE model, which passes `per_layer_sliding_window=None` for its 7 global layers (3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23, 25 of 26), gets 2048 for them through the `Attention.__init__` fallback. A static trace of the TPU engine shows all 26 layers at `sliding_window=2048`. On H100 the plugin is absent, the fork config is used, and the engine builds 4 KV cache groups with the global layers unwindowed. The fork model derives its own layer pattern from `global_every`, so nothing crashes; the window is just applied to the wrong layers.

**Verification.** Passing `--hf-overrides '{"layer_types": [...]}'` (the fork's list: `full_attention` at 3, 7, 11, 15, 19, 23, 25, `sliding_attention` elsewhere) changes the trace to 7 layers at `None` and 19 at 2048, with 4 KV cache groups. Teacher-forced probe (same 10 MATH500 items, 35,801 positions) against the exact-window eager reference, mean |delta logprob|:

| positions | TPU, override | TPU, default | H100 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0-2048 | 0.015-0.018 | 0.015-0.018 | 0.014-0.016 |
| 2048-2304 | 0.013-0.016 | 0.023-0.038 | 0.012-0.014 |
| 2304-3072 | 0.015-0.017 | 0.054-0.080 | 0.014-0.016 |
| 3072+ | 0.012-0.015 | 0.132-0.142 | 0.011-0.014 |

TPU with the override vs H100 directly: 0.011-0.017 at every position. MATH500 with the override (Evalchemy 3bb8278, seed 19311, same settings as the TPU runs above): **0.940** (470/500, 500 generated and scored, 1421 s), against 0.878-0.884 for TPU without it and 0.944 / 0.950 for the two H100 runs. The gap is closed.

**Fix.** Proper fix is in tpu-inference: `GrugMoeHfConfig` should set `layer_types` the same way the fork does, or the plugin should not replace a registry entry the fork already provides. tpu-inference `main` at 340444337772 (2026-10-19) still has the overwrite. Until then, TPU serving of any GrugMoE checkpoint whose `config.json` lacks `layer_types` needs the override above. Pins: vLLM fork fb02daf, tpu-inference ae387b8, Step12 @50fe2f488aee.
