topics.title: [tasks] Ingest native structural closure tasks
topics.body:
Import Snowball tasks that complete a supplied assistant prefix to match a reference JSON or delimited structure. Register pinned training and development-evaluation splits through the existing curation catalog. The converter uses curation row IDs and retains original identities in audit metadata.

Use a generic PrefillHarness selected explicitly by TaskRolloutSpec.harness. It continues the final assistant text once, can advertise final tool schemas, and rejects interactive tools and parsed reasoning or tool-call responses. Ordinary chat and tool-loop rendering retain their existing behavior. The serving model chooses its tokenizer; source token IDs remain provenance and rollout traces retain actual model tokens.

Private verifier resources remain byte-identical and stay out of model requests. A correct first closed outer region scores one even when later output follows. Historical terminal-marker normalization stays outside the semantic grader. The changed converter uses a fresh recipe version.

The 341 focused regression tests, mechanical lint, library type checks and documentation-link checks pass. One case-sensitive filesystem check was excluded on macOS. GPU inference for the revised harness has not been validated.

The [trainer companion](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/1032) needs explicit PrefillHarness selection, genuine shared-library releases and a real lock update.

Part of #10314.
topics.head: 543f7d7d4b22c0bc040b2a335337506cfa038486

comments.body: 🤖 Removed the local validation paragraph from the PR description. Local checks: 214 safe engine tests and 5 focused converter/grader cases passed; the repository type baseline reports 0 errors. Full affected-suite collection is blocked on this Mac by the existing Linux-only `bubblewrap_bin` import. The broader Verifyit plugin-test failure also reproduces on clean main `5ec80e7` with identical grader and test files. Linux CI remains the full-suite validation path.

🤖 Review of dde5d25: two blockers and two should-fix findings in the shared prefill path. I reproduced each one locally at this head with fake models; no GPU path has run.

**Blockers**

**1. A prefill task with tools sends a wrong second request.** `completion_request` puts `extra_body={"continue_final_message": True, "add_generation_prompt": False}` in the request ([submission.py:186-192](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dde5d253555367c816aa4eef095c3236b6c97d54/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/submission.py#L186-L192)). `task_prompt` copies it into `Prompt.options` ([shell.py:103](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dde5d253555367c816aa4eef095c3236b6c97d54/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/harness/shell.py#L103)). The recorder sends the first prompt's options with every request of the conversation ([recorder.py:80-98](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dde5d253555367c816aa4eef095c3236b6c97d54/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/recorder.py#L80-L98)). After a tool call, the last message is the tool result, and the request still tells the server to continue the final message. Run with `ReplayModel`, a prefilled `arithmetic_task` and one provider tool:

```
request 0: roles=['user', 'user', 'assistant']                      extra_body={'continue_final_message': True, 'add_generation_prompt': False}
request 1: roles=['user', 'user', 'assistant', 'assistant', 'tool']  extra_body={'continue_final_message': True, 'add_generation_prompt': False}
```

With a ChatML template, `transformers.utils.chat_template_utils.render_jinja_template`, which vLLM uses for this flag, ends request 1 inside the tool message: `...<|im_start|>tool\n{"attempts": 1}`. There is no assistant header, so the model continues the tool output, and that text is graded with no error. The new [task-rollouts.md:117](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dde5d253555367c816aa4eef095c3236b6c97d54/docs/references/task-rollouts.md#L117) says "Tasks with tools use its normal tool loop". The Snowball rows have no tools, so this source is not affected; the next prefill task with a tool is. Fix: reject a prefill when the prompt has tools and correct the doc, or send the flags with the first request only.

**2. A correct continuation can get a normal reward of 0.** With a vLLM reasoning parser, `continue_final_message` can return the continued answer under `reasoning`. [taskforge/llm/policy.py:19-21](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dde5d253555367c816aa4eef095c3236b6c97d54/lib/taskforge/src/taskforge/llm/policy.py#L19-L21) records this for GLM-5.3. `ChatModel` keeps `content` and `reasoning_content` apart ([chat.py:58-62](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dde5d253555367c816aa4eef095c3236b6c97d54/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/chat.py#L58-L62)). `grade_answer` then grades the empty content: `StructureClosureSpec` defaults to `EmptyOutputPolicy.GRADE` ([spec.py:164](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dde5d253555367c816aa4eef095c3236b6c97d54/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/spec.py#L164)), so `_gradeable_empty_text` accepts `""` as the candidate ([grading.py:119-143](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dde5d253555367c816aa4eef095c3236b6c97d54/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/grading.py#L119-L143)). Three fake replies to the prefix `{"x":` through `RolloutEngine` and `ShellHarness`:

```
correct, returned in content    -> status=graded  reward=1.0  failure=None
correct, returned as reasoning  -> status=graded  reward=0.0  failure=None
wrong answer                    -> status=graded  reward=0.0  failure=None
```

The trainer cannot tell rows 2 and 3 apart. It would push the policy away from correct answers, and the 243-row validation split would score near 0. The PR does not say whether the training server runs a reasoning parser. If it does not, this does not occur. Fix: after a prefill, treat an empty `content` with non-empty `reasoning_content` as a failed attempt (for example `RolloutContractError`), so that the trainer drops it. Also run the validation split on the real serving stack before training.

**Should fix**

**3. `terminal_markers` never changes the reward.** The reward is `score.success` ([grade_structure_closure.py:45](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dde5d253555367c816aa4eef095c3236b6c97d54/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/modes/grade_structure_closure.py#L45)). `score_closure_region` computes it from the first closed region only ([closure_scoring.py:129-130](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dde5d253555367c816aa4eef095c3236b6c97d54/lib/verifyit/src/verifyit/closure_scoring.py#L129-L130)). Text after that region, marker or not, sets only `trailing_content`. The replies `1}`, `1}<|eot_id|>`, `1}<|im_end|>` and `1} and more text` all get reward 1.0. Only `trailing_content` differs, and it is wrong for `<|im_end|>`. The field writes Llama 3 end tokens into the grader, and so into the fingerprint, of all 57,607 imported tasks. This conflicts with the body's statement "The serving model chooses its tokenizer". The markers come from MarinSkyRL's `ClosureReplaySession`, which serves with `skip_special_tokens: False`. This text path uses vLLM's default, which removes special tokens. Fix: remove the field, its validator branch, the special case in `grade_answer` ([grading.py:144-148](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dde5d253555367c816aa4eef095c3236b6c97d54/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/grading.py#L144-L148)), the converter parameter and `TERMINAL_MARKERS`.

**4. The prefill is inferred from the role of the last message** ([submission.py:186](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/dde5d253555367c816aa4eef095c3236b6c97d54/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/submission.py#L186)). On main, a context that ends with a finished assistant reply gets the instruction at the end and a new reply. With this PR it is continued, and the instruction moves before the reply. `completion_request` on `user: "Tell me a fact about six."`, `assistant: "Six is the smallest perfect number."` returns `continue_final_message=True`. No current converter makes such contexts. But the task does not record the intent, and `ConversationInput` cannot reject a prefill with tools (finding 1). Fix: an explicit `AssistantPrefill` event that is allowed only as the last event, or the separate harness in the next comment, which removes the rule from the shared renderer.

🤖 A design to consider in place of the shared-renderer prefill: one harness for prefill tasks, selected by name.

Rolloutengine selects the harness of each rollout by name (`TaskRolloutSpec.harness`). MarinSkyRL already routes these rows by name: they carry `session.task_session: "structure_closure"`, and `episode_factories` maps that name to `ClosureReplaySession` ([skyrl_gym/task_factories.py:128](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/82396a73a31e776229f3240c3af2b50ad53c4336/skyrl-gym/skyrl_gym/task_factories.py#L128)). A text-prefill harness in rolloutengine keeps that routing and leaves `completion_request` and `ShellHarness` as they are on main. Sketch, not run:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PrefillHarness:
    """One reply that continues the task's final assistant message."""

    def check(self, task: TaskSpec, limits: RolloutLimits) -> None:
        last = task.context.events[-1]
        if not (isinstance(last, TextMessage) and last.role == "assistant"):
            raise ValueError("A prefill task must end with an assistant text message")
        if task.final_tools or task.interaction_tools or task.environment_requirements.tool_providers:
            raise ValueError("A prefill task cannot have tools")

    async def run(self, context: HarnessContext, session: ModelSession) -> None:
        messages = conversation_messages(context.task.context.events)
        options = {"extra_body": {"continue_final_message": True, "add_generation_prompt": False}}
        turn = await session.start(Prompt(tuple(messages), options))
        if not turn.message.get("content") and turn.message.get("reasoning_content"):
            raise RolloutContractError("The continuation came back as reasoning; check the server's reasoning parser")
        session.record()
```

Effect on this PR:

- `completion_request`, `chat_request` and `ShellHarness.task_prompt` return to their main versions. The taskcompendium README and `task-rollouts.md` need no new contract for contexts that end with an assistant message, and the prefill tests in `test_schema.py`, `test_chat.py` and `test_rollout.py` become one harness test.
- `check()` rejects tools before any machine starts (finding 1). The shared renderer infers nothing (finding 4). The harness knows that its prompt is a prefill, so it can do the reasoning check (finding 2).
- The converter, the `structure_closure` verifyit mode, in-process grading, controls, the deduplication key and the catalog source do not change.

Cost: the catalog writes a `TaskSpec` with no harness name, so the step that writes the training rollout specs must set this harness for the two Snowball sources. MarinSkyRL already does this for every session that is not the shell harness. The body says that "no new harness is required". The harness above is about 20 lines, and it keeps one task family's request format out of the contract that every `TaskSpec` uses.

🤖 Implemented the explicit PrefillHarness in 543f7d7d4b. Ordinary chat and tool-loop rendering are restored; continuation is a separate one-turn choice. It allows advertised final tool schemas for the paired probes, rejects interactive tools and parsed reasoning/tool-call channels, and removes historical terminal markers from the semantic grader. The evaluator and ToolHarness rename are updated in the stack. The combined CPU regression suite passes 428 tests; live model validation remains outstanding.

topics.title: [grug] Honor dynamic attention bounds in reference backends
topics.body:
Honor the per-query bounds that the hero layer scan uses to select local attention windows in the reference and XLA attention backends. These backends previously ignored the bounds and silently evaluated local layers with full-causal attention.

Zero outputs for fully masked padding queries and reject precomputed bounds in Splash, which does not support them. Scan regressions compare outputs and Q/K/V gradients across local windows, packed segments, and padding. The XLA fallback materializes a dense mask; the active FA4 kernels are unchanged.

topics.title: [inference] Eval runner keeps a stale serve endpoint after the serve job is preempted
topics.body:
When an Iris serve job started by `marin.inference.iris.remote_inference` (`lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris.py`, `_start_direct_inference` / `_wait_for_endpoint`) is preempted by Kueue and its retry attempt registers a new endpoint on another host, the running evaluation keeps the first host:port it resolved. The Evalchemy chat client then loops on `ClientConnectorError` / `ReadTimeout` (or gets HTTP 404 from whatever now listens on that address) until the group's timeout or a manual cancel. The serve job itself is fine; only the client is stale.

Observed in marin #9920 and #9984 on cw-rno2a, 2026-10-09/10: nine evaluation groups lost this way (examples: `/karan/eval-20261009-030945-gate-rs-sft-lr1e-06-step375-5e80`, serve child `inference-553ee1e1…` preempted 6× and re-registered on 10.168.194.211 at 04:25 UTC while the eval kept 10.168.192.27:10241; `/karan/eval-20261010-030426-gate-merge-ta-a1.0-b1.0-gpqa28k-152a`, 188 logged requests answered 404 by the old address). Each costs the serve's partial GPU time plus a full relaunch; several evals ran 16–20 h before being noticed.

Expected: the client re-resolves the endpoint from the Iris registry when requests fail with connection errors (and periodically), and fails fast with a clear error when the serve job reaches a terminal state instead of retrying forever.

Done when: an eval whose serve is preempted and re-registered elsewhere continues against the new address, and an eval whose serve job dies fails within a bounded time with the serve job's state in the error.

comments.body:
🤖
# Research

Evalchemy launches with direct routing, and the orchestrator resolves the serve endpoint once before putting that pod address in the child job's config. The child keeps using that address while `eval_job.wait(timeout=inf)` blocks; serve health is checked only before and after the evaluation. [PR #9480](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9480) chose direct routing after 7,734 hub and 10,749 peer proxy 502s in five minutes, so the recovery path must preserve direct connection reuse.

**Relevant code**
- [`launch.py#L195`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7405c96fe6ea3675d5a1bf7977d406cfc3887243/experiments/evaluation/launch.py#L195) — selects direct Evalchemy routing
- [`runner.py#L352-L363`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7405c96fe6ea3675d5a1bf7977d406cfc3887243/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/runner.py#L352-L363) — resolves before evaluation
- [`runner.py#L602-L609`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7405c96fe6ea3675d5a1bf7977d406cfc3887243/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/runner.py#L602-L609) — turns registry entry into a fixed URL
- [`evalchemy/runner.py#L223-L233`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7405c96fe6ea3675d5a1bf7977d406cfc3887243/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evalchemy/runner.py#L223-L233) — serializes the URL into the child
- [`evalchemy/runner.py#L327`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7405c96fe6ea3675d5a1bf7977d406cfc3887243/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evalchemy/runner.py#L327) — waits without checking serve state

# Proposed Fix

1. Pass the endpoint name and serve job IDs to the Evalchemy child. Point Evalchemy at a loopback HTTP forwarder in that child; the forwarder uses a pooled connection to the current direct Iris endpoint and preserves streaming responses.
2. Refresh the registry address periodically and immediately after connection errors, timeouts, or a 404. Replace the upstream pool when the address changes, retry requests that have not started a response, and wait through a live job's preemption; propagate a 404 from an unchanged current address.
3. Poll serve status while the parent waits for the Evalchemy job. On a terminal serve state, cancel the evaluator and record `INFRA_FAILED` with the serve job ID and state within one poll interval; update both evaluation call paths to pass the inference session.
4. Cover address replacement, a stale-address 404, streaming interruption, recovery with no registered endpoint, and terminal serve state using local HTTP servers and a fake registry. Compare request failures and latency at Evalchemy's default concurrency before replacing direct routing.

topics.title: [levanter] Vectorize FA4 SM100 segment mask and zero accumulators in prep
topics.body:
This PR changes two parts of the SM100 FA4 kernels. The forward evaluates the document segment mask 32 columns at a time. The backward zeroes its fp32 accumulators the same way as upstream FA4 and no longer launches scalar zero-fill kernels. Before this change, the forward for document-masked local attention at hero shapes was about 1.7x slower than upstream FA4 varlen. Now the forward is within 5% of upstream.

The vectorized mask_mod builds keep-bitmasks with `r2p_bitmask_below` and `r2p_bitmask_above`. Its output is bitwise equal to the output of the scalar mask. In the backward, the preprocess kernel clears the dQ accumulator while it computes the row dot products. dK and dV start from an XLA zeros buffer that the kernel receives through `input_output_aliases`. Callers give the aliases to `cutlass_call` as a tuple of pairs, because the kernel cache key must be hashable. `cutlass_call` converts them to the dict that `cutlass.jax` expects. SM90 and SM120 keep the current zero-fill path.

Kernel measurements on one GB200 at hero shapes (median 16K rows):

| Metric | Before | After | Upstream varlen |
|---|---|---|---|
| Local-layer forward | 3.16 ms | 1.96 ms | 1.87 ms |
| Local-layer fwd+bwd | 10.23 ms | 8.97 ms | |
| Projected attention cost | 0.777 s/step | 0.672 s/step | |

Output, dq, dk and dv match an fp32 reference with the same relative error as before. That error is 2.0e-3 to 2.6e-3, which is the bf16 rounding floor. The FA4 test file passes on GPU.

The end-to-end test ran on one GB200 NVL72 rack, restored from hero step 240000. At 16K context, the step time goes from 13.055 to 12.956 s/step (+0.76% tokens/s). The loss stays inside same-code noise, and the drop fraction does not change. A rank-0 trace shows that the attention kernels are 0.23 s/step faster. Peak memory increases by 0.5 GB because of the aliased dK/dV buffers.

The remaining gap to upstream is about 0.035 s/step, and it is in the backward. This backward uses 1-CTA with the scalar mask. The upstream backward uses 2-CTA.

topics.title: [datakit] Release the shared Zephyr pool after its last stage
topics.body:
Release the shared Zephyr pool when its last stage succeeds, so idle shared workers stop holding hosts needed by dedicated pools. `run_reference_steps` runs normalization before starting the shared pool; a watcher thread calls `ZephyrContext.shutdown()` after every step in `DatakitSteps.shared_pool_steps` succeeds. `ZephyrDatakitSteps` and `DecontaminationSteps` each list the stages that receive the shared context. If the watcher's status check raises, the run fails with that error. All three ferries use this path through `run_reference_ferry`, as does `reference_pipeline.py --target all`. The shared pool uses `_IdleWorkerPolicy.RETAIN`, so it previously kept every acquired worker until the DAG ended: up to 512 workers (2 CPU / 16 GiB each) on v5e hosts, while the embed, quality, fuzzy-cluster, and store pools waited for hosts.

Reduce the tier-1 store worker from 4 CPU / 32 GiB RAM / 64 GiB disk to 2 CPU / 8 GiB RAM / 16 GiB disk. A store task with one normalized shard peaks below 2 GiB RAM and spills below 1 GiB. On 2026-10-12, the old shape received 1 of 106 workers; the new shape received 12 workers in 1 minute.

On the fixed code, tier 1 (`/rav/iris-run-job-20261012-153556`) succeeded in 56 minutes. Tier 3 (`/rav/iris-run-job-20261012-153605`) succeeded, and its shared pool stopped at 19:30 UTC after fuzzy dedup. Tier 3 took 5h47m, exceeding the 20,700-second CI wait. On a busy cluster, the shared pool received only 275 of its 512 workers, and tokenization took 2h37m, compared with 37 minutes on 2026-10-05.

The tier-3 fuzzy-cluster workers drop from 16 CPU / 128 GiB / 64 GiB disk to 8 CPU / 64 GiB / 32 GiB, with 64 instead of 32 workers, so the task count stays at 512. Only one of the larger workers fits on a v5e host. On 2026-10-13 the verify workers waited 3h46m for hosts, and the tier-3 ferry took 7h30m. At 16 tasks per worker, cluster text peaked at 66 GiB and verify at 26 GiB.

The three tiers passed in CI on this branch. Tier 1 took 56 minutes, and tier 2 took 1h51m. Tier 3 (`/runner/iris-run-job-20261013-165715`) took 2h25m, with 36 minutes for fuzzy verification. This is much less than the 20,700-second CI wait.

The tier concurrency groups now include `github.ref`, so a run started on a branch and the scheduled run on main do not cancel each other.

Fixes https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10047. Part of https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10059.

<details><summary>Original description</summary>

```markdown
* fixes https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10047
* part of https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10059
* stop the shared Zephyr pool when its last stage succeeds, so that idle shared workers do not hold the hosts that the dedicated pools need
* add `run_reference_steps`: it runs the normalize steps first, then starts the shared pool, and a watcher thread calls `ZephyrContext.shutdown()` when every step in `DatakitSteps.shared_pool_steps` succeeds [^1]
  * all 3 ferries use it through `run_reference_ferry`, and so does `reference_pipeline.py --target all`
* tier-1 store worker: 4 cpu / 32g / 64g → 2 cpu / 8g / 16g
  * one normalized shard per store task peaks below 2 GiB RAM and spills below 1 GiB
  * on 2026-10-12 the old shape got 1 of 106 workers, the new shape got 12 workers in 1 min
* validation runs on the fixed code:
  * tier 1 (`/rav/iris-run-job-20261012-153556`) succeeded in 56 min
  * tier 3 (`/rav/iris-run-job-20261012-153605`) succeeded, and the shared pool stopped at 19:30 UTC, after fuzzy dedup [^2]

[^1]: the shared pool uses `_IdleWorkerPolicy.RETAIN`, so it keeps every worker that it gets until it stops. Before this change it held up to 512 workers (2 cpu / 16g each) on the v5e hosts until the end of the DAG, and the embed, quality, fuzzy-cluster and store pools waited for hosts.
[^2]: tier 3 took 5h47m, which is longer than the 20,700 s CI wait. The shared pool got only 275 of its 512 workers on a busy cluster, and tokenize took 2h37m against 37m on 2026-10-05. Thus #10059 stays open for the capacity part.

```

</details>
🤖 Changed the title to `[datakit] Release the shared Zephyr pool after its last stage` and removed the `---` footer from the body.

🤖 Holistic review of 781c86817111af521068d874daae8aace3f99fc0.

The PR starts the shared Zephyr pool after the normalize steps and stops it once every shared-pool stage succeeds. It also shrinks the tier-1 store and tier-3 fuzzy-cluster workers and scopes the canary concurrency groups by ref. The design fits the existing `ZephyrContext` lifecycle: `shutdown()` is idempotent, and a later `execute()` raises `Cannot execute with a closed ZephyrContext`. `test_shared_pool_is_held_only_between_normalize_and_its_last_stage` passes locally and checks the ordering this PR depends on. Nothing blocks merging.

**Should fix**
1. `experiments/datakit/reference_pipeline.py:1147` `shared_pool_steps` is a second, hand-written list of the steps that `zephyr_datakit_steps` and `decontamination_steps` built with `zephyr_context`. The list is complete today. A future stage that gets `zephyr_context=zephyr_context` but is left off this list will run after the release and fail with `Cannot execute with a closed ZephyrContext`, hours into a tier-3 ferry. Fix: have each builder return its own list, for example a `shared_pool_steps` property on `ZephyrDatakitSteps` (exact_dedup, tokenize, minhash, fuzzy_dedup) and on `DecontaminationSteps` (bloom, drop_sets, marks), and set `shared_pool_steps=zephyr_steps.shared_pool_steps + decontamination.shared_pool_steps`. The membership then lives next to the code that passes in the context.
2. `experiments/datakit/reference_pipeline.py:1210` If `step_is_built` raises inside `_release_shared_pool`, for example on a transient object-store error reading a `StatusFile`, the daemon thread exits. `threading.excepthook` prints the traceback to stderr, `watcher.join()` returns normally, and the pool keeps its workers until the DAG ends. That is the #10047 behavior again, and no failure is reported. Fix: submit the watcher through a `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)` and call `future.result()` after `stop.set()`, so the exception reaches the caller. Alternatively, catch the error, log it, and retry on the next poll.

**Claims versus evidence**
3. PR body, "Fixes #10059": the first draft kept #10059 open for capacity, because one tier-3 run on a busy cluster took 5h47m and tokenization alone took 2h37m. The upgrade to "Fixes" rests on a single 2h25m CI run (`/runner/iris-run-job-20261013-165715`). The fuzzy-worker change fixes the 128 GiB placement failure that #10059 records. A busy cluster can still push the tier-3 ferry past 20,700 s, because the shared pool still requests 512 workers. Fix: change the body to "Part of #10059", or cite a second tier-3 pass under load before closing the issue.

**Related PRs**
4. #10108 also edits `experiments/datakit/reference_pipeline.py`, but only the embed and centroid `pip_dependency_groups`. It is independent of this change, and the two can merge in either order.

2. The watcher now runs in a `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=1)`. After `stop.set()`, `run_reference_steps` calls `future.result()`, so an error in the status check fails the run. The new test `test_failed_pool_release_check_fails_the_run` covers this. It fails on the previous code.

topics.title: Pre-registering Snowball post-distillation SWE-bench pass@1
topics.body: Our aim is to predict the SWE-bench pass@1 of the final Snowball 9.97T base model after distilling on 2B tokens of SWE-smith trajectories generated by Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. We take the Snowball 3k, 9k, 18k, and 39k [intermediate checkpoints](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/snowball-intermediate) and [Grug](https://huggingface.co/penfever/grug-67b-a2b-sft-s1-wildchat-step257), and SFT them on [2B tokens](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nanoswe/swesmith-qwen3.6-35b-a3b) generated by a lightly fine-tuned variant of [Qwen3.6-35B-A3B](https://huggingface.co/nanoswe/qwen-3.6-35b-a3b-teacher) against the [SWE-smith](https://huggingface.co/datasets/SWE-bench/SWE-smith) problem set. We SFT the Snowball checkpoints at 0.21B and 0.64B token budgets, and Grug additionally at 0.37B, 1.1B, and 1.9B budgets. We evaluate the bpb of all fine-tunes on 1.3k SWE-smith trajectories generated by the teacher model. We also evaluate the pass@1 of the Grug fine-tunes. We fit two scaling laws, one relating pre-training steps and SFT budget to bpb, and a second relating bpb to pass@1. We obtain a final prediction of 33% pass@1 for the 9.97T Snowball checkpoint fine-tuned on our SFT dataset. ## Predicting bpb on teacher trajectories We use a multiplicative law. In ongoing work using pre-training checkpoints trained under constant LR (SmolLM3), we found the following law to work well: ```math \text{bpb} = E \left(1 + A\, D_{\text{pre}}^{-\alpha}\right) \left(1 + B\, D_{\text{sft}}^{-\beta}\right) ``` To account for the LR schedule of Snowball, we use the approach of [Scaling Law with Learning Rate Annealing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.11029) to model both the Grug anneal and the Snowball anneal. We thus turn $`1 + A\, D_{\text{pre}}^{-\alpha}`$ into ```math 1 + A\, S_1^{-\alpha} - C\, S_2 ``` where $`S_1 = 10^{-4} \sum_i \eta_i / \eta_{\text{peak}}`$ is the LR area over pre-training optimizer steps (proportional to $`D_{\text{pre}}`$ at constant LR, warmup counted at peak), and $`S_2 = 10^{-3} \sum_i m_i`$ is the annealing area, with momentum $`m_i = \lambda\, m_{i-1} + (\eta_{i-1} - \eta_i) / \eta_{\text{peak}}`$, $`\lambda = 0.999`$ (as in Tissue et al.), and $`\eta_{\text{peak}} = 5.28 \times 10^{-3}`$. The full law is ```math \text{bpb} = E \left(1 + A\, S_1^{-\alpha} - C\, S_2\right) \left(1 + B\, D_{\text{sft}}^{-\beta}\right) ``` with $`D_{\text{sft}}`$ in billions of tokens. We fit the six coefficients on our 13 datapoints using least squares, obtaining $`E = 0.0538,\ A = 0.278,\ \alpha = 0.783,\ C = 0.124,\ B = 0.260,\ \beta = 0.306`$, and a df-adjusted RMSE of 0.000441 bpb. Extrapolating to 9.97T pre-training tokens at 1.93B SFT tokens, we predict 0.0635 bpb. It is unclear whether calibrating the law on the much shorter Grug cooldown will extrapolate to the cooldown of Snowball. ## From bpb to pass@1 We fit the following law: ```math \log \text{pass@1} = a - b \cdot \text{bpb} ``` We fit the law using OLS on the five Grug SFTs, obtaining $`a = 5.98`$ and $`b = 39.1`$ (i.e., $`\text{pass@1} = 397\, e^{-39.1 \cdot \text{bpb}}`$), and extrapolate to the bpb predicted by the previous law, resulting in a predicted pass@1 of 33%. The 95% CI on the mean at the forecast is large: 29.3% to 37.5% pass@1. Our hunch is that the 33% prediction might be slightly conservative: fitting the law on only the three largest SFT budgets instead predicts 35%. ## Conclusion Our laws predict that fine-tuning the final Snowball checkpoint on our 2B Qwen3.6-35B-A3B dataset will result in a SWE-bench pass@1 of **33%**. If anything we expect to err low, and would not be surprised by 35%.

comments.body: Nice work @RicardoDominguez !

**Update (Lightning SFT data).** We now fine-tune on SWE-smith trajectories generated by Nemotron 3.5 Lightning instead of Qwen 3.6. This is a separate prediction from the 33% above, which used Qwen 3.6 data and a different eval harness. We pre-register a new prediction for the final Snowball base model, as released by Marin, fine-tuned on **7.55B Lightning tokens** with the recipe of our Grug Lightning ladder (3,600 steps, 32k context). We evaluate on SWE-bench Verified (483 instances, 5 attempts each).

![Snowball Lightning forecast](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/rdolmedo/2ad458a02acae99b551f3739fa16834c/raw/e68176824598a2884c5b4fa02689f56094e3f0ac/forecast.png)

**Loss.** We predict **0.1334 bpb** on held-out Lightning trajectories. We start from Grug's measured Lightning loss at the same budget and subtract the Snowball–Grug gap predicted by the law above. To convert that gap from Qwen 3.6 loss to Lightning loss, we use the teacher map fitted at matched budgets on four students (SmolLM3 base, SmolLM3 mid-trained, Qwen3-4B, Grug):

```math
L_{\text{Lightning}} = 1.711\, L_{\text{Qwen 3.6}} + 0.033
```

We apply only its slope to the gap: $`\Delta L_{\text{Lightning}} = 1.711\, \Delta L_{\text{Qwen 3.6}}`$.

**pass@1.** We use three links. Each maps loss $`L`$ to ability $`\theta`$, and $`\theta`$ to pass@1 through a Rasch model averaged over the 483 instances, $`\text{pass@1} = \frac{1}{483}\sum_i \sigma(\theta - z_i)`$. Link 1 uses the instance difficulties $`z_i`$ fitted on the 29-model sweep; links 2 and 3 share difficulties fitted on the 25 Lightning fine-tunes.

| Link | $`\theta(L)`$ | pass@1 |
|---|---|---|
| Global ability law | $`13.22 - 47.59\,L`$ | **41.6%** |
| One law across four students on Lightning (SmolLM3 base/mid, Qwen3-4B, Grug) | $`10.94 - 68.17\,(1 - r\,e^{-D/D_0})\,L`$, with Grug's $`r = 0.065`$, $`D_0 = 4.57\text{B}`$ | **40.3%** |
| Grug only (linear) | $`8.39 - 48.98\,L`$ | **39.4%** |

We expect the law across four students to be the most accurate, which gives a final predicted pass@1 of **40.3%**.

We also pre-register each link as a function of the measured loss (middle panel), so the links can be checked even if the loss prediction misses.

**Update (complete evals).** When we posted the Lightning prediction, three of the 25 fine-tunes behind the links had not yet finished all 2,415 attempts (483 instances × 5): Grug at 7.55B (2,363 attempts), SmolLM3 mid-trained at its largest budget (2,355) and SmolLM3 base at one epoch (2,343). All three have now completed. Refitting on the complete evals changes links 2 and 3 slightly. Link 1 does not use these fine-tunes, so it is unchanged. At the predicted loss of 0.1334 bpb:

| Link | $`\theta(L)`$ | pass@1 |
|---|---|---|
| Global ability law | $`13.22 - 47.59\,L`$ | **41.6%** (unchanged) |
| One law across four students on Lightning (SmolLM3 base/mid, Qwen3-4B, Grug) | $`10.93 - 68.06\,(1 - r\,e^{-D/D_0})\,L`$, with Grug's $`r = 0.064`$, $`D_0 = 5.02\text{B}`$ | **40.4%** (previously 40.3%) |
| Grug only (linear) | $`8.48 - 49.52\,L`$ | **39.6%** (previously 39.4%) |

The law across four students now predicts a pass@1 of **40.4%**.

**Update (released base).** Our predictions assumed the end of the final 65K cooldown (step 156,000, 9.97T tokens). The base model Marin released is [`open-athena/snowball-67b-a2b-base-262k-qk175-skew8`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/snowball-67b-a2b-base-262k-qk175-skew8) (step 157,000; #7495). It is the same run after 1,000 more steps (67B tokens) of 262K-context extension, during which the learning rate decays from 5% to 1% of peak (#8813).

**Loss.** Under our law, the extra annealing raises $`S_2`$ from 0.6496 to 0.6687 ($`S_1`$: 8.239 → 8.242), which lowers Snowball's predicted loss by 0.25%. Mapped to Lightning as before, the predicted loss goes from 0.1334 to **0.1331 bpb**.

**pass@1.** With the links from our previous comment:

| Link | pass@1 |
|---|---|
| Global ability law | **41.8%** (previously 41.6%) |
| One law across four students on Lightning | **40.6%** (previously 40.4%) |
| Grug only (linear) | **39.7%** (previously 39.6%) |

Our final predicted pass@1 is **40.6%**.

topics.title: [iris] Capability-URL round trips into cw-us-east-02a take 6–10 s under load (cw-rno2a: 0.15–0.5 s through the same gateway)
topics.body:
**Symptom.** Generation jobs in cw-us-east-02a each serve an OpenAI-compatible proxy as an Iris link endpoint (`/glm-harbor/<run>-<id>`). Agents call it through its capability URL (`https://iris.oa.dev/proxy/t/...`) once per agent step. On 2026-10-20 at about 04:50Z, a `GET /v1/models` on such an endpoint took 6–10 s through the capability URL. The same request sent directly to the endpoint's registered address from inside its container took under 10 ms. At the same time, capability URLs for endpoints in cw-rno2a (vLLM servers) answered the same request in 0.15–0.5 s from the same client. About 900 concurrent agent trials sat behind cw-us-east-02a endpoints then: 28 jobs × 32 trials, 56 registered endpoints. That was roughly double the load before about 03:10Z.

**Measurements**

| | result |
|---|---|
| `GET /v1/models` via capability URL, cw-us-east-02a endpoint (4 endpoints, 3–6 calls each) | 5.9–10.5 s; connect 0.01 s; nearly all of it is time to first byte |
| same endpoint, direct to its registered address from its own container | 0.000–0.009 s |
| `GET /v1/models` via capability URL, cw-rno2a endpoint, same client, same minute | 0.15–0.49 s |
| per agent step, gap from model reply to the next request (job request logs) | p50 0.4–1.3 s before ~03:05Z; 23–28 s after ~03:40Z |
| model backend latency per request, measured at the proxy (same window) | unchanged: p50 0.8 → 1.0 s, 6.7 → 6.9 ms per output token |

**Ruled out**
- The proxy process: it answers directly in under 10 ms, uses 5–7% of a core, and the containers have no CPU limit.
- The model backend: its latency and per-token speed are unchanged.
- The sandboxes (Daytona): command execution takes 20–80 ms per call, CPU speed is normal, host load is 22–37 on 64 cores.
- Client-side connection setup: connect time is 0.01 s, and the delay is all time to first byte.

**Not available.** There are no gateway or endpoint-relay metrics from before the slowdown. Load dependence is inferred from timing: the gap rose from about 03:10Z and leveled off by 03:40Z, as about 450 more trials started behind cw-us-east-02a endpoints. It has not been measured directly.

**Ask**
1. Gateway and endpoint-relay metrics for cw-us-east-02a from 2026-10-20 00:00Z onward: request rate, latency, queue depth and in-flight connections, compared with cw-rno2a.
2. Is there a per-cluster limit on proxied endpoint traffic (connection pool, worker count, a single relay stream to the cluster) that about 900 concurrent clients would saturate? If so, can it be raised, or should high-request-rate clients use another path?

# Research

Finelog `telemetry_v1.iris.rpc` holds minute snapshots; this table compares POST time-to-response-header counter deltas on endpoint names shared by parent and child, so it does not match individual requests or the reported GET probes.

| UTC window | cw-us-east-02a parent / child mean | parent / child completions | child total RPS / mean in-flight |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 00:00–00:15 | 6.35 / 4.57 s | 40,100 / 46,384 | 55.2 / 274 |
| 02:50–03:05 | 3.43 / 3.28 s | 40,025 / 48,026 | 68.5 / 307 |
| 03:40–04:00 | 14.64 / 5.61 s | 32,553 / 33,036 | 54.6 / 339 |
| 04:45–05:00 | 10.48 / 3.51 s | 50,900 / 51,105 | 61.5 / 374 |

At 04:45–05:00, cw-rno2a parent/child means were 5.21/5.23 s (2,458/2,437 completions); cw-us-east-02a's added wait appears in the parent-to-child path. The native proxy has no per-peer semaphore or single relay stream, but its upstream client retains zero idle connections; the metrics do not split decision, connection setup, and Traefik time. Live Traefik middleware inspection was denied by this session's Kubernetes role, so an ingress-side limit remains unverified.

**Relevant code**
- [`lib.rs#L1127-L1135`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/rust/src/lib.rs#L1127-L1135) — parent relay route
- [`dashboard.py#L278-L292`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/dashboard.py#L278-L292) — peer target decision
- [`lib.rs#L444-L447`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/rust/src/lib.rs#L444-L447) and [`lib.rs#L1367-L1371`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/rust/src/lib.rs#L1367-L1371) — upstream connection reuse
- [`native_proxy_metrics.py#L229-L244`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/native_proxy_metrics.py#L229-L244) — available counters and histograms

# Proposed Fix

1. Add per-peer timings for parent decision, upstream connection setup, and response headers, plus connection reuse and in-flight counts; inspect cw-us-east-02a Traefik active connections and request duration in the same windows.
2. Reproduce the POST and GET request mix on staging at approximately 450 and 900 concurrent clients. Change the measured bottleneck: bounded keep-alive reuse if connection setup dominates, or the identified ingress/decision path if it does not.
3. Verify p95 added relay time below 1 s at 900 clients, with no cw-rno2a regression or higher error rate. Off-cluster clients should continue using capability URLs until another authenticated route is validated; the child ingress is IP restricted.

Incident record: https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/795
@weaverbot are you saying there's no per-cluster limit, either implied by the setup or explicit, and that the best we can do is add metrics? or am I missing the point above ?

On it — https://loom.oa.dev/s/m6g97lda

- 🟢 `Oct 20 14:17Z` Answered the per-cluster limit question and corrected the incident record: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10318#issuecomment-6293000838

🤖 The earlier answer was too categorical. I found **no explicit per-cluster request or active-connection cap in the checked-in Iris proxy or ingress configuration**, and the parent does not send a cluster's traffic through one relay stream. There is still shared capacity: each CoreWeave cluster has [one controller pod](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/platforms/k8s/controller.py#L249), each relayed request gets a [target decision from the public parent's private Python listener](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/rust/src/lib.rs#L540), and the requests traverse the child's Traefik ingress. Any of those stages can saturate without an explicit limit. We have not established a threshold at 900 trials; the child proxy's measured mean in-flight request count was 339–374 in the cited later windows, and trials are not simultaneous HTTP requests.

I also need to correct my earlier connection-pool claim. [PR #9480](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9480), merged September 27, changed the Rust upstream client to retain up to **256 idle connections per host for 90 seconds**. That is an idle-reuse ceiling, not a cap on active connections. I have not verified which controller image was deployed during the incident. The checked-in Traefik route has an IP allowlist, with no request-limit middleware configured; the live Traefik settings remain unverified because the earlier Kubernetes read was denied.

The existing [Finelog comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10318#issuecomment-6283946880) shows added time between the parent and child proxies for the POST workload, but its counters cannot distinguish the parent's decision, connection setup, and the child's ingress. So adding timings is useful, but it is not the only action: check the deployed image and live Traefik/controller resources, then run the same GET/POST mix at roughly 450 and 900 trials while timing the public route and the parent-to-child route separately. Change whichever stage shows the added wait, then verify the latency and error rate under the same load. Until an authenticated alternative is validated, off-cluster Daytona agents should use the capability URL; in-cluster clients can use their registered endpoint address. I corrected the [incident record](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/795) to remove the stale zero-idle-connection claim.

topics.title: Vendor Evalchemy with an isolated evaluation runtime
topics.body:
Vendor Evalchemy under `vendor/evalchemy` with all 42 benchmark dataset
generators, active graders and resume support. Remove benchmark pages,
database tracking, reporting, original model providers, standalone rollout
drivers and unused evaluator configurations. Keep the prompt processing and
scoring code used by Marin.

Evalchemy has its own `uv.lock` and environment outside the root workspace's
dependency resolution. Marin invokes its CLI in a child process. FineStore and
Rigging resolve from checkout-local sources so changes can land atomically.
Replace the active fork pin and refresh machinery, and retire the fork's
nightly dashboard lane while preserving its history.

Fetch larger canonical benchmark datasets from full Hugging Face commit SHAs.
Stage shared copies under repository/revision/file keys using the configured
scratch storage, with leases and completion markers. Standalone runs can use
the native HF cache without origin probes or an explicit local/object-store
destination. Direct HTTP files use the same staging mechanism with an explicit
publisher version; downloads stream without additional content hashing. The
NUPA-Loose and NUPA5K-Loose benchmarks also read from the shared cache. Preserve
dataset ordering, prompts, benchmark test cases and sample identities; keep tiny
datasets and custom snapshots bundled. The default Iris bundle is 14.4 MiB,
within the deployed 25 MiB limit.

Immutable evaluation caches track evaluator inputs, portable configuration
and the dependency lock. Evaluation records retain broader adapter and
local-library provenance. Dated `eval-policy-*` configurations that select
external Evalchemy commits fail before writing configs or starting jobs.
Historical policies and grader replay scripts require the corresponding
pre-vendoring Marin checkout.

🤖 Holistic review of 756177c960c258387fd80b56ec18414dc0f6d6c1.

This PR replaces the commit-pinned external Evalchemy fork with a vendored copy in `vendor/evalchemy` (origin commit `09d27c93`). The copy has its own `uv.lock`, sits outside the root workspace, and gets its own CI lane. The fork-ferry and `config/external/evalchemy` machinery is removed. The vendoring itself fits the repository: Marin still reaches Evalchemy only through the `client.py` CLI boundary. The integration changes around it need work before merge. They are the new runtime identity, an unrelated broker startup change, and a bundle-cap raise that is no longer needed.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph launcher["experiments/evaluation launch"]
    resolve["_resolve_definitions"]:::changed -->|"evalchemy_runtime_descriptor"| ident["EvaluationIdentity / pipeline cache_key"]:::changed
  end
  subgraph child["Evalchemy child job (same Iris bundle)"]
    uvrun["uv run --project vendor/evalchemy --frozen"]:::changed --> cli["evalchemy CLI"]:::added
    cli --> fs["FineStore tables"]
  end
  resolve --> child
  cli -->|"OpenAI HTTP"| broker["brokered inference: waits for all N workers"]:::changed
  classDef changed fill:#fde7c8,stroke:#e8710a,stroke-width:2px
  classDef added fill:#d7f0dd,stroke:#1e8e3e,stroke-width:2px
```

**Before.** `EvalchemyRuntimeConfig.requirement` held a `git+…@<commit>` requirement, and the child ran it through `uvx --from` with CPU-torch wheel URLs and `s3fs`/`gcsfs` added via `--with`. That requirement string was both the record's `eval_runtime` and, for pipeline launches, part of the run-id cache key. It changed only when someone bumped the pin. Verified eval-policy cohorts selected their own Evalchemy commit through `RUNTIME_COMMITS`.

**Design.** The child now runs `cd $IRIS_WORKDIR; UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=$IRIS_WORKDIR/vendor/evalchemy/.venv uv run --project vendor/evalchemy --frozen --no-default-groups --extra …` with `setup_scripts=[]`. The torch pin and the cloud filesystems move into the vendored `pyproject.toml`. `evalchemy_runtime_source_hash()` hashes `vendor/evalchemy/eval`, `evalchemy_config`, `lib/finestore/src`, `lib/rigging/src`, both locks/manifests, and Marin's own `client.py`, `runner.py`, and `runtime.py`. Verified `eval-policy-*` versions that include Evalchemy now raise and point to a pre-vendoring checkout. Separately, `_start_brokered_inference` now blocks in `_wait_for_broker_workers` until every requested worker's current task attempt has registered. Iris raises `MAX_BUNDLE_SIZE_BYTES` to 50 MiB. The merge of main brings in the new default bundle exclusions (`tests/` and `docs/` at any depth), and with them the vendored tree fits under the deployed limit.

**Evidence and limits.** I ran the changed root tests locally (`tests/evals/test_evalchemy_config.py`, `tests/evals/test_inference_proxy.py`, `tests/evaluation/test_eval_policy_launch.py`, `experiments/evaluation/test_launch.py`) plus `lib/iris/tests/cluster/client/test_bundle.py`, and all passed. `create_workspace_zip('.')` at this head is 22.3 MiB, under the 25 MiB cap that deployed controllers enforce. All 1,072 tracked `vendor/evalchemy` files outside the top-level `tests/` ship in the bundle; I found no runtime file that main's any-depth `tests/` and `docs/` exclusions drop. So the earlier inline controller-rollout concern on `lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/bundle.py:33` no longer applies at this head. Nothing in the PR shows an Evalchemy job running on Iris with the new child command.

**Findings**

- **1. Should fix:** `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evalchemy/runtime.py:15` The source hash covers `lib/rigging/src`, `lib/finestore/src`, and Marin's `runner.py`/`client.py`/`runtime.py`. `experiments/evaluation/launch.py:378` puts that descriptor into the run-id cache key whenever `cache_key` is set, which is every immutable `eval_step` in `experiments/evaluation/pipeline.py:106`. As a result, a pipeline whose eval step is relaunched after any unrelated rigging or finestore commit (28 in the last month) gets new run IDs. It then re-executes evaluations that already finished and abandons their partial archives, which is the reuse that `test_relaunch_reuses_completed_steps_and_preserves_partial_archive` protects for the CLI. Under the old pin, identity changed only on a deliberate bump. Key the cache on the evaluator inputs only (`vendor/evalchemy/{eval,packages,pyproject.toml,uv.lock}`) and keep the wider hash as provenance. Also hash the git-tracked file set that the bundle actually ships. The current `rglob` with a hand-written skip list includes untracked files, so two checkouts of the same commit can record different `eval_runtime` values. `rigging.cache.directory_content_hash` already exists for this, and #10287 uses it.
- **2. Should fix:** `lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris.py:750` `_wait_for_broker_workers` makes brokered startup wait for all `instances` workers. Before, startup proceeded once one worker registered (`_registered_worker_metadata`). With `instances=8`, a single worker that cannot be placed holds the evaluation for up to `_ENDPOINT_PLACEMENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` (4 h) and then fails the whole startup, even though seven servers are ready. One worker job that exhausts its retries fails the startup the same way. This is unrelated to vendoring and has no stated motivating incident. Move it to its own PR. If the actual problem is stale registrations, keep the current-attempt check but require at least one current registration, and let later workers join the broker as they register.
- **3. Related PR:** `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evalchemy/runtime.py:32` #10287 (Harbor vendoring, same author, still open) adds `vendored_runtime_digest` in `marin/evaluation/harbor/provenance.py`. It hashes the same `lib/rigging/src`, `lib/finestore/src`, and manifest set with `rigging.cache.directory_content_hash`, while this PR hand-rolls an `rglob` with its own skip list. Whichever PR lands second should switch to one shared vendored-runtime digest helper. The two would otherwise drift on which files count as runtime identity. #10287 also still carries its own `[tool.iris.bundle].exclude` mechanism, written before main's default exclusions landed. It needs a rebase onto main's exclusions before it merges, and the combined bundle needs a size check against the 25 MiB deployed cap: this PR alone leaves 2.7 MiB of headroom.
- **4. Should fix:** `eval_policy/launch.py:139` `launch_policy` still builds Evalchemy configs and runs one `experiments.evaluation.cli launch` subprocess per Evalchemy benchmark, and the launcher now always rejects those launches. A default full-policy run therefore fails on its first benchmark (`math500`) inside a subprocess, not in the up-front validation loop. The PR also deletes `test_subset_requests_separate_nonblocking_h100_launches`, which was the only test of the H100 fan-out and the `--dry-run`/`--no-wait` handling for the Harbor-only subsets that remain supported. Reject Evalchemy entries in `launch_policy`'s validation loop with the historical-checkout message, and retarget the deleted fan-out test to a Harbor subset.
- **5. Should fix:** `lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/bundle.py:33` With main's exclusions the bundle is 22.3 MiB, so the raise to 50 MiB is no longer needed. It also opens a mismatch window: clients from `main` pass their local check up to 50 MiB, while every deployed controller still rejects anything above 25 MiB in `_store_launch_payload`. The PR body says the cap is "for updated controllers", but no controller rollout is part of this change. Drop the raise here, and land it together with a controller rollout when a bundle actually needs it.
- **6. Drop test:** `lib/iris/tests/cluster/client/test_bundle.py:195` `vendor_bundle` writes 26 MiB of `os.urandom` only to exceed the old cap, which mirrors the `MAX_BUNDLE_SIZE_BYTES` constant. The nested `…/vendor/scorer/tests` resource is reachable only through an explicit `extra_includes`, so the test checks main's include mechanism, not anything this PR adds. Drop it along with finding 5.
- **7. Should fix:** `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evalchemy/runner.py:208` The child command is the riskiest change, and nothing shows it running on a worker. It builds a fresh `vendor/evalchemy/.venv` in the task workdir, with editable `fschat`/`alpaca-eval`/rigging/finestore and `setup_scripts=[]`. The unit test replaces `uv` with a probe script. Before merge, run `experiments/evaluation/configs/evalchemy/gsm8k-smoke.yaml` once on Iris, plus one extra-bearing benchmark such as `ifeval`, and link the record.

topics.title: [rolloutengine] Keep the tools of each conversation in ConversationRecord
topics.body:
`ConversationRecord` (`lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/models.py:128`) keeps the messages of a conversation, but not the options of the prompt that started it, for example the tools that the model saw and `tool_choice`. Each request of the conversation sends these options (`lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/recorder.py:80`), and the `ConversationStarted` event gives them to an observer (`models.py:285`). But `_Conversation.record` (`recorder.py:119`) does not put them in the record, so a `GradedRollout` does not tell which tools the policy had.

`analyze_failed_runs` (#10265) shows its agent the tools of each failed rollout. Because the record has no tools, it takes `(TaskSpec, GradedRollout)` pairs and builds the tool list again with `task_prompt`. That list is not complete: it does not have the shell tool or the provider functions that `ShellHarness` adds.

Done when:
- `ConversationRecord` keeps the options of the prompt that started the conversation.
- A test shows that the record of a `ShellHarness` attempt has the shell tool and the provider functions.
- `analyze_failed_runs` takes only `GradedRollout` and reads the tools from the record.

comments.body:
🤖
# Research
`_Conversation` retains the options passed to `ModelSession.start()`, but `record()` omits them from `ConversationRecord`. `ShellHarness` adds the shell and provider functions to those options; the open #10265 analyzer builds each failed-rollout text file's tool header with `task_prompt(task, None, ())`, which omits those runtime-bound functions.

**Relevant code**
- [`recorder.py#L77-L126`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/recorder.py#L77-L126) — options lost when recording
- [`shell.py#L209-L220`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/rolloutengine/src/rolloutengine/harness/shell.py#L209-L220) — runtime tools enter prompt
- [`analyze_failed_runs.py#L245-L254`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/97b3c4ccd00ecf81e3926ece7b0190d85dfd54be/experiments/post_training/capability_driven_envs/analyze_failed_runs.py#L245-L254) — incomplete tool header

# Proposed Fix
`ShellHarness.run()` passes a prompt through `ModelSession.start()` to `_Conversation.record()`, where its options are lost. Store each conversation's starting options in `ConversationRecord`; change #10265's analyzer to accept `GradedRollout` values and render the recorded options and messages. Test a `ShellHarness` attempt with both shell and provider functions, then send the follow-up PR against #10265's branch.

🤖 The fix is in [PR #10323](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10323), stacked on #10265. `ConversationRecord` now keeps each conversation's starting options, including shell and provider functions; `analyze_failed_runs` reads those options from `GradedRollout`. The rolloutengine suite passed 208 tests, the taskforge and capability suites passed 131 tests, and the required lint and type checks passed.

topics.title: [taskforge] Grade decision-model tasks on the host
topics.body:
Grade decision-model tasks on the host. The owner is undecided on this kind of task, so this PR is kept separate from the rest of the stack; its upstream counterpart is #10280.

Verification is now one of five kinds (`answer_in_box`, `decision_model`, `code`, `llm_as_judge`, `composite`), and a composite is a weighted list of at least two other kinds. A `DecisionGrader` is its own grader type, not an LLM judge: the authoring model writes a rubric and a gold reference, and a decision model of fixed strength reads one state, by default the visible output of the solver's final turn, and answers one comparative question on five levels. Grading stays out of the rollout: a trial runs with the grader swapped to `NoGrader`, and the host grades the trial's final conversation afterwards. A read that fails transiently is read once more on the same conversation, and the solver's rollout is never re-run. `ClefDecisionClient` sends the reads to Clef behind the Orion gateway, using the request schema and state budget copied from clefclient into `taskforge.llm.clef`.

TaskSpec has no decision grader type until #10280 lands, so a TaskSpec carries the grader as a `NoGrader` whose contract holds it.

Builds on #10301 and is the last PR of the stack. Its five commits are the restack's own, cherry-picked unchanged; the stack sync adds the decision port and the decision parts of the spec and validation ports. The tree under `lib/taskforge` and the experiment matches the restack head (`taskforge/capability-restack` 87ffb54b02). The taskforge suite passes 814 tests here (78 more than #10301).

topics.title: [grug] Take ring_dedup's slot-weight gradient through a gather
topics.body:
The ring_dedup dispatch gathers each send slot's combine weights with `combine_weights_local[safe_source]`, whose autodiff transpose is a bfloat16 scatter-add into [Tlocal, K]. On MI350X that scatter takes 31 ms per June Snowball step at 65536 tokens per rank, and 7 ms at half the tokens: atomic bfloat16 adds slow down superlinearly with contention. Each kept (token, assignment) pair has exactly one send slot, so a custom VJP reads the gradient back through that slot map with a gather. Padding tokens and sender drops map to the sentinel slot and keep a zero gradient.

Together with the AMD cross-entropy backward block (#10341), on June Snowball (EP8, batch 128 per node, save_moe, PGLE): 8x MI350X 2.906 -> 2.805 s per step (15.56% -> 16.12% MFU); one 8x MI355X node 2.523 -> 2.448 s; two MI355X nodes (EP8 x DP2, batch 256) 3.198 -> 3.106 s. On a one-GPU stand-in for one EP8 rank this change alone is -1.3%. Losses are unchanged. The ring_dedup tests pass on MI350X.

Merge after #9880. Part of #9812.

topics.title: [rl] Build a source-stratified Snowball curriculum v0
topics.body:
Current results (October 20): the ten-update smoke completed with a verified checkpoint and Hugging Face export. The longer Smartie Step14 continuation has 61/100 verified optimizer updates. A paired 910-task development evaluation improved across all five families at update 25: equal-family mean verifier score 30.96% → 39.98% under a 4,096-token reply cap. The in-training structural score reached 61.32% at update 50. Datakit SFT and released Dr.Doom comparison runs have loaded their models; baseline evaluation and optimizer updates remain unverified. Those arms use an 8,192-token reply cap, so their scores require budget-matched comparisons. [Current results, protocol and limitations](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10314#issuecomment-6298575217).

Build an immutable 100,000-task candidate curriculum for fast-turnaround Snowball RL. Version `2026.10.19.2` contains 88,366 production-admitted TaskSpecs and 11,634 reviewed historical native closure imports. The [private browser](https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/e2bd5c9d-0f93-4ce9-b7af-3c78ca55e5d1/v/2/) contains the complete selected pool; sign in with a work Google account.

The approved recipe targets equal shares across five families: 20,000 each. Calendar capacity is 9,115, so its shortfall is distributed over the other four families. Final counts are calendar 9,115; competitive coding 22,722; Reasoning Gym 22,721; STEM 22,721; structural 22,721. This supersedes the initial proposal to reuse [Ben's intended one-sixth/four plus one-third structural weights](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/fed5a9383b92acacbe264c7e601e93d8437218d3/experiments/post_training/smartie/mixture-v2.json).

Sources:

- Calendar: Nemotron calendar and two Task Trove calendar datasets.
- Coding: Nemotron competitive coding, Eurus2, and verified Glaive sandboxes.
- Reasoning Gym: Nemotron puzzles and standalone Reasoning Gym.
- STEM: Nemotron STEM MCQA and OpenScience.
- Structural: all 11,087 selected admitted structured-output tasks plus 11,634 of Ben's synthetic structural-compliance tasks.

The 12 admitted sources have 244,938 eligible contracts after known holdout exclusions. Ben's pinned structural training release adds 57,364 native rows; full-contract deduplication removes 52, leaving 57,312 eligible. Combined candidate population: 302,250. Native additions are sampled as evenly as possible across eight structural families, then their control strata; no row is repeated to fill a quota. Distinct private grading contracts remain distinct and all selected source aliases are retained.

Inputs are pinned in the export:

- Production catalog `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/catalog/production`, snapshot `8c5d247ef6c2416fb3d14b2f159f74c4`; admitted `final/part-*.parquet` identities resolve through the verified CoreWeave migration receipt.
- [Exact historical native data](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-Data/tree/cb728a7636caad3fc6fa6b6ba85a49194d9d69a3), with file hashes, native validation IDs and tokenizer-aware prompt identities.
- Four evaluation sources and the known 910-task native validation panel. Native holdout checks use effective token prompts and full contracts, not their shared generic instruction text.

Done when:

- [x] Freeze source revisions, admission/import status, holdouts, recipe, and replay code.
- [x] Exclude known exact holdout overlap; deduplicate complete contracts and retain source aliases.
- [x] Select deterministically without replacement, recording quotas, probability denominators and provisional difficulty labels.
- [x] Publish 100,000 selected contracts, rejection accounting, Parquet, original payloads, readiness, and hashes.
- [x] Implement the historical native closure adapter and validate exact prompts and grading through the current CPU engine/trainer.
- [ ] Publish/pin the updated runtime libraries and trainer, resolve canonical external grader dependencies, and validate actual inference before declaring the complete pool training-ready.

Immutable export: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/curricula/snowball-v0/2026.10.19.2`. Its verified-copy completion manifest covers 20 files, 3,812,705,369 bytes. All published payload hashes match the frozen artifact manifest. Predecessor `2026.10.19.1` remains available unchanged.

Independent validation confirms 100,000 unique task IDs and full contracts, exact family quotas, source/stratum probabilities, retained aliases, and zero known exact holdout overlap. Retained canonical TaskSpec JSON strings are byte-identical to the same task records in the verified predecessor; native payload strings match the pinned historical release. Parquet round trips preserve both formats byte-for-byte. Twenty focused tests, scoped repository lint, and Pyrefly pass. Implementation is tracked in the linked ingester/runtime and trainer PRs.

The immutable pool retains original historical payloads. In its `train.parquet`, `contract_kind` selects either `task_json` or `lowered_task_spec`; the unused payload is null. A separate native adapter now emits 11,634 current `TaskRolloutSpec` records in the trainer’s `task_rollout_spec` column. All selected native tasks passed reference/invalid completions through the current CPU engine (23,268 attempts); all 88,366 canonical identities remain unchanged. The native export passed the actual trainer dataset, and scripted workers covered all eight native families. This is local source/CPU evidence. Published runtime-library releases and trainer lock updates remain release gates. For the smoke, the three adapter packages use exact Git revisions and a separately published full 100,000-task deployment pool. It remaps only the package-lock URI in 51,915 script tasks to a derived historical environment; the expired original dirty-build environment cannot be reconstructed exactly. The remaining 48,085 task payloads, including all native tasks, remain unchanged. The live Linux CPU gate validated the complete pool and returned grades for ten sandbox probes. An earlier GPU attempt failed during model initialization. The subsequent smoke completed ten optimizer updates using the full 100,000-task inventory, sampling 32 shuffled prompts per update with four answers per prompt. Training and export in Hugging Face format succeeded. Final verification checked the step-10 checkpoint commit marker, completed export request, successful terminal manifests, and exported model file inventory against its manifest. This run exercised inference, grading, optimization, checkpoint writing and model export. Checkpoint resume remains untested. A separate continuation with a fresh optimizer has completed 61 of 100 updates; the paired five-family development evaluation improved at update 25, and the in-training structural score improved through update 50. See the current results update linked above for coverage and token-budget limits. Difficulty remains a source/family prior; exact holdout exclusions do not establish semantic decontamination.

The approved derived native component is published at `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rl-data/curricula/snowball-v0/native-runtime/2026.10.19.1`: nine files, 8,473,539 bytes. Independent full readback matches every frozen SHA-256 and size. Its Parquet contains 11,634 native tasks and does not replace the full 100,000-task pool.

Related: [10k quality/annotation pilot #10315](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10315), [design #10316](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10316).

Implementation: [canonical ingester and runtime support #10319](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10319), following the existing curation catalog and TaskCompendium converter pattern; [trainer companion draft](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/1032). The canonical converter reproduces all 11,634 selected native TaskSpecs byte-for-byte. Package publication and the trainer lock update remain release gates.

| Reasoning Gym | 167 | 58.90% | 66.30% | +7.40 pp |
| STEM | 166 | 46.39% | 53.61% | +7.23 pp |

| Equal-family mean | 910 total | 30.96% | 39.98% | +9.02 pp |

The recipe samples 128 shuffled prompt groups × four answers per update from the full 100,000-task inventory, with a fresh optimizer, RLOO-N, AdamW `1e-6`, zero weight decay, gradient clip `0.5`, PPO clip ±`0.2`, and no KL or entropy auxiliary loss. Full inventory availability does not mean every task has been sampled. The first 25 updates took 1h24m and the first 50 took 2h41m, including checkpoint/evaluation work inside training; initial startup and standalone five-family evaluations are additional. The Datakit arm tests learning directly from cold SFT. Dr.Doom is an RL-trained descendant of the same SFT checkpoint; it tests whether those intervening RL stages help. The completed smoke and current continuation start from the already RL-trained Smartie Step14 checkpoint. The new 8,192-token scores will require budget-matched reference evaluations before comparison with the 4,096-token table.

Next: finish the 100-update continuation and both 50-update arms, verify checkpoints and final exports, and report per-family changes with scoring coverage. At the end of scheduled PR monitoring (18:04 UTC), prerequisite library publication and the dependent trainer lock update were still outstanding.

| Initializer | Step 0 | Step 25 | Step 50 | Token-limit stops, 0 → 25 → 50 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| [September 21 Datakit SFT](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21/tree/fe666478454e79fe6027a0bab0388d9abd68f51a) | 24.68% | 37.56% | 40.09% | 333 → 224 → 162 |
| [Released Dr.Doom](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21-dr-doom/tree/5b5705e8345bb111de03b3f0f9a00c8041e57db4) | 17.57% | 33.07% | 42.29% | 479 → 282 → 228 |

Family denominators remain fixed. Each evaluation scored 910/910 tasks using the same paired development panel, greedy decoding, one answer per task, an 8,192-token reply limit and a 24,576-token context limit. Token-limit counts are out of 910. Every family's step-50 mean was at least its step-25 mean; Datakit SFT calendar accuracy was unchanged. These are results on a reused development panel, not an untouched test set.

Both original training jobs failed their final evaluation coverage gate after committing checkpoint 50: two SFT grader errors and one Dr.Doom grader error. Recovery graded only those three saved answers using their original grader contracts; no answers were regenerated. The other 908 SFT scores and 909 Dr.Doom scores and the original failures remain preserved in the derived reports. The isolated regrading and export jobs succeeded; the original training-job failures remain part of the record.

[Recovery source](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/026dcb6398da47a159af34c0e4d8553c2f221158) preserves the original failures and appends the recovered grades. The draft implementation stack ends at #10409. The next comparison should use an untouched test split before treating these gains as generalization.

topics.title: [sft] Add the GLM 5.3 Harbor trace generation driver
topics.body:
Generate k=8 GLM 5.3 trajectories for TMax and SWE-smith pool tasks with
Harbor, plus v0/GLM relay episodes in which the v0 student acts until a trigger
(a completion claim, a format error or the context budget) hands the turn to
GLM. Each family runs under its eval-campaign Harbor policy, whose YAMLs and
Harbor/Evalchemy pins come from #9569 (now on main). Inside the run, a local OpenAI-compatible proxy
routes each request to the student or the GLM bulk relay and logs every request
and reply per trial. rebuild_traces turns those logs into one row per
conversation with turn authors, triggers and per-author token counts.

The relay student runs as its own root job (serve_student.py) on
non-preemptible H100 workers, in any cluster. A run picks the student with
--student: Snowball v0 or v0.1, each served from a regional bucket copy whose
config lives in students/. driver_config records the student's config,
location and Hub revision for every run, plain runs included, along with the
Harbor source pin. A lane reaches it through a capability URL for
the job's fixed endpoint name, passed only as STUDENT_BASE_URL. The lane waits
until /v1/models answers and takes v0's model id from that reply. On cw-rno2a,
preemptible students were evicted for hours, and each eviction failed every
trial in flight. While Iris moves v0, the proxy retries gateway errors
(404/502/503/504) and refused connections for up to 20 minutes. A run fails
when more than 20% of its trials raised without any proxy reply, since that
means a backend was down, not that the agent failed. httpx logs at WARNING, so
request URLs, the capability URL among them, stay out of logs.

Capability URLs are bearer credentials, so every output is scrubbed of Iris
capability tokens before it is written, including JWTs split across escaped
line breaks. scrub_run re-checks finished runs, and publish_hf refuses to
upload a row that still holds one. During the agent phase the sandbox reaches
only the proxy, and mini-swe-agent installs from pinned constraints. The
null, network and tool-env probe agents record what a sandbox can reach.

Only agents that run inside the sandbox (mini-swe-agent) call the proxy through
its capability URL. Terminus-2 runs in Harbor's own process, so it calls the
proxy at its local address. Under load, each capability-URL round trip into
cw-us-east-02a took 6-10 s (#10318). That raised the gap between a model reply
and the agent's next request from about 1 s to about 25 s. On the local address
it is back to about 1 s. driver_config records which route the agent used.

--reasoning-effort low|high (REASONING_EFFORT in run_lane.sh) makes the proxy
add the GLM 5.3 chat template's reasoning_effort to every teacher request.
Without it, nothing is sent and the template renders Max. Each requests.jsonl
turn and driver_config record the added fields, so a trace's effort is
readable from the trace itself.

--window-tokens (WINDOW_TOKENS) sets the SWE-smith generation window. The
default stays 30,000, so a trajectory fits a 32,768-token row in v0's chat
template. TMax keeps its policy window and refuses the flag, and a window
above the student's max_model_len is refused. The relay handoff budget
(window x --budget-fraction, BUDGET_FRACTION) and the proxy's /tokenize limit
follow the window. A larger window lets GLM reach the submit after a context
handoff, but its traces need a longer SFT row. run_lane.sh also logs sha256
prefixes of its credentials at start, so a secret rotation can be checked from
the lane log.

The traces from these runs are published as
open-athena/GLM-5.3-tmax-swesmith-k8-traces-2026.10.

Part of #10213

topics.title: Marin Eval Policy (2026-10-16)
topics.body:
## Overview

This document is an attempt to formalize Marin’s policy towards what constitutes reportable, public-facing, canonical eval results for Marin models as well as the baselines we compare against.

Why do we need this document? With the first “snowball” release of a 67B A2B MoE, Marin is entering a regime where we regularly compare Marin models to existing open and closed-source models. Because Marin’s unique claim is that we are open development, we will need to hold ourselves to a high standard of transparency on how we report eval scores of Marin models and what claims we make about Marin model capabilities based on those scores.

What is in scope? This document is intended to act as a living snapshot, trustworthy for any given period in time, as to the what and the how of Marin’s canonical set of evals, a set of standards to which we will aspire to hold ourselves. By "the what", we mean “which evals did we run, with what consistent set of hyperparameters and experimental constraints”. By "the how", we mean “where is the self-contained codebase that is both necessary and sufficient to reproduce our eval results independently”.

## Previous version notes

* Released Sept 24, 2026: 18 non-agentic benchmarks, 8 Harbor agentic benchmarks, and 4 reserved out-of-distribution benchmarks.

## Complete eval list, with hyperparameters
