comments.body:
🤖 Archived the description before automated prose cleanup.
<!-- marin-prose-cleanup-archive:b5089f579a6e1aeff26575db225c1143dba41cf3809bd78bd75283ed47114b86 -->

<details><summary>Original description</summary>

```markdown
The hero's shared and routed MLPs now flatten `[B, S, D]` into tokens locally on each device instead of with a global `(b s)` rearrange. With the sequence sharded over context, the global rearrange is an all-to-all in each direction, forward and backward, in every layer. Without context sharding nothing changes: each device already holds whole rows, so the local and global token orders are the same.

`_flatten_tokens` reshapes each device's block of rows and sequence shard in a `shard_map`, and `_unflatten_tokens` inverts it and restores the residual layout. Under context parallelism the experts then see tokens shard-major. Routing is per token, so the only order-dependent effect is which tokens a full expert drops first. A CPU test checks that CP2 logits equal CP1 logits on the same parameters when no token drops; the compiled CP2 forward goes from 8 all-to-alls to the 4 of the expert transport.

On one GB200 NVL72 rack restored from hero step 240000 at 65K context on CP4/EP16, on top of #10121's row balancing (same rack, 106 scored steps per arm), step time goes from 15.035 to 14.626 s (+2.80% tokens/s). The drop fraction falls from 2.21% to 0.23% and loss is 4.2e-3 lower. The old flatten gave each expert-parallel group 16 whole 65K rows, so a single-document row put a sixteenth of the group's tokens on one document's preferred experts; the local flatten splits that document across the four groups and mixes slices of all 64 rows into each. The same configuration on CP1 runs at 15.137 s with 1.94% drops, so with this change CP4 is the faster and more faithful 65K layout.

https://claude.ai/code/session_01V7n2oqJz61dkhYLBwNWYj9

```

</details>

topics.title: [taskforge] Add the TaskProposal document and proposal sources
topics.body:
Add `stage10_proposal`. A `TaskProposal` is strictly validated YAML front matter plus a markdown body with the required section headings; a repeated front-matter key is refused rather than resolved to its last value. `parse` and `render` round-trip it and `digest` hashes the canonical bytes, so a proposal's identity does not depend on how its author formatted the header. `document_regex` constrains a completion to that canonical layout, matching the body fence by fence so a fenced Markdown example may contain headings. `parse` also checks the research decision against the listed research items. `stage10_proposal.source` defines `ProposalBatch`, its slots, and the `ProposalSource` protocol.

`solver_machine` pins the solver's machine in the proposal: `null` for a container proposal, which runs in the image its build publishes, or one of `none`, `shellsim`, `cpython` and `packages` otherwise, with `none` legal only for a reasoning proposal. The proposer or triage writes it, and the build refuses a task whose machine differs from it (#10298), so no revision can move the solver between machines.

Builds on #10294; #10296 builds on it.

topics.title: Support Terminus-2 host-side agents in the shared RL rollout path
topics.body:
Allow RL runs to select Harbor's Terminus-2 controller, retaining its prompts, terminal interaction, context management, and grading inputs.

Current main (`2b08e2432c8871b7e6c4cd7c389d7bb2df2b4950`) routes task rollouts through RolloutEngine. Its [agent adapter](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/2b08e2432c8871b7e6c4cd7c389d7bb2df2b4950/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/agent_runtime.py) requires `BaseInstalledAgent` and rejects host-side Harbor agents. Host-side means the controller runs in the rollout-worker process or a host subprocess while task commands execute in a sandbox. Harbor's [Terminus2](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/aee476676983dfa62f5d824538193302ef46e3f9/src/harbor/agents/terminus_2/terminus_2.py) derives from `BaseAgent`, so it cannot use this adapter.

Done when:

- A documented configuration runs the existing Harbor controller with a trainable policy and Daytona task environment through the shared rollout path.
- Multi-turn requests preserve the exact served prompt/completion tokens and behavior log probabilities required by the chosen RL objective. Tokenization, context recovery, and any summarization are covered; unsupported modes fail before training.
- Host-side agent lifecycle, verifier execution, cancellation, and sandbox cleanup have explicit ownership. Failure classification and retry behavior are tested without silently scoring infrastructure failures as model failures.
- A live smoke completes multiple tool turns, verification, trajectory conversion, an optimizer update, and evaluation after inference-weight synchronization. It retains reproducible configs and model/verifier traces.

Prior compatibility work: https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/issues/538 documents a historical Terminus-2 tokenization-endpoint failure and is closed. This request covers integration with the current shared runner, not reopening that old failure.


Transferred from https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10387.
<!-- skyrl-migration: issue=I_kwDOSx5uL88AAAABW2xbuw -->

comments.body:
🤖 Open design question shared by marin-community/marin#10387, marin-community/MarinSkyRL#989, and marin-community/marin#10385: can the agent implementations remain in Harbor, with MarinSkyRL collecting the training evidence through an adapter? Is there a concrete operational constraint that requires porting them into Marin?

Please compare two ownership models before choosing an implementation:

- Harbor owns the full trial: agent controller, environment lifecycle, retries, and verification. MarinSkyRL supplies policy inference and captures training evidence.
- RolloutEngine owns the trial: its adapter runs Harbor's agent controller and propagates cancellation to it, while Marin manages environment lifecycle and verification.

For either option, establish how the integration retains exact model requests, sampled tokens, behavior log probabilities, tool observations, and verifier outcomes. Assign explicit owners for inference-request retries, tool-operation retries, whole-trial retries, cancellation, and cleanup, without duplicate handling of the same operation. Preserve original Harbor errors and diagnostics when mapping outcomes to MarinSkyRL's training decisions: include, exclude, or fail.

Keeping the implementations and, where practical, the full trial lifecycle in Harbor may avoid duplicating its operational behavior. This remains an architectural question, not a decided requirement or a claim that the current adapter supports it. What would prevent that arrangement, and what tests would establish that Marin's tracking and training interfaces can observe it correctly?

🤖
# Research

At MarinSkyRL main (82396a73), both the installed-agent runner and full Harbor trial runner require BaseInstalledAgent; Harbor's Terminus2 derives from BaseAgent, so selection fails before its first model turn. The full-trial path already lets Harbor run setup, verification, and cleanup while a correlation-keyed bridge sends model requests through RolloutEngine. Terminus-2's default summarization can leave its rollout details incomplete, and [#10326](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10326) reports that a history reset can discard earlier trainable actions.

**Relevant code**
- [agent_runtime.py, lines 150–275](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/82396a73a31e776229f3240c3af2b50ad53c4336/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/agent_runtime.py#L150-L275) — full trial and installed-agent gate
- [harbor_trial_session.py, lines 38–114](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/82396a73a31e776229f3240c3af2b50ad53c4336/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/harbor_trial_session.py#L38-L114) — trial grade and model session
- [agent_backend.py, lines 31–116](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/82396a73a31e776229f3240c3af2b50ad53c4336/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/agent_backend.py#L31-L116) — correlation and served token data
- [terminus_2.py, lines 316–445](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/blob/e96b6dcca1513e97e43523eaa971a85c68fcedae/src/harbor/agents/terminus_2/terminus_2.py#L316-L445) — host agent and context options
- [task_projections.py, lines 238–352](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/blob/82396a73a31e776229f3240c3af2b50ad53c4336/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/rollouts/task_projections.py#L238-L352) — training rows and masks

# Terminus-2 shared rollout plan

## Design

1. Extend the existing full Harbor trial route in agent_runtime.py and harbor_trial_session.py to accept a host-side BaseAgent. Keep Terminus-2 in Harbor. Use Trial.create and Trial.run so Harbor continues to own the controller, Daytona environment, verifier, attempt deadlines, cancellation, and sandbox cleanup. Give each host trial a local inference URL and unique correlation header; installed agents keep their current leased endpoint. Reject a model request without an active trial correlation ID.
2. Add a checked-in Terminus-2 RL recipe with a trainable policy, Daytona snapshot mapping, verifier, and evaluation settings. Validate the supported mode before allocating training workers: text chat completions through LiteLLM, exact token capture and requested behavior log probabilities, no Responses API, and summarization disabled for the first release. A context overflow must stop that attempt as nontrainable. Summarization can be enabled only after its rewritten prompts and all generated actions can be represented without loss; configuration that requests it before then must fail preflight.
3. Use served Prompt/ModelTurn records as the training source of truth. Before a trainable smoke, land a strict append-only guard for [#10326](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10326): transport metadata and generation-budget changes must not reset the trace, while genuine non-prefix rewrites fail closed. Check every turn's prompt IDs, completion IDs, finite aligned log probabilities, and loss mask through the chosen training projection. A last-segment-only sample must never receive the whole-trial reward.
4. Keep retry ownership singular. Harbor's controller handles tool operations and its model client handles inference-request retries; the bridge must replay an identical accepted request without generating another action. MarinSkyRL's TaskWorker owns whole-trial retry/backoff, while Harbor Trial owns verification and cleanup on success, timeout, error, or cancellation. Preserve the original Harbor exception and trial URI in the grading result. Missing or invalid verifier scores and infrastructure failures must follow the configured nontraining/error policy, even if the agent produced turns.

## Validation

Add focused CPU tests for a two-turn host trial, per-trial request isolation, duplicate inference requests, token/log-probability alignment into both training projections, a changed prompt, context overflow, cancellation and cleanup, verifier failure, and trial retry classification. Then run one live Daytona smoke with a trainable policy and GRPO objective: at least two terminal turns, verifier result, trajectory conversion, one optimizer update, inference-weight synchronization, and evaluation. Attach the pinned recipe, model and verifier traces, trial URI, and training/evaluation results to this issue.

## Coordination and open question

Searches of open PRs in Marin and MarinSkyRL found no Terminus-2 host-agent implementation. [MarinSkyRL #1030](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/1030) changes nearby rollout evidence and failure handling; reuse its final contracts. [#10386](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10386) can share the host-agent bridge but needs separate native-tool and multimodal validation. For a later summarization-capable mode, should every segment receive the whole-trial reward, or should summary-only actions be excluded from the loss? Decide this before enabling summarization.

topics.title: Add the Smartie joint-domain RL campaign
topics.body:
Add the Smartie campaign for joint training on structural closure, competitive coding, SWE-smith, NL2Bash, TaskForge and CalibForge tasks. Version the admitted data, fixed validation panels and saved training configurations. New runtime revisions use fresh run identities; submitted configurations remain immutable.

Pin MarinSkyRL to eedfec34799dd35ba3e19733d9e70efedc4730e1, which includes concurrent native/Harbor evaluation and benchmark task caching. The continuation starts from run 2026.10.15.32 step 14, the best surviving checkpoint by recorded inline validation score, shuffles training data, retains ten checkpoints, and uses 112 H100s. Run 2026.10.16.43 finished its initial validation pass with 621 of 663 attempted tasks graded; optimizer updates and post-update validation remain unverified. Before merging this PR, repin to the merged runtime repair commits on MarinSkyRL main, including [#1019](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/1019).

RolloutEngine accepts an explicit remote judge connection, propagates caller cancellation during cleanup, and checks replay prefixes after history transitions. Preserve grading after a conversation reset or an abandoned completion request; exclude undelivered responses from training records. RL coordinators reject missing declared secrets, and colocated SkyRL jobs reject expert-block weight synchronization. Local Shellbox execution rejects non-Linux hosts; curation image builds enforce tracked inputs only inside Git worktrees.

Offline closure audits reuse Verifyit's training scorer, including typed JSON comparison and signed-zero equality. 1. `config/external/MarinSkyRL/pyproject.toml:15` The uv source changes from `branch = "main"` to `rev = "ea93af58…"`, which is the head of MarinSkyRL#1007. That PR is open and unmerged. Add one launch config per ported cybersecurity suite for the evaluation

produced the baseline scores recorded in the cybersecurity tracker. The
adapters that generate these task datasets are in the companion harbor PR.

topics.title: [grug] Reorder AMD flash attention launches and retile dK/dV
topics.body:
The Pallas-Triton flash attention kernels for AMD GPUs now put the block index on the last grid axis, so programs launch longest blocks first, and compute dK/dV with transposed 64x128 tiles (4 warps, 1 stage). The transposed tiles produce P^T and dS^T in the layout the dV and dK matmuls take, which removes two in-register transposes per block. The forward, dQ and dK/dV kernels share one band-mask predicate.

June Snowball on 8x MI350X (EP8, batch 64, ring_dedup, save_moe): flash attention time per step 245 -> 167 ms, step 1.597 -> 1.528 s (14.15% -> 14.80% MFU), with unchanged loss and peak memory. A sweep of 65 block configurations at batch 16 after this change found no faster tiles. The flash attention tests pass on MI350X.

Part of #9812.

topics.title: [grug] Read precomputed fa4_bounds in the AMD Pallas flash kernel
topics.body:
`moe_hero_ep`, `moe_hero_fsdp` and `fast_track` run their layers in one homogeneous `lax.scan` and pick each layer's sliding window by selecting between precomputed `fa4_bounds` arrays (`experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/model.py:1338-1359`). They have to: the window is a static `AttentionMask` field that the scan body cannot vary. `gpu_pallas_triton_flash` rejected any mask that carried those bounds, so none of these models could run on AMD GPUs with it. The kernel now uses the bounds as its per-query key lower bounds, as `gpu_fa4_cute` does.

A padding query (`valid=False`) attends only to itself, so outputs differ from the segment-ID path only on padding rows, which the loss masks. The kernels trust the bounds: after padding rows are set to their own position, the bounds must be nondecreasing and at most each query's position, which `fa4_cute_segment_bounds` gives when every segment ID is one contiguous run. The dK/dV pass depends on that ordering, so arbitrary bounds give wrong key and value gradients without raising. The module docstring and the `AttentionMask.fa4_bounds` comment state this.

The tests run the `moe_hero_ep` pattern against the reference on a 2x2 data/model mesh: long and short bounds computed outside a `lax.scan`, sharded over the batch, and selected per layer with `jnp.where`. The one-device Grug mesh test also runs through the bounds path, where the bounds, like q, name length-1 Explicit axes. A GPU-only test covers bf16 at the default tile sizes, 4096 tokens and window 2048.

Part of #9812

Loss, gradients and gradient shardings are checked against the reference across three layers.
- bf16 at production settings (93bf041b5a): a GPU-only test runs the bounds path in bf16 at the default tile sizes, 4096 tokens and window 2048, against the reference. It is skipped in the CPU interpreter. An MI350X run of the full test file is queued on the AMD cluster, and I will post the result here.
- Bounds contract (93bf041b5a, 470be30b3c): the kernel module docstring, the `_key_lower_bounds` comment and the `AttentionMask.fa4_bounds` comment now spell out the requirement. After invalid rows are set to their own position, the bounds must be nondecreasing and at most each query's position. `fa4_cute_segment_bounds` produces such bounds when every segment ID, padding included, is one contiguous run. Other bounds give wrong dK/dV without raising. A runtime check would run on every scanned layer, so the bounds are documented rather than validated.

The PR description is updated to match.

🤖 GPU results at commit 8f4aaa0f2f: all 20 tests in `test_amd_pallas_triton_flash_attention.py` pass through Triton on MI350X (HPC Fund job 470890) and MI355X (Vultr job 11648). This includes the bf16 bounds-path test at the default tile sizes, 4096 tokens and window 2048, and the one-device Grug mesh test, which now also runs on precomputed bounds that name length-1 Explicit axes, the way `moe_hero_ep` shards them. The scan and multi-device tests run in the Pallas interpreter on CPU devices.

topics.title: [eval] Recover brokered evaluations after inference preemption
topics.body:
Use the existing inference broker for evaluations with one model-serving instance, with streaming responses and worker readiness. Requests keep a stable endpoint when GPU workers move. Pipeline-parallel gangs retain direct serving.

When model or judge inference is unavailable, Marin stops the evaluator, waits for readiness, and restarts it against the same output path. The vendored Harbor and Evalchemy runtimes resume from their saved checkpoints. Completed evaluation steps stay cached.

The broker can retry a request only before accepting response headers from the worker. Later worker loss breaks the stream. Buffers are bounded and abandoned requests are canceled. The broker's in-memory queue is not durable across broker actor failure.

Uses the existing broker instead of the separate relay proposed in #10033.

Fixes #10030.

The PR moves inference-outage handling from the Harbor runner into a shared `run_with_inference_recovery` loop. The shared loop fits the existing `EvalExecutor` seam, and the changed unit tests pass locally. One consequence of the transport-failure rejection needs an operator path, and one write is redundant. #10033 is a competing fix for the same failure and should be reconciled before either PR lands.

**Should fix**
1. `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/runner.py:426` `resuming_archive` is true for any non-empty archive at `output_dir`, not only for archives this process interrupted. `run_served_evalchemy` uses the step's deterministic `out_path` (`experiment/evaluation.py:77-79`), and StepRunner or orchestrator retries reuse it. Suppose a first attempt saved even one transport failure that the fresh-attempt branch at :437 and the coverage gate at :505-514 accepted. Every later rerun of that step then fails as `INFRA_FAILED`, and no retry can clear it. The message at :440 does not name the archive or say what an operator must do. Put `output_dir` and the remedy (delete the archive to rerun) in the `EvaluationError` message. Add the same sentence to the README paragraph that this PR adds, so the permanent failure has a documented exit.

That fn writes the full `ArtifactRecord` at the same path from `result.result_payload()` after `run_served_evalchemy` returns. Since `FineStoreEvalchemyResult` now carries `jobs`, the step record already persists them. The manual write adds a window in which a minimal record exists with no name, version, fingerprint, or provenance. Delete line 117 and the `write_artifact` import at :37.
3. `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evalchemy/result.py:58` and `lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/runner.py:201,262` The docstring rewrites are unrelated to preemption recovery, and they remove invariants that the code still depends on. `EvalchemyResult` lost the note that historical reports persist its type name, so the class is part of the durable decoding contract; without it, the class reads as deletable. `_attempted_trials` lost the reason it returns `None` rather than the number of trials found: a found count would certify an interrupted run as complete. `_aggregate` lost the reason it divides by scored trials. topics.title: [Post-training][RLVR] Smartie: Multi-Domain RLVR Revisited on Snowball 67B A2B
topics.body:
## TL;DR

Smartie revisited multi-domain reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) on Snowball, a 67B-total / approximately 2B-active-parameter model. Run `2026.10.15.32` produced the checkpoint released as [Marin Snowball 67B-A2B v0.1](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Marin-Snowball-67B-A2B-v0.1). At its released update 14, recorded native validation pass@1 rose from **41.21% to 50.22%**. NVIDIA task mean reward rose from **40.59% to 55.50%**, while structural-task mean reward fell from **39.09% to 32.92%**. The experiment shows useful task learning and recorded structural regression. It does not establish successful balanced joint optimization.

The intended mixture combined four domains from [NVIDIA Nemotron-RL-Ultra-Training-Blends](https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/Nemotron-RL-Ultra-Training-Blends): calendar reasoning, competitive coding, Reasoning Gym puzzles, and STEM multiple-choice questions. These are called the NVIDIA cohort below. Synthetic structural-compliance tasks formed the other cohort. The launch configuration left shuffling disabled: domain-grouped NVIDIA rows preceded the structural rows. The training-reward spike near update 16 therefore cannot be interpreted as a sudden general capability gain. The fixed-validation curves are the evidence used here.

## Setup

The run started from [Grug Merge Campaign2 DARE-TIES-02](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Merge-Campaign2-DARE-TIES-02-2026.10.10/tree/153f5369f69a0c0a7203779099ec94e98c66748f), with a fresh optimizer. It did **not** start from the separately released Marin Snowball v0, which is a Campaign3 merge. [The model provenance report](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14#provenance-report) records the initializer's merge parents.

Training used asynchronous RLOO-N, a leave-one-out policy-gradient estimator with neutral treatment of masked infrastructure failures, and truncated importance sampling. The learning rate was `4e-6`, with 512 accepted prompt groups and 16 responses per group per update. The run used 64 H100 policy GPUs and 48 separate inference GPUs. There was no KL, entropy, or auxiliary FTPO loss; structural tasks used the same verifiable-reward objective as other tasks. Loss reduction was token-mean. The [exact submitted launch config, resolved config, and source patch](https://gist.github.com/penfever/40f0f81dd4fba022697e4fa5aeabb91d/b79646603c23bd466969ff498661a0e313b1024a) are public.

The N means neutral: a masked infrastructure-failure sample gets zero advantage and is excluded from other samples' leave-one-out baselines. Model failures can remain zero-reward samples in the baseline. A group contains responses to the same prompt; 512 accepted groups is the optimizer-batch target, not 512 arbitrary completed responses. The configuration requires at least four baseline-eligible responses per group; fully masked, stale, undersized, or contract-invalid groups cannot contribute normally, and constant-reward groups provide no relative learning signal. Exact accepted groups and valid loss-token shares per domain were not reconstructed. File row proportions must not be treated as optimizer exposure.

The [exact public data release](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-Data/tree/cb728a7636caad3fc6fa6b6ba85a49194d9d69a3) contains 69,487 training tasks and 910 native validation tasks. Training rows comprise 741 calendar, 7,553 competitive-coding, 1,918 Reasoning Gym, 1,911 STEM, and 57,364 structural tasks. These are task inputs for online generation, not a static collection of model answers. Structural families cover JSON objects, arrays, nesting and string escapes, code fences, reasoning delimiters, tool-call delimiters, and repeated-opener retention. A continuation task can ask the model to finish a supplied JSON prefix without adding fields or changing reference content. Valid syntax alone does not pass that content-preservation check.

## Results and limits

| Fixed native validation measure | Initializer, update 0 | Released update 14 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Combined recorded pass@1, 910 tasks (%) | 41.21 | 50.22 |
| NVIDIA mean outcome reward, 667 tasks (%) | 40.59 | 55.50 |
| Structural mean outcome reward, 243 tasks (%) | 39.09 | 32.92 |

Grading coverage was 654/667 NVIDIA tasks and 235/243 structural tasks at initialization, versus 667/667 and 226/243 at update 14. Structural mean among graded tasks also fell, from 40.43% to 35.40%, so missing grades do not fully explain the recorded structural regression.

Each validation task has one sampled response. Mean outcome reward averages per-task rewards in `[0,1]`; missing grades remain zero outcomes in the fixed denominator. The combined native metric is task-count weighted, not an equal average of source means. The runtime's recorded pass@1 uses an explicit pass verdict when available and otherwise positive reward; partial-credit tasks can count as passing. Reasoning Gym exhibits this distinction: its initial mean reward is 76.48%, while recorded pass@1 is 82.04%. Mean outcome reward and pass@1 are therefore different measures. These repeatedly inspected development results are not an independent final test or a statistical-significance claim.

Update 12 had the highest recorded native pass@1, **50.33%**, but its weights had already been removed by checkpoint retention. Update 14 was the best surviving checkpoint, at **50.22%**, and was exported with that limitation recorded. The [complete public W&B metric archive](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-Artifacts/tree/20a22f8a7bdcbca7edf38279b7c24d22826693a3/wandb-full-20261019) covers 22 returned history rows: the pre-training row 0 and recorded optimizer steps 1–21, with native validation through step 20. This does not establish whether an additional unlogged update occurred before cancellation.

The separate in-line BFCL-Parity, SWE-bench Verified, and OpenThoughts-TBLite panel suffered execution failures. Its incomplete results were not used as valid zero-accuracy benchmark measurements. A later independent release-policy evaluation and baseline comparison is published in [#10283](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10283); it is separate from the native validation curves in this report.

Later campaign runs tested shuffled mixtures, Harbor-native Mini-SWE-Agent execution, task-source repairs, and staged SWE-Smith repository setup. They do not contribute weights to the Step14 release. The active `.57` job is deliberately left running; its later results will be reported separately. This issue closes the historical publication record, not that live job.

## Reproducibility and conclusion

The release includes public weights, exact Step14 training/native-validation Parquets, launch configs, frozen metric history, figure inputs, and source revisions in the [campaign artifact archive](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026/tree/9f01d8146fc48d7c5eb9c95d08d46d86b81c0f66). The archive's [reproduction guide](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026/blob/9f01d8146fc48d7c5eb9c95d08d46d86b81c0f66/REPRODUCING.md) collects the historical revisions, submitted patch/config, input mapping, and original launch command. Code is recorded in [Marin #10190](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10190), [MarinSkyRL #1030](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/1030), and [Harbor #277](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/277). These are code-publication links, not claims that the PRs have merged. Historical reproduction uses the submitted source pins. Marin's latest-main RolloutEngine API integration remains pending in its draft PR; the two runtime fork worktrees were refreshed against main.

Existing private repositories remain private. Raw conversations, restricted TaskForge inputs, uncleared third-party task assets, secrets, and transient environments are excluded from this public artifact upload. Those exclusions limit independent reconstruction of later restricted-data runs and trace-level failure analyses. The original Megatron optimizer checkpoint and a complete raw rollout history are not included, so bitwise training or export reproduction is not claimed.

The main next experiment is shuffled joint exposure with measured per-domain optimizer admission and valid-token contribution. A separate comparison can test sequence-mean loss to reduce response-length weighting. Structural retention needs an explicit checkpoint-selection constraint. Agentic benchmark claims require complete, graded benchmark cohorts; a training-reward increase alone is insufficient.

## Historical campaign tracker

This is the campaign TRACKER snapshot, with public artifact links replacing local paths. Iris and W&B links are operational references that may require authentication; Step14 evidence is mirrored publicly. The tracker includes failed and preparatory runs. A dash in a score column means no usable recorded score; in other columns it means missing or not applicable. Inaccessible raw evidence is labeled as unavailable.

The real/structural mean-reward columns use the tracker's graded-only convention and may differ from the fixed-denominator means in the release figure. `Real` denotes the four NVIDIA domains in `.32`, but later runs change the cohort. `Recorded optimizer step` is the run's counter, separate from initializer ancestry; it can reset with a fresh optimizer and continue across a training-state resume. The `.32` value is 21, the last optimizer step in the public metric history, not the 22 returned history rows that include baseline step 0.

BFCL/Pi means the Harbor BFCL-Parity adaptation using the Pi coding-agent harness; SWE is SWE-bench Verified; OT is OpenThoughts-TBLite. Historical benchmark columns use their linked audited scored-trial denominators, which differ by run. A documented early comparison uses 123 BFCL tasks and 498 SWE tasks; the failed `.32` in-line panel instead attempted 30 tasks per benchmark. @ravwojdyla FYI this issue contains the experiment that produced v0.1

🤖 Update: Smartie `2026.10.19.57` completed 12 recorded optimizer updates and was stopped on October 20 after later agentic validation scores declined. [Update 8 is exported publicly](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.19.57-step8). This is an experimental continuation; it does not replace the earlier Marin Snowball v0.1 release.

The initializer was [Smartie `.32` update 14](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14), with a fresh optimizer. The run used asynchronous RLOO-N, a configured training batch of 512 groups × 16 responses per update, AdamW at `4e-6`, token-mean loss, and no KL or entropy auxiliary loss. [W&B](https://wandb.ai/dogml/snowball-smartie-rl/runs/v1vksnkr).

### Per-domain results and artifacts

The [public artifact bundle](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/e0d611e5e5d10ce2ba7b1f807e3a8a/runs/2026.10.19.57/update-20261020) contains PNG/SVG figures, CSV/JSON plot values, selected numeric W&B metrics, plotting code, the launch configuration, and exact data links.

![Per-domain validation reward](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/e0d611e5e5d10ce2ba7b1f807e3a8a/runs/2026.10.19.57/update-20261020/per-domain-validation-reward.png)

All values below are mean verifier scores among graded attempts, scaled to percent. Scores can include partial credit, so these are not uniformly binary success rates. They differ from fixed-denominator averages in some earlier campaign figures. These are repeatedly inspected development panels with one sampled response per task, not full release-policy evaluations. [Exact graded/attempted counts for every domain and checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-Campaign-Artifacts-2026/blob/6662745944e0d611e5e5d10ce2ba7b1f807e3a8a/runs/2026.10.19.57/update-20261020/validation-curves.csv).

| Validation domain | Initializer | Update 8 | Update 12 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| SWE-Smith full issue repair | 27.16 | 34.34 | 9.78 |
| CalibForge | - | - | - |
| NL2Bash | 71.00 | 57.58 | 27.00 |
| Competitive coding | 51.28 | 45.07 | 26.87 |
| Structural compliance | 36.36 | 63.20 | 76.09 |
| TaskForge | 72.88 | 6.26 | 0.88 |
| SWE-bench Verified, Terminus-2 | 3.33 | 33.33 | 6.67 |
| BFCL-Parity, Terminus-2 | 53.33 | 66.67 | 13.33 |
| OT-TBLite, Terminus-2 | 6.90 | 13.33 | 0.00 |

CalibForge has no valid grades: all four tasks fail agent startup at every checkpoint. SWE-Smith grade coverage is 81/100, 99/100, and 92/100 at the three tabulated checkpoints. The decline also holds on the same 64 SWE-Smith tasks graded at all seven evaluations (updates 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12): 28.13% initially, 42.19% at update 8, and 14.06% at update 12. Update 8 was selected for export by the user; it is not uniformly best across domains.

![Validation grading coverage](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/e0d611e5e5d10ce2ba7b1f807e3a8a/runs/2026.10.19.57/update-20261020/validation-coverage.png)

### Training mix and exact data

Training used 3,322 rows: **1,661 SWE-Smith Stage 1 repository-setup tasks and 1,661 structural tasks**, with shuffle enabled. Stage 1 asks the agent to prepare the correct repository, branch, commit, and installation; it does not ask for a bug fix. SWE-Smith validation still tests full issue repair. CalibForge and the other domains above are validation-only in this run.

![Training-source reward](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/e0d611e5e5d10ce2ba7b1f807e3a8a/runs/2026.10.19.57/update-20261020/training-source-reward.png)

- [Exact training Parquet](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/task-trove-smartie-continuation-private/blob/3cd8b45655637b5d1b79ca607d007537706e2981/releases/2026.10.19.1/stage1-structural-mixture/train.parquet).
- [Exact 573-row validation Parquet](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/task-trove-smartie-continuation-private/blob/3cd8b45655637b5d1b79ca607d007537706e2981/releases/2026.10.19.1/stage1-structural-mixture/validation.parquet).
- [Source-owned agent profile and task requirements](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/task-trove-smartie-continuation-private/blob/3cd8b45655637b5d1b79ca607d007537706e2981/releases/2026.10.19.1/stage1-structural-mixture/README.md).
- [Launch config](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/e0d611e5e5d10ce2ba7b1f807e3a8a/runs/2026.10.19.57/update-20261020/training-launch.yaml) and [data hashes/provenance](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/e0d611e5e5d10ce2ba7b1f807e3a8a/runs/2026.10.19.57/update-20261020/data-provenance.json).

The exact data files remain **private and access-controlled**. Validation includes restricted TaskForge payloads, and the complete task bundle has not been cleared for public redistribution. Both Parquet hashes were verified against this pinned HF revision. Exact reproduction requires data access.

Validation used the same declared release, URI, and file as `.56`; the release README also records that rows were copied unchanged from the preceding cohort. The 573 rows comprise 100 SWE-Smith, 100 NL2Bash, four CalibForge, 85 coding, 41 TaskForge, and 243 structural tasks. Three additional panels of 30 tasks each (BFCL, SWE-bench, and OT-TBLite) are configured in the launch file.

### Interpretation and follow-up

Structural scores improved while later issue-repair and tool-use scores declined. Original Harbor traces from 30 SWE-bench and 30 BFCL tasks at each of updates 8 and 12 show increased parser-error fractions (73.99% to 87.62% for SWE-bench; 74.95% to 88.56% for BFCL). These evaluation traces were recovered independently of the training-trace publisher. A confirmed training-path defect clears earlier action tokens after history resets, leaving the final segment to receive whole-task reward. [Marin #10326](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10326) records the evidence and required TITO safeguards.

The defect's contribution to the reward decline has not been isolated experimentally. A separate trace-publisher failure limits late-run training evidence. The next training run needs verified preservation of all action segments and repaired trace retention before testing whether the narrow setup/structural mix itself harms broader behavior. No replacement run was launched as part of this update.

🤖 Data preservation follow-up: the campaign's staged SWE-Smith data and versioned RL inputs are archived in [the private campaign data archive](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/task-trove-smartie-continuation-private/tree/ab5173cc03cd4392d5b8cdf38a3392e1ff44a0bc/campaign-archive/2026.10.20): 84 archives, 179,190 data/evidence files plus a curation-code snapshot, about 5.8 GB compressed. Existing public releases remain public; this archive does not change their visibility.

| Data | Preserved release | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SWE-Smith Stage 3 | [Data, manifests, overlays and verifier evidence](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/task-trove-smartie-continuation-private/blob/ab5173cc03cd4392d5b8cdf38a3392e1ff44a0bc/campaign-archive/2026.10.20/swesmith-staged-v2-20261017.tar.gz) | 778 handoffs from 600 parents: 762 train / 16 validation. Includes 600 complete and 178 partial handoffs. Private. |
| SWE-Smith Stage 1 | [Original staged cohort](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/task-trove-smartie-continuation-private/blob/ab5173cc03cd4392d5b8cdf38a3392e1ff44a0bc/campaign-archive/2026.10.20/swesmith-staged-v1-20261017.tar.gz) and [2026.10.19.1 source-owned prompt/verifier mixture](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/task-trove-smartie-continuation-private/tree/3cd8b45655637b5d1b79ca607d007537706e2981/releases/2026.10.19.1/stage1-structural-mixture) | Setup tasks, source profiles, verifier repairs, and historical mixture versions. Private. |
| Repaired CalibForge | [Public shared-environment v2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/task-trove/tree/3b6c5b5533f1b702163f365b7ce869b834cb2994/releases/calibforge-shared-20261017-v2) | 324 environment-admitted tasks, 259 train / 65 validation; fixtures, qualification evidence, source attribution and reproduction scripts. Oracle solution execution was waived. |
| Repaired NL2Bash | [Public admitted release](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/task-trove/tree/772fd68384a511b9a2b8db9f2e397ae12ca0621e/releases/smartie-continuation-20261016/nl2bash) | 996 retained tasks; task payloads and quality decisions. Historical oracle-path fixes and splits are also in the private archive. |
| Repaired full SWE-Smith | [Public admitted release](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/task-trove/tree/0e8137a6a1eca1e2c8c12eeb90a16c5d7f1f750c/releases/smartie-continuation-20261016/swesmith) | 8,045 quality-admitted tasks. Historical filtering, split and oracle inputs are also in the private archive. |
| Other campaign RL data | [Archive manifest](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/task-trove-smartie-continuation-private/blob/ab5173cc03cd4392d5b8cdf38a3392e1ff44a0bc/campaign-archive/2026.10.20/manifest.json) | Structural datasets, mixed training/validation revisions, TaskForge inputs, source splits, admission decisions, and canary inputs. Private where redistribution review is incomplete or source access is restricted. |

Stage 3 was not used in run `.57`. Its 600 complete handoffs start from repaired code that passed the original required tests. Its 178 partial handoffs start from partially repaired code with a witnessed remaining test failure; the known repair passes those tests. All 30 representative runtime controls across six repositories returned expected grades, including rejection of protected-file corruption and injected passing tests. This does not establish 778 independent full agent runs. Original parent-task split assignments are preserved, but repositories overlap across splits.

Direct Stage 3 downloads: [train JSONL](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/task-trove-smartie-continuation-private/blob/ab5173cc03cd4392d5b8cdf38a3392e1ff44a0bc/campaign-archive/2026.10.20/stage3/train.jsonl), [validation JSONL](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/task-trove-smartie-continuation-private/blob/ab5173cc03cd4392d5b8cdf38a3392e1ff44a0bc/campaign-archive/2026.10.20/stage3/validation.jsonl), and [admission manifest](https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/task-trove-smartie-continuation-private/blob/ab5173cc03cd4392d5b8cdf38a3392e1ff44a0bc/campaign-archive/2026.10.20/stage3/variants-manifest.json). These are private, byte-verified copies of the frozen exports.

Stage 3 still needs its local actor/verifier images rebuilt or separately distributed before another machine can execute it. Its image locators are local IDs, not pullable registry references. The archive includes the curation source snapshot, recorded image mappings, and task resources; it does not include local container image archives. Rebuilding from the archived material has not been tested on a fresh machine, so this is not a self-contained execution release. Keep private tests, gold solutions, and verifier resources outside model access.

“Quality-admitted” means the curation pipeline accepted a task; it is not a model-solving accuracy claim. CalibForge's environment admission checks cover fixture equivalence and setup/verifier execution, with oracle solution execution explicitly skipped. Its public v2 release includes train/validation splits. The public NL2Bash and full SWE-Smith releases contain task cohorts and review decisions; their campaign-specific splits are in the private archive. Private downloads require access to the Open-Athena repository.

The archive contains historical and rejected candidates as well as admitted data. Use each version's admission manifest rather than treating all archived rows as approved training examples. Raw source mirrors, mounted source volumes, caches, and operational log directories were excluded. The file manifest records SHA-256 hashes and exclusions; no archived dataset is silently relabeled as public or fully runnable.

The latest run's validation Parquet was also checked against the previous Stage 1 release: both have SHA-256 `5e851fd5376aca35f307b13d3d16b74414fcc8d9be7b4ab26b4c9e46b45a1c6c`. No validation-data change was introduced between those releases.

topics.title: [iris] GPU jobs default to NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and flood log forwarding
topics.body:
Every Iris job that requests a GPU extra gets `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` with `NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=INIT,BOOTSTRAP,ENV,NET,GRAPH,TUNING,RAS` from the default environment in `lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/types.py:779`. Marin's training launcher sets `NCCL_DEBUG` to `WARN` only when nothing is preset (`lib/marin/src/marin/training/training.py:418`, `setdefault`), so the Iris default wins for every training job.

On 2026-10-17 four 32-GPU SFT jobs (`/karan/task203-lr*`, cw-rno2a) emitted about 80,000 log lines per second, mostly `NCCL INFO` per-collective output, while log forwarding accepts about 34,500 lines per second; the hub fell about 90 minutes behind on that cluster's logs.

Reproduce: submit any GPU job without setting `NCCL_DEBUG` and read its task log; `NCCL INFO AllReduce: ... Algo TREE proto LL ...` lines appear for every collective.

Expected: GPU jobs default to `NCCL_DEBUG=WARN` (abort and transport errors remain visible), with INFO and the subsystem list set only by jobs that are debugging NCCL (for example the recovery or wedge repro experiments, which already set INFO explicitly).

Done when: the Iris GPU default is `WARN` without a subsystem list, Marin's training launcher no longer needs to guess, and the two call sites that want INFO set it themselves.

`EnvironmentSpec.to_proto()` sets `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` for every GPU extra. Marin's training launcher uses `setdefault("NCCL_DEBUG", "WARN")`, so Iris's submitted environment keeps INFO; the reported 32-GPU SFT jobs produced about 80,000 lines/s against roughly 34,500 lines/s of forwarding capacity.

**Relevant code**
- [`types.py#L764-L771`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/types.py#L764-L771) — GPU submission defaults
- [`training.py#L396-L408`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/marin/src/marin/training/training.py#L396-L408) — training fallback
- [`ci-coreweave-gpu-smoke.yaml#L49-L52`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/lib/iris/config/ci-coreweave-gpu-smoke.yaml#L49-L52) — explicit diagnostic INFO
- [`launch_wedge_supervised.py#L36-L41`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/grug/recovery/launch_wedge_supervised.py#L36-L41) — explicit wedge INFO

# Proposed Fix

A GPU submission passes through `EnvironmentSpec.to_proto()`, which writes INFO before Marin's fallback can choose WARN. Set the Iris GPU default to WARN without `NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS`, remove Marin's redundant fallback, and keep the two explicit INFO call sites.

🤖 PR #10241 sets Iris GPU jobs to `NCCL_DEBUG=WARN` without a subsystem list and removes Marin's redundant fallback; diagnostic jobs retain explicit INFO. The affected tests pass, while the Iris unit check is blocked by the native wheel pin addressed in #10243. Both PRs remained open and review required when the 12-hour monitor timed out.

The GPU smoke config and supervised wedge repro continue to request INFO explicitly; Marin training inherits the Iris default.

topics.title: [fast-track] Marin Belay v1: hill-climb the scaling ladder (Paloma macro loss, 8 min on 8×H100)
topics.body:
This issue tracks iterative improvements to the Marin pretraining scaling ladder (`experiments/grug/fast_track`) using the **Marin Belay** process. It is a twist on autoresearch: an agent runs experiments in batches, and anyone can steer it with research directions. > **To suggest a research direction, comment on [Marin Belay Intake (#9514)](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9514).** Suggestions a maintainer approves (👍 from a `marin-devs` member) are copied into this thread automatically, and the agent acts only on this thread. This thread holds the agent's batch reports and maintainer steering. ![fast_track MoE ladder: Marin 535B baseline, clean KMA and candidate 9](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/9697c11ef215ec0f9d536a1bceb0876f768fcf26/v1/ladder_scaling.png) The Marin 535B compute-optimal baseline follows `L(C) = 1.2 + 59.0·C^(−0.0843)` over four data-matched rungs. Clean KMA, the current baseline (★), is 0.022 lower at d512, 0.049 lower at d768, 0.040 lower at d1024 and 0.033 lower at d1280, which is about 1.14×, 1.43×, 1.40× and 1.35× the baseline's compute efficiency. Its dashed curve is fit to all four points: `L(C) = 1.2 + 64.8·C^(−0.0870)`. The **?** marks the open question this issue is chasing: how much further down each point can go. The red diamonds are the current best recipe, candidate 9 (Status below): **2.977 / 2.725 / 2.515 / 2.397** at d512 / d768 / d1024 / d1280. d512 and d768 are seed means, and the bigram table follows rule A. d768–d1280 are data-matched; d512 sits at its fixed-time step count (2817 vs 2383 steps), so it's plotted slightly to the right. That is 0.157 / 0.098 / 0.078 / 0.074 below clean KMA. Its dash-dot curve is fit to all four points: `L(C) = 1.2 + 55.0·C^(−0.0847)`. Its slope is a little shallower than clean KMA's, so the gap narrows with compute: projected to **1e24 FLOPs, 1.710 vs clean KMA's 1.727, about 1.48× clean KMA's compute efficiency and 2.95× the 535B baseline's**. Because the fixed-time d512 point flattens the fitted slope, that projection is probably conservative. The right panel is clean KMA's training MFU at each rung on one 8×H100 node: 9.5% at d512 and d768, 12.2% at d1024, and 13.0% at d1280. FLOPs are counted from KMA's own layers (KDA, MLA + Inkling, AttnRes), as 3× forward with no recompute. The trainer's logged `throughput/mfu` uses the baseline architecture's FLOP formula, so it is slightly off for KMA. ## Objective **Minimize Paloma macro loss (`eval/paloma/macro_loss`, final step) at the d512 rung after a fixed 8 minutes of 8×H100 train-step time.** - **Fixed time, not fixed tokens.** Faster code trains on more tokens within the 8 minutes, so a pure speedup counts as a win. - The LR schedule depends on the step count, so fix steps before each run: `num_steps = round(480 s × ex/s ÷ batch)`. - Measure ex/s with a short `--no-eval` probe (~30 steps) on the same cluster, and use the steady-state throughput. - Compile, evals and startup are excluded from the 8 minutes. - **Numerics changes are allowed** (e.g. FP8, precision changes, approximate kernels). They count as ordinary wins; no parity check needed. - **Noise.** Differences under ~0.005 are noise. A win must beat the current best by more than 0.005. ### Gates (both relative to the current baseline, same fixed-time rule at each rung) - **Gate 1:** beat the baseline at d512 and d768. - **Gate 2:** also beat it at d1024 and d1280, **and** project to lower Paloma macro loss at 1e24 FLOPs. Fit a power law of final loss against training FLOPs across the four rungs, for both the baseline and the variant, fixing the asymptote to 1.2. ### Fixed - Training data, the 16k BPE tokenizer, and the eval sets. - Sequence length 4096. - One 8×H100 node per rung. - The FLOP accounting used for the gate-2 projection. ### Judgment calls - **Hero-scale speed is out of scope for v1, so use discretion.** - Robust target criteria would also check training speed and inference speed at hero scale. Marin Belay v1 skips those checks. - Judge whether a change's d512 gain would carry over to hero scale, and avoid changes whose gain comes from d512-only effects. Two examples: - Dropping MoE for dense would be a clear win at d512 because dense gets ~5× higher MFU there, but that MFU gain would not carry over at hero scale. - A much larger KV cache would also be a clear win at d512, but it would hurt long-context inference speed. - **Avoid magic numbers.** - Prefer changes with few new tuned constants. A tuned constant is justified when its gain is above the noise threshold and holds as a pattern across scales. For example, a 2× LR on one parameter group qualifies if it clears the noise threshold and the gain shows up consistently at larger rungs. - The higher a change's risk of curve fitting, the more scales it must be validated at before it counts as a win. - **Spend effort in proportion to an idea's likelihood of improvement.** - Promising ideas deserve several attempts. Long shots can be tried once and dropped. - A first run is not a verdict for a large change. If you try a new architecture or component, tune its optimizer assignment, LR, init and other key hyperparameters before concluding it doesn't work. The baseline's settings were tuned for the baseline, not for the new idea. ## Architecture (current best, d512) The diagrams below show **clean KMA**. The current best recipe adds the components listed under **Status → Current best recipe**: MLA key norm and key offset, a gated bigram-memory AttnRes source, ReLU² experts, and optimizer, schedule and logit changes. The diagrams show d512; the other rungs differ in the Shape table only. **1. Layer stack and Block Attention Residuals.** Every sublayer reads its input through its own AttnRes gate, a per-token softmax over the residual history. At d512 each layer closes an AttnRes block, so the history at layer *i* is the embedding plus one sum per earlier layer. [¹](#arch-note) ```mermaid flowchart TB tok["token ids

fused CE, vocab tile 8192, z-loss 1e-4"] head --> loss(["next-token loss"]) ``` **2. One layer.** The two sublayers each have an AttnRes gate. The MoE gate also sees the attention output written just before it, as the running partial. ```mermaid flowchart TB Hin[("history
embedding + b0…b(i−1)")] --> GA subgraph GATE["AttnRes gate (one per sublayer, 13 at d512)"] direction TB GA["logit_n = q · rms_norm(source_n)

KDA (local) or MLA + Inkling (global)"}} MIX --> SCA["ShortConv (MLA layers only)"] --> PA(["partial = attn out"]) PA --> GM["AttnRes gate
history + partial"] Hin --> GM GM --> M1["RMSNorm → GatedNorm"] --> MOE{{"LatentMoE + 2 shared experts"}} MOE --> SCM["ShortConv"] --> PB(["block b_i = attn out + MoE out"]) PB --> Hout[("appended to history")] ``` **3a. Kimi Delta Attention, the local mixer (layers 0, 1, 2, 4 at d512; D = 512, 4 heads × 128).** ```mermaid flowchart TB kx["x"] --> kq["q = SiLU(ShortConv(x W_q))"] & kk["k = SiLU(ShortConv(x W_k))"] & kv["v = SiLU(ShortConv(x W_v))"] kx --> kg["decay g = −5 · σ(exp(A_log) · (x W_a↓ W_a↑ + dt_bias))
rank-128 gate, per channel; A_log per head"] kx --> kb["write strength β = σ(x W_β), per head"] kq & kk --> kn["L2-norm q, k; q × 1/√128"] kn & kv & kg & kb --> rec["delta rule, chunked Pallas kernels (chunk 16)
S_t = (I − β k kᵀ) Diag(e^g) S_{t−1} + β k vᵀ
o_t = S_tᵀ q_t · state resets at document starts"] rec --> kon["per-head RMSNorm (shared 128-wide scale)"] --> kog["× σ(x W_g), per channel"] --> ko["W_o → sublayer out
no RoPE, no window, no output ShortConv"] ``` **3b. MLA + Inkling, the global mixer (layers 3 and 5 at d512).** ```mermaid flowchart TB mx["x"] --> mq["q = x W_q (full rank, 4 × 128)"] mx --> ml["KV latent = RMSNorm(x W_dkv), 512 wide, learnable gain"] --> mk["k = latent W_uk"] & mv["v = latent W_uv"] mx --> rel["Inkling bias[h,i,j] = R[i,h,:] · P[:, i−j]
R = x W_r (16 per head) · P 16 × 1024, shared across heads"] mq & mk & mv & rel --> fa["FA4 causal attention (fwd + SM90 bwd)
logits × 1/√128 (qk_mult 1) · no RoPE · no QK-norm
Inkling bias added before softmax"] fa --> xsa["XSA: subtract each head's component along its own v"] --> mg["× 2σ(x W_gate), per head, zero-init"] --> mo["W_o → ShortConv → sublayer out"] ``` **3c. LatentMoE with quantile-balanced routing (every layer).** ```mermaid flowchart TB ex["x (512)"] --> fused["one fused GEMM:
router · W_latent↓ · shared-expert gate/up"] fused --> rt["router logits (fp32)
top-(8+1) on logit − β_QB; 9th = threshold α"] rt --> qb["QB: β_e = global (1 − 8/384) quantile of logit − α
10k-bin histogram each step; router bias = −β, not trained"] rt --> cw["combine weights = σ(unbiased logits) of the top 8,
renormalized to sum to 2.5"] fused --> lat["latent = RMSNorm(x W_latent↓), 256 wide"] lat & cw --> ep["384 SwiGLU experts, hidden 256
pooled-wave EP all-to-all over 8 GPUs, capacity 1.15"] ep --> up["W_latent↑ 256 → 512"] fused --> sh["2 shared SwiGLU experts, 512 → 256 → 512
down projections fused into one GEMM"] up & sh --> sum["routed + shared → ShortConv → sublayer out"] ``` ¹ AttnRes rolls a new block at layer *i* while `i % max(1, L // 8) == 0` and fewer than 8 blocks exist. At d512 and d768 every layer closes a block. At d1024 (12 layers) and d1280 (14 layers) only layers 0–7 do, so layers 8 and up all accumulate into one running partial instead of their own blocks. **Optimizer routing:** - **MuonH:** every attention and MoE matrix, and every GatedNorm (KDA `W_β` at 2× the MuonH LR). - **AdamH:** lm_head. - **Adam:** embedding, router, attention output gate, norm gains, ShortConv kernels, KDA decay parameters, Inkling weights. - **Adam at 0.1× the Adam LR:** the AttnRes queries. ## Baseline: clean KMA Branch [`fasttrack-moe-kma`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/fasttrack-moe-kma) @ `4eba59cafa`. Build from this branch. The recipe below covers every model and optimizer component. Values are for d512 unless noted; the code is `experiments/grug/fast_track/{model,optimizer,heuristic,launch}.py`. **Shape** | Rung | Width D | Layers | Local (KDA) / global (MLA) layers | Heads × head dim | Batch | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | d512 | 512 | 6 | 4 / 2 | 4 × 128 | 128 | | d768 | 768 | 8 | 6 / 2 | 6 × 128 | 128 | | d1024 | 1024 | 12 | 9 / 3 | 8 × 128 | 256 | | d1280 | 1280 | 14 | 10 / 4 | 10 × 128 | 256 | - Every 4th layer and the last layer are global; all other layers are local. - The run uses a 16k vocab and sequence length 4096 with packed documents. Every ShortConv and the KDA state respect document boundaries (the KDA state resets at each document start). - Weights are initialized with std 0.5/√D. Compute is bf16. **Embedding and output** - Token embedding → RMSNorm → GatedNorm. The result is AttnRes source 0. - Output path: final AttnRes gate → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → untied lm_head (`output_proj`). - The fused lm_head + cross-entropy loop uses a vocab tile of 8192. - GatedNorm (every GatedNorm in the model) is `x · sigmoid(W_up · SiLU(W_down · x))`, with a rank-128 bottleneck. **Block (every layer)** - **Attention sublayer:** input = its AttnRes gate mix → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → mixer (KDA or MLA). - **MoE sublayer:** input = its AttnRes gate mix → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → MoE → ShortConv on the MoE output. - Each ShortConv is a 4-tap causal depthwise conv. **Local layers: Kimi Delta Attention** (Kimi K3's layer) - **Projections:** q/k/v are D → N·128 with full heads (no GQA). Each goes through a ShortConv followed by SiLU. q and k are L2-normalized, and q is scaled by 1/√128. - **Decay:** per-channel log-decay `g = −5·sigmoid(exp(A_log)·(x·W_a_down·W_a_up + dt_bias))`. - The gate projection has rank 128. - `A_log` is one value per head, initialized to 0. - `dt_bias` is one value per channel, initialized so the decay rate spans 0.02–0.5. - **Write strength:** `β = sigmoid(x·W_β)`, one value per head. - **Recurrence:** `S_t = (I − β·k·kᵀ)·Diag(exp(g))·S_{t−1} + β·k·vᵀ`, read out as `o_t = S_tᵀ·q_t`. - It runs as chunked Pallas kernels, with a stable block-doubling inverse inside each chunk. - **Output:** per-head RMSNorm with a learnable 128-wide scale shared across heads → full-rank per-channel gate `sigmoid(x·W_g)` → `W_o`. - No positional encoding, no window, no XSA, and no ShortConv on the branch output. **Global layers: MLA + Inkling relative position** - **q:** full-rank, D → N·128 (no Q latent). - **k and v:** k = `W_uk · RMSNorm(x·W_dkv)` and v = `W_uv · RMSNorm(x·W_dkv)`. - They share one 512-wide KV latent, with a learnable RMSNorm on the latent. - Heads are 128 wide with no RoPE part. - There's no ShortConv on K, so the up-projections can be absorbed at inference. - **Scaling:** no QK-norm; `qk_mult` = 1, i.e. standard 1/√128 logit scaling. - **Position — Inkling relative-position bias**, added to the pre-softmax logits in place of RoPE: - `bias[h,i,j] = R[i,h,:] · P[:, i−j]`, where `R = x·W_r` is 16 values per head. - `P` is a bank of shape [16 × 1024] shared across heads. The relative extent is 1024. - It runs inside the FA4 attention kernel (forward, backward, and the SM90 backward pass). - **XSA** (exclusive self-attention): subtract the component of each head's output that is parallel to its own value vector. - **Output gate:** per head, `2·sigmoid(x·W_gate)`. `W_gate` is zero-initialized, so the gate is 1 at init. - The branch output also gets a ShortConv. **MoE sublayer (LatentMoE with quantile-balanced routing)** - **Experts:** 384 routed experts, top-8. Each is a SwiGLU with hidden size D/2. - **Latent space:** experts operate in a D/2-wide latent. The input goes through `W_latent_down` → RMSNorm, and the combined expert output goes back up through `W_latent_up`. - **Router:** reads the full-width token and computes logits in fp32. - Experts are selected by top-(8+1) on bias-adjusted logits, where the 9th logit is the threshold α. - Combine weights are the sigmoid of the unbiased logits, renormalized to sum to 2.5. - **Quantile balancing:** each step, each expert's threshold β is the global (1 − K/E) quantile of the logit margins (logit − α), read from a 10k-bin histogram. The router bias is set to −β. - The router bias is not trained by gradient. - **Capacity:** capacity factor 1.15, with pooled-wave expert-parallel dispatch. Receiver ranks are sort-based and the expand backward is gather-based. - **Shared experts:** 2 shared SwiGLU experts that bypass the latent: D → D/2 hidden → D. - **Fused projections:** - The router, latent-down, and both shared experts' gate/up projections run as one GEMM. - The shared experts' down-projections run as one GEMM. **Residual stream: Block Attention Residuals** - **Sources:** the embedding source, one running sum per completed block of sublayer outputs, and the running partial sum of the current block. - The model has 8 blocks. Block sums use the raw sublayer outputs. - **Gates:** every sublayer (attention and MoE) has its own gate, and there is one final gate before the output norm. Each gate has one learned pseudo-query `q ∈ ℝᴰ`, zero-initialized so every gate starts as a uniform average. - **Mixing:** per token, `logitᵢ = q · rms_norm(sourceᵢ)`, using a parameter-free (frozen) RMS key norm, then `softmax` over sources and a weighted sum of the raw sources. - **Implementation:** - Each completed block is scored once against every gate that reads it. - Backward: at d512 the layer's forward intermediates are saved. At d768–d1280 each layer is recomputed. At d1280 the attention branch is also rematerialized. - The model keeps one layer stack per mixer kind. **Optimizer** | Group | Update rule | LR | Parameters | |---|---|---|---| | `muonh` | MuonH | MuonH LR | all attention and MoE matrices: MLA `W_q`/`W_dkv`/`W_uk`/`W_uv`/`W_o`; KDA `W_q`/`W_k`/`W_v`/`W_o`/`W_g`; experts; shared experts; latent down/up. Also every GatedNorm `W_down`/`W_up`. | | `kda_beta` | MuonH | 2 × MuonH LR | KDA `W_β` | | `adamh` | AdamH | MuonH LR | lm_head (`output_proj`) | | `adam` | Adam | Adam LR | token embedding; router; attention output gate; router bias slot (overwritten by QB); all 1-D norm gains; ShortConv kernels; KDA `W_a_down`/`W_a_up`, `A_log`, `dt_bias`; Inkling `W_r` and `P` | | `attn_res_query` | Adam | 0.1 × Adam LR | the AttnRes pseudo-queries | - **MuonH:** Nesterov momentum 0.95 → Newton–Schulz orthogonalization (5 quintic steps, bucketed across same-shape matrices) → a step along that direction, then projection back onto the matrix's Frobenius sphere. Each matrix's norm stays fixed at its init value. - **AdamH:** the Adam direction with the same Frobenius-sphere (hyperball) projection. - **Adam:** β1 0.9. comments.body:
Some ideas to get started. Treat this as a general pool of ideas, that indicates the spirit of what can be tried.
1. https://blog.tilderesearch.com/blog/online-kl-shampoo. Consider interactions with hyperball and selectively replace matrices.
2. Add a second embedding table with its own random init. Attn residuals queries both embedding tables, treating them as unique inputs.
3. Lets add value embeddings. That is, a second embedding table that gets added to V on the MLA layers. So take KV latent-> project to num_heads of size 128. Then do values = lambda1*values + lambda2*value_embeds[layer_i]. lambda 1 init to 1, lambda2 init to 0. value_embeds has [vocab_size, num_heads*head_dim, num_mla_layers] dimension. Can also try gated value embeds, where instead of lambda2, its conditional on residual stream via sigmoid(linear(x)).
4. Add learnable scalars to each submodule output, that feeds into attention residuals. May be worth tracking and plotting these in wandb, to see if indicates any architecture changes will help.
5. Try different variations of linear attention to replace KDA.
6. It has been shown in many places that the final couple layers of attention dont prefer to attend to outputs from the final MLPs. See if there is any change to attention residuals to help make this more natural.
7. Adding an lm_head auxillary loss to the output of layer 1 for the first X (say 500) steps can help give the routed experts a cleaner role early. Unclear how this interacts with attention residuals.
8. Hash routing on first layer.
9. Instead of Adam/AdamH on embed and lm_head, look into other optimizers here that have shown promise in literature.
10. Do any weights benefit from extremely different beta1/beta2/momentum terms, or swapping their optimizer group.
11. Update the router behavior (sigmoid vs softmax), normalizing over picked experts vs not, sampling over experts instead of top k).
12. Null routing (enable tokens to select null experts which skips their computation, dynamic compute per token).
13. Multi-token-prediction.
14. Sparse attention.

If users give comments with singular specific ideas, give it priority over this laundry list.

🤖 **Agent check-in.**

**Identity:** Claude Code (model `claude-opus-5-5`, 1M context), running locally on @ClassicLarry's machine in the `marin` repo.

**Prior context:** a fresh session with no conversation history. I carry the persistent auto-memory notes from earlier sessions in this repo (Iris/CoreWeave job submission quirks, W&B 128-char run-name limit, GB200 gang-retry flakes, grug MoE perf notes). I have no prior runs on this issue. I will build from `fasttrack-moe-kma` @ `4eba59cafa` as the issue specifies.

**Prompt I was given (verbatim):**

> Your job is to execute on https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9451. Continue working until told to stop. First post a comment showing this exact prompt. Indicate your identity and prior context. Stay alert for human input via the github issue.

**Next:** read `experiments/grug/fast_track/{README.md,agent.md}` and the code, measure baseline throughput on cw-us-east-02a, then launch batch 1 (5–10 d512 runs drawn from the idea list above). I will post one comment per batch and edit it as runs finish.

🤖 **Batch 1: cheap architecture adds from the idea list, an LR check, and a noise and profile baseline** (d512, 2475 steps) — **done**

**Goal.** Test the lowest-cost ideas from @ClassicLarry's list: `#2` (second embedding table), `#3` (value embeddings, both forms), and `#4` (learnable sublayer output scalars, logged to W&B). Also check whether the `MoeHeuristic` LR, which was fit on the old baseline architecture, is still right for KMA (×1.5 and ×0.67 on both LRs). Add a seed-1 baseline to calibrate noise, and a 60-step profile to find speed levers. Speed counts as a win under the fixed-time objective.

**Assumption (I'll correct it next batch if it's wrong).** None of these changes adds meaningful compute, so all runs use the baseline's 2475 steps instead of a separate probe. After each run I check its steady-state ex/s. If it is more than about 1% below 660, I rerun at `round(480 × ex/s / 128)` steps. Branch [`ladderclimb_v1_batch01`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/eb26f3cbc9) @ `eb26f3cbc9`: every change is gated by a `--model-set` / `--opt-set` flag and defaults to off.

**Implementation details**
- **ve:** each MLA layer gets a [16384 × N·128] table, and `v = λ1·v + λ2·VE[token]` (λ1 = 1, λ2 = 0 at init). The tables, λ and the gate go to Adam at the Adam LR, like `token_embed`.
- **veg:** `v = λ1·v + sigmoid(x·W)·VE[token]`, with one gate per head. `W` is zero-initialized, so the gate starts at 0.5.
- **osc:** a scalar initialized to 1 on each attention and MoE sublayer output before it enters the AttnRes history (Adam). Logged as `train/attn_res/scale_{attn,mlp}_L*`.
- **emb2:** a second randomly initialized table → learnable RMSNorm, prepended as an extra AttnRes block that every gate can read.

**Takeaway.**
- **Noise is the story.** The identical-code seed-1 baseline landed at 3.1195, 0.0056 below seed 0. Against the two-seed baseline mean of 3.1223, none of the architecture changes clears noise: emb2 −0.005, veg −0.004, osc −0.002, ve −0.002. ve, veg and emb2 also ran 7–13% slower, so at a fair 8-minute step count they would lose part of that.
- **The LR heuristic holds for KMA.** Both ×1.5 and ×0.67 are clearly worse.
- **The learned scalars in osc point at the MoE output.** Its final values: MoE outputs grow to 1.2 / 1.4 / 1.5 / 2.1 / 1.7 / 1.9× by layer, the early KDA outputs shrink to 0.48×, and the MLA outputs stay near 1.0. The routed-expert output magnitude is capped by MuonH's sphere and the 2.5 combine renorm, and it wants to grow.
- **Profile (8×H100, d512, ~187 ms/step).** Compute is ~155 ms: elementwise fusions ~61, GEMMs ~43, sort/scatter/gather ~23, KDA ~14, FA4 ~7. Exposed EP all-to-all is ~18 ms, and the host gap between steps is ~6 ms.
  - **One kernel is a bug:** the token-embedding gradient takes **~11 ms/step**. Under the bf16 compute policy, the gather's transpose scatter-adds every token's cotangent directly into a **bf16** table. That means contended bf16 atomics, with frequent tokens' gradients rounded at every add. A single-GPU microbenchmark puts the fp32 scatter at 0.2 ms. The same scatter is why ve, veg and emb2 were slow: each extra table adds one.

**Next (batch 2).**
- Fix the embedding backward with an fp32 scatter-add plus a psum: [`ladderclimb_v1_batch02` @ `269387e86b`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/269387e86b). It is a pure speed and precision change, so it is a baseline candidate in its own right.
- Probe throughput with the fix, then rerun ve, veg and emb2 on it at fair step counts, with replicate seeds.
- Test MoE output-magnitude variants: combine renorm sum 2.5 → 4, sigmoid without renorm, softmax combine, and K3's normalized LatentMoE.
- In response to the literature-scan comment: a background scan turned up these candidates for later batches: K3 normalized LatentMoE, per-head Muon, NorMuon-style row normalization, Engram n-gram memory, null experts, and FP8 lm_head.
**Next batch (tentative):** act on the profile. Validate any win above 0.005 at d768. Try combinations of the winners, MTP, and router variants (`#11`).
Also, feel free to scan the literature for new papers with promising ideas.

🤖 **Batch 2: fp32 embedding-gradient fix, embedding variants at fair step counts, and the MoE output magnitude** (d512) — **done**

**Goal.**
1. Make the **fp32 embedding backward** the new baseline candidate. The embedding gather's backward now scatter-adds in fp32 inside each shard and then psums, instead of scatter-adding bf16 cotangents into a bf16 table. On an 80-step probe that is **+9.9% ex/s** (754 vs 686), and it also makes the embedding gradient more precise. Replicated over 2 seeds, because noise is about 0.005.
2. Rerun **ve, veg and emb2** on the fix, where their extra tables are nearly free (probes: 750 / 744 / 735 ex/s).
3. Follow the batch-1 osc signal that the **MoE output wants to be larger**: combine renorm sum 4.0 instead of 2.5; sigmoid without renorm (`2.5·σ/(K/2)`, so the per-token total can vary); softmax combine (idea `#11`); and Kimi K3's normalized LatentMoE (a learnable RMSNorm before `W_latent_up`, from the literature scan @ClassicLarry asked for). osc is rerun on the new base.

**Step rule.** Short probes read about 3% above full-run steady state, so steps = `round(2475 × probe ex/s ÷ 686.5)`, where 686.5 is the baseline's own probe from batch 1. Cost-neutral variants use the fix's 2719 steps.

**AttnRes logit bias and z-loss** (added for the follow-up comment). Each of the 13 gates gets a zero-init bias per source it reads: one per completed block, plus one for the running partial. It is added to the logit before the softmax and trained with Adam at 0.1× the Adam LR, the same as the queries. The z-loss is the mean over tokens of logsumexp(gate logits)², averaged over gates, and added to the loss. Every run now logs the pseudo-query norms: `train/attn_res/query_norm_{mean,max,gNN}` plus the unweighted `train/attn_res/z`. One caveat: a z-loss can be satisfied by shifting a gate's biases down together, which leaves the mix unchanged. I'll compare the q norms across the three runs.

**Correction:** the AttnRes z-loss runs' eval losses also included the z-loss term (the same bug, found in batch 18). That inflated them by weight × z: about +0.0012 for 1e-3 and +0.001 for 1e-1. Their deltas are about +0.004 and +0.047 instead of +0.0055 and +0.0485, so both are still worse.

**Takeaway (all done).**
- **AttnRes logit bias is neutral (+0.0011).**
- **The AttnRes z-loss hurts:** +0.0055 at 1e-3 and +0.049 at 1e-1.

  | run | AttnRes z (unweighted) | query norm mean | query norm max |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | bias only | 6.31 | 0.227 | 0.377 |
  | bias + z 1e-3 | 1.23 | 0.286 | 0.583 |
  | bias + z 1e-1 | 0.01 | 0.332 | 0.565 |

  The z-loss is minimized by pushing every logit down. With keys that are RMS-normalized but not mean-centred, the query does this by growing along the direction opposite the common component of the sources, instead of shifting all biases together. That distorts the mix.

Try a simple version of looped models (w/ and wo/ growing, a la https://github.com/qlabs-eng/slowrun/pull/92 and https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19107) with untying and see if that improves performance. Make sure to include the input injection as well!

🤖 **Batch 9: looped models (@neel04's request): tied looping, with and without growth, with input injection** (d512, paired seed 0 vs qk_mult-2.5 base **3.0858**)

**Addresses** @neel04's comment. It follows [slowrun#92](https://github.com/qlabs-eng/slowrun/pull/92) (1× for 70% of training, then 2×) and [arXiv 2609.19107](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.19107) (boundary operator `Norm(h) + α·e`, growth partway through training, backprop through all passes, and FLOPs of every pass counted). Branch [`ladderclimb_v1_batch09`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/c2803601b0).

**How it maps onto KMA** (`loop_passes`, `loop_grow_step`):
- **The looped core is the whole 6-layer stack**, weights tied. Each pass extends the Block AttnRes history. Pass 2's gates read the embedding, every pass-1 block, and the pass-2 blocks so far. Pass 2 has its own zero-initialized AttnRes pseudo-queries, so its gates start as uniform averages over that longer history.
- **Input injection.** At the start of each extra pass, the running partial is initialized to `α·e`, where e is the normalized embedding source and α is learned (init 1, Adam), and the pass's layers write onto it. The AttnRes gates already see e as source 0. This is the explicit re-injection from both references. The AttnRes softmax already normalizes what each sublayer reads, which plays the part of `Norm(h)`.
- **Growth** uses a step-gated `lax.cond`. Before the growth step only pass 1 executes, at full base speed. After it both passes run, with gradients through both. The router biases are shared per physical layer; their QB statistics are averaged over the passes.
- **Fixed-time steps.** Two passes run at 0.506× the base throughput (80-step probe: 381.8 vs 754.1 ex/s), so every run is given 8 minutes of train-step time:
  - loop2 throughout: 1426 steps.
  - Grow at 70%: N solves `0.7N/751 + 0.3N/380 = 480/128`, so N = 2179 and growth is at step 1525.
  - Grow at 50%: N = 1892, growth at step 946.
- **Not in this batch: untied growth**, where the core is copied at the growth step and the copies train separately. It changes the parameter tree and optimizer state mid-run, so it needs trainer work. It's next if tied growth looks promising.

- **Looping loses at d512 fixed time**, in every variant:

  | grow 1→2 at 70% | +0.021 |

- **Why it loses.** The paper's gains are compute multipliers at ≥1e20 FLOPs with 7–8 tokens per parameter for its growth variants. Here the whole run is about 1e17 FLOPs and data-limited: in 8 minutes the model sees only about 1.1B tokens. An extra pass costs tokens, which are the scarce resource at this rung. Untied growth has the same FLOP cost after growth, so I'm not building it for d512. It is a better fit for a hero-scale study.
